notes_for_editor.note: Standing is not confirmed: the Register describes the tower as decommissioned and privately owned, but no statement of current condition or recent photo was found, so facts.status is 'unknown'. Owner names appear in the Register description and are left out of the story and evidence quotes. The brief's 'George & Rebecca Taylor' is the Register's administrator field and was kept. The Forest Lookouts page has only a county and agency line. The Jackson's Ramblings post and the 1819 News column add nothing new on this tower. Used 1 WebSearch and about 7 page reads, over the per-tower budget, because the sources are thin.

Thin record. NHLR is the only tower-specific source. The Forest Lookouts Aimwell page has a header only (Marengo County, Alabama Forestry Commission) and no body text. Kaufmann's 1819 News column is general, cited only for the MC-39 and climbing context, not for Aimwell's condition. NHLR gives a 100' Aermotor without naming a model, so the MC-39 point is not applied to Aimwell. Brief record matched: 1951 built and 2010 registration. height_m 30.5 converts 100 ft. Staffing, fires, access and current condition are left out because no source supports them. The only evidence that the tower still stands is NHLR's 'only one remaining' wording; no visit date is given. No photos added.

The 1941 history comes from newspaper passages quoted on the Forest Lookouts page (Daily Mountain Eagle), not from the original paper. The Weebly passage spells it 'Alridge Tower'; the tablet and NHLR use Aldridge. NHLR lists the build year as unknown, so the 1941 event rests on the May 29, 1941 'now completed' line and the June 1941 dedication. Brief gap closed: no built event was in the record. Access upgraded from unknown to private from NHLR's 'located on private property' line; no owner or permission information was found. Not verified: condition after the July 2022 site visit, staffing and fires. Kaufmann's column is general and does not name this tower. No photos added.

Thin record. NHLR is the main source. The Weebly Allison page has a header only (Choctaw County, Alabama Forestry Commission) and no body text. Jackson's Ramblings repeats the Register's description and gives AL 45 where the Register gives AL 44. The UWA archive listing includes an August 9, 1926 letter from Mr. Allison to Major Bunker about a lookout tower; no tower is named, so it is not linked to Rudder Hill. Brief record matched on the 1954 built field and 2010 registration. The 1953 date comes from the Register description and is added as a replacement event. No photos added. Not verified: current condition, access, staffing and fires. The drone video and any other video or social posts were not read and are not cited.

Only the NHLR detail page and the Talladega National Forest Wikipedia article were read. An Anniston Star article ('Grant allows restoration of fire tower', annistonstar.com) appeared in a search snippet describing a Friends of the Talladega National Forest effort to restore a Bankhead tower north of Heflin. Both fetch_text and WebFetch returned HTTP 429, so it is neither read nor cited. Retry it: it is the likeliest source for current condition and access. The maker claim is the register writer's hedged belief and is kept hedged. Brief elevation (419.1 m) and USFS agency match the register; no corrections. The name 'Bankhead' points to a different national forest, so the register's Talladega placement should be double-checked against the Forest Service. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the story's no-condition-change line was narrowed to 'in the sources we could read', because the unread Anniston Star snippet may describe restoration work on a tower north of Heflin (Cleburne County).

Built year, design, elevation, registration and the Salem note all come from the NHLR register entry alone; no second source for the build. The register's 'only surviving' wording implies standing when written, but the date is unknown, so the record's 'standing' status is not independently confirmed. No staffing, fire, access or current-condition source found. Wikipedia's Beauregard article does not mention the tower. The Forestry Commission homepage and the FFLOS Alabama page gave nothing useful. The 1819 column does not name this tower; it is used only for statewide context and the climbing warning. Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 7 page reads.

Thin record. The 1948 build year is in the Register and matches the 1948 dedication notice quoted by Forest Lookouts; the Anniston Star page itself was not checked. No design, height, staffing, fire, condition or access information was found. The record's 'standing' status is unconfirmed by any dated source, so it is not in facts. Web searches returned only an Oklahoma tower also named Beaver Mountain, which was excluded. The Register gives the build year only, so no design or height facts were added.

Build year (1942) and the CCC Camp P-76 attribution agree across the NHLR entry and Jackson's Ramblings. Registry number conflict: NHLR says US 862, AL 40; Jackson's Ramblings says US 862, Al 41. The story reports both and does not pick one; NHLR is the register of record, so check it before any correction. Jackson's spells the town Bellville, while the register and record use Belleville. Facebook and YouTube posts seen in search were not used (one calls the county Connecticut County). The drone videos are the only sign of a recent visit or sighting, and they carry no condition or access statement. No staffing or fire source found. The Forest Lookouts Alabama list in the local cache (eastern_us_lookouts/lee.html navigation) does not include Belleville, Beauregard or Blackjack; treat that as a snapshot, not a verdict. Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 5 page reads.

Thin record: NHLR is the only substantive source. The Forest Lookouts Bibb page has a header only (Bibb County, Alabama Forestry Commission) and no body text. The Alabama Forestry Commission Facebook post on fire towers was not readable beyond its title. The 1819 News column is by Thomas Kaufmann, who also nominated Bibb to the Register; it is general about Alabama towers and is cited only for the MC-39 model context, not for Bibb's condition or climbing status. A Jackson's Ramblings entry for Brooks Lookout Tower (Conecuh County) is a different tower and was not linked to Bibb. height_m 30.5 converts NHLR's 100 ft. Access, staffing and current condition are left out of facts because no source supports them. No photos added. Not verified: whether any closure or restoration has happened since 2009.

One detailed Register entry (nominated by Andrew Zerb; photo credit Andrew Zerbe) and a thin Forest Lookouts page. No staffing, fire, restoration-date or current-status sources were found. A Forest Service Bankhead page read had no tower content. The 30.5 m height is the 100-foot tower height converted, not a cab-floor height. The record's built year of 1936 may be widened to the Register's circa 1936-1938 range.

Lowest confidence of the three: only the NHLR register entry describes this tower. No source found for condition, current status, public access, staffing, fires, or who built it (the register lists the Forestry Commission only as administrator and cooperator). The record's 'standing' status is not confirmed by any source read. Searches returned mapping and topo-map pages (anyplaceamerica, mapcarta, itouchmap) that add nothing on the tower's history, and were not cited. The 1819 column is general statewide context and does not name this tower. Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 4 page reads.

NHLR is the only tower-specific source. The 1941 build year and 2009 registration in the brief match the Register. Height_m 36.6 is converted from the Register's 120-foot wording in its description, not from a separate height field, so check it if strict. The Forest Lookouts Blacksher page returns 404. Two WebSearch queries found no history beyond the Register. Status standing is taken from the Register's 'still standing' wording. No photos added: the NHLR photo us853_blacksher.jpg is already in the photo manifest and its license is not stated on the page.

Unresolved agency conflict: the Register's 'Administered by' field names Charles Daniel Mullins, its description says the tower was built for the Alabama Forestry Commission, and Forest Lookouts names the Forestry Commission. Left out of facts.agency pending a human look; the record's agency field is unchanged. The Register gives only 'late 1940s' for the build, so no built event was added. The condition description is undated. Web searches found no other source on this tower or its owner. The ownership correction is for human review.

Thin record: the NHLR detail page is the only substantive source. Its 2016 description is the latest word on condition, so current status, access and climbing rules are unverified. No build date, designer or staffing history in any source read; the easternuslookouts.weebly.com page guessed at as boar-tush.html returned 404 and was not used. A Facebook video titled 'Boar Tush Lookout Tower in Haleyville, Alabama' appeared in search; it is unread and unused, and Haleyville is the nearest town to the NHLR coordinates. Grokipedia and Wikipedia's Boar Tush community article were checked and do not add tower history. The 1819 News column is by Kaufmann, who may have nominated sites on the Register; it is cited only for general Alabama tower condition and climbing rules. Height 30.5 m converts the NHLR's 100 ft. No photos added. No corrections to the brief's record; access 'unknown' kept.

Thin record: the NHLR detail page is the main source, and the Forest Lookouts page for Bridge Creek is a header only (Lawrence County, Alabama Forestry Commission) with no body text. Status rests on the NHLR listing and a 2021 photo credit; no current condition, access, staffing or fire history was found in two searches. The Kaufmann column is by the NHLR nominator and is used only for model context and general climbing caution, not for this tower's condition. Height 30.5 m converts the NHLR's 100 ft. Facts omit access and visit because no source supports either. No photos added: the NHLR photo has no image URL in the fetched page. No corrections to the brief's record.

NHLR is the only tower-specific history. TopoQuest confirms the name, county and approximate location (its coordinates agree with the Register's to about 0.001 degree) but nothing about the history. The brief's 1962 build year matches the Register's replacement date; the event is recorded as replaced because the Register describes a replacement. Forest Lookouts' cached brooks.html page covers a Pennsylvania site, so it was not used. Two WebSearch queries found no build history. The brief's status standing is not stated by any fetched source, hence the proposed correction. No photos added: the Register's photos are not listed with URLs or licenses in the page text I read.

Four independent sources agree on location, the 1934 completion and the CCC build; the 1934-35 and 1936 dates differ by source and are both given. Current access is supported by the Encyclopedia of Alabama and the 2026 America's State Parks guide, not by an official park page; the official alapark.com Cheaha page has no Bunker Tower text. A Cheaha State Park Facebook post titled 'Bunker Tower Road is back...' appeared in search and says the tower reopened after a television-tower repair, but the page returned only its title, so nothing from it is used; a closure and reopening date should be checked before publication. Staffing is 'occasional' per the marker, whose undated text was photographed in 2021. Height 15.2 m is the marker's approximately 50 feet. No photos added. No corrections to the brief's record; events and agency match.

Build year 1948 agrees across the register, the 1948 newspaper dedication and the blog. Unresolved: the state number is AL 42 in NHLR (and in the record) but AL 43 on Jackson's Ramblings. The register's 100-foot figure is not said to be to the cab floor, so height_m (30.5) is only the register's figure converted and may not match the cab-floor definition. Current condition is not settled: search snippets for a YouTube short and a Facebook reel titled 'Butler Mountain Fire Lookout' describe it as abandoned, but neither page could be read, so that claim is not used. Access, climbing and staffing are unknown; no visit facts are recorded. The record's ownership 'state' is an inference: sources name the Alabama Forestry Commission as administrator, not owner. The 1948 dedication is known only from a newspaper quote on Forest Lookouts; no original newspaper page was read. Verification 2026-10-08: the 428 ft figure is the register's elevation, not a hill height; OpenStreetMap's tag is tower:construction=lattice, not a tower type.

Thin record. The NHLR disagrees with itself: build field 1936, description 1935. No source read gives staffing, closure, fate or current public access, so the story says so. The NHLR links an article, Exploring the Forgotten Fire Towers of Alabama (rootsrated.com), which returned no text from fetch_text; it was not read. A search snippet gives elevation 178 ft (584 m) from aboutus.com, against the NHLR's 563 ft (172 m), which matches the record's 171.6 m; not verified. Access status should be checked with the Talladega National Forest before any visit advice is published.

Thin record: no build year, designer, builder, staffing or access information found. The Alabama state forestry history PDF has no Cains Ridge mention, so it is not cited. Register elevation 617 ft (188 m) matches the record; a search snippet from another site gave 178 ft, which is not used. The 1819 News piece is general Alabama context, not about this tower. The story's climbing advice is precautionary. The register page was searched for access, visit, build and climb wording and none was found, so the no-public-access line rests on that absence rather than a quote; the earlier evidence row that quoted the height line for it was removed.

No staffing, notable fire or access sources found. The make of the tower and the removal date conflict across sources and the story reports both. The 2013 sale to New York rests on Forest Lookouts alone. Two WebSearch-era leads were checked; none added a source beyond the three above. Brief's status 'standing' is wrong: both NHLR and FFLOS say removed.

Only two sources, and neither describes the tower's condition after the 2011 registration, so the record's 'standing' status and 'unknown' access are unconfirmed. No staffing, fire or fate information was found; one web search added nothing new. NHLR elevation 402 ft (123 m) matches the record.

Single source: the NHLR page. It gives no build year, design, height or builder. Two WebSearch queries found nothing about this tower; the results were other Cedar Grove places and fire departments. The Forest Lookouts page at easternuslookouts.weebly.com/cedar-grove.html is a Livingston County, Kentucky tower and was not used. The brief's status standing is not stated by any fetched source; the 2021 photo caption is the only dated evidence, so status is left out of facts. Brief elevation_m 48.5 agrees with the Register's 159 ft (48 m) to rounding. The NHLR photo cedar-grove.jpg is already in the photo manifest and its license is not stated on the page, so no photo is added.

Brief elevation 303.6 m matches NHLR 996 ft (304 m); an OpenStreetMap node shows 299 m and was not used. Standing status rests on the NHLR site visit of 26 November 2022; no later check found. Climbing access is not stated in any source read; the birding guide gives only the kiosk. The anyplaceamerica.com listing returned HTTP 403 and was not used.

Direct conflict on build date: NHLR says 1935 (CCC, 1930s); the Anniston Star items reprinted by Forest Lookouts describe construction in 1947-49. The Star originals were not checked; we relied on the reprints. Current condition of the tower is not confirmed by any source read; the JSU notice concerns the overlook. Owner is unverified (one social-media post could not be read), so none is stated. No staffing or fire history found for this lookout.

Record status 'standing' is wrong per both registers; the 11-27-21 update gives no removal date or cause. Record kind 'tower' may need review now that FFLOS lists it as a former site. Elevation differs by one foot between the registers (965 ft NHLR, 964 ft FFLOS); the record was not changed. No staffing, fire or newspaper history was found in one search.

Two sources only. Build year conflicts: NHLR 1960 vs Anniston Star item (quoted by Forest Lookouts) 1961. The Anniston Star item spells the towerman's name two ways ('Edlers' and 'Elders'); the story uses 'Edlers'. The Forest Lookouts page is a transcription of a newspaper item, not the paper itself. No source read gives the current condition, closure, or access; a search snippet (YouTube) links the tower to Little River Canyon Preserve near Canyon Mouth Park, unverified and not used. Checked NPS pages for Canyon Mouth Park and directions: no mention of the tower. The Alabama state forestry history PDF (forestry.alabama.gov) was searched for Daniel's Gap and had no match in the grep. Check current status with the Alabama Forestry Commission before publishing visit advice.

Only the two register pages describe this tower, and they repeat one description, so the history is thin. Both give 1952 for the reconstruction and removal around 2010. The original construction date and earlier site are unknown. The 100 ft figure is the register's tower height, not confirmed as height to the cab floor, so height_m is omitted. The NHLR page gives the state number as AL 36, but the FFLOS cross-reference says AL 37; the record keeps AL 36, the NHLR page's own number. Access is set to closed because no tower remains; the park itself is public. The state forestry PDF is a manuscript submitted in March 1961, reproduced by the Department of Conservation; its author is not named in the text read, and its 157-tower count is general, not specific to this site. No new photos. Two web searches added nothing specific to this tower.

Single substantive source: the NHLR detail page has no visit report, condition note or staffing answer. The brief's status standing is not confirmed by any source read, so status is left out of facts. County check: the NHLR Location field reads Evergreen, Autauga County, Alabama, confirmed on the page 2026-10-09. A web search described Evergreen as the seat of Conecuh County, but that came from a search snippet, not a page read, so it is not cited. Two web searches found no Autauga County fire tower record. The Forest Lookouts (easternuslookouts.weebly.com) Evergreen page returns 404 and its Alabama list omits Evergreen. Thomas Kaufmann's 1819 News column is general about Alabama towers and is not used for this tower's condition. The story does not call the NHLR tower steel: that word comes only from the column's general remark about the MC-39 model. No photos added. Not verified: build details beyond 1949, fire history, staffing, current condition, access, fate.

One source for the build year, design, agency and registration: the NHLR entry, read in full (it names Alabama Forestry Commission as administrator). The 1819 News article is general background and does not name Fabius. Not found: staffing, fire history, condition today, access, and any dated source for the record's 'standing' status (the Register does not state it). A search surfaced the Joe B. Shirley tower near Huntsville in Madison County, a different tower, excluded. The 120 ft height (36.6 m) is the Register's figure and may not be cab-floor height. 'Internatioinal' is a typo in the Register, not in our text.

One register source (read in full) for the 1941 build, the CCC camp and the 2021 registration. The camp name 'Vrendeburgh' matched no source found. Searches surfaced Vredenburgh, a Monroe County mill town (EOA), and the part of that entry read names no CCC camp; the spelling may be a typo for Vredenburgh, or the camp may be unrelated. Unconfirmed, and the story does not state the link as fact. The register gives no managing agency. Standing status, staffing, access and condition are unsourced. The 100-foot height (30.5 m) is the Register's tower height and may not be cab-floor height. A search for a 1941 Alabama tower returned Rock Mountain (Jefferson County), a different tower, excluded.

The 2022 reopening year comes from the Coosa County News web address (2022/06/24); the article body says June 15 without a year. height_m 15.2 is converted from the register's 50-foot figure. Staffing is recorded as unstaffed as of 2017; the register notes a full-time caretaker on site then, and a later caretaker is mentioned in the 2022 article without a date. The register lists elevation 1,104 ft; a Wikidata entry gives 1,142 ft and spells the name 'Flag Mountain'; not used. An al.com 2011 article was blocked (HTTP 403) and was not read. The Alabama Living magazine article on issuu was not readable. The NHLR is the only source for the 1989 staffing end date.

Thin record. Build year 1951 rests on one 1977 newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts; the Register gives none. Current condition rests on the Register's present-tense description (missing lower stairs); no 2025-26 source found and access is undocumented. Do not conflate with Fire Tower Camp on Smith Lake, Crane Hill: a different, 109-foot restored tower seen only in search snippets. Thomas Kaufmann's 1819 News column and the Alabama forestry history PDF were read and do not mention Grandview. Coordinates in the record (34.1336, -86.9246) match the Register's 34 08 01 N, 86 55 29 W.

Register (read in full) and one WAFF news report from August 2024. The Redstone Arsenal origin rests only on the Register; a search for the move found nothing, and its results were a different Green Mountain Lookout in Washington State, excluded. No build date, date of the move, staffing, condition after 2021 or climbing rule is sourced. The record's 'standing' status is not stated on the NHLR page (the Register gives no status); it rests on the 2021 visit and the 2023 registration, not on a condition statement, and the story says so. Elevation 412 m matches the record. The four photos on the Register page were not inspected; the record's photos are all rights reserved.

The April 21, 2019 Register visit report is the newest condition record found; the standing status rests on that visit, and no later check exists. The Forest Lookouts Grove Hill page holds only a header (name, county, agency). Elevation conflict: Register 495 ft (151 m) vs TopoQuest 485 ft MSL. Build year, builder and model are absent from every source read; two web searches turned up no Alabama Forestry Commission record for Grove Hill. The access level restricted is inferred from the office location, not from a stated rule. The Register page credits a 2019 photo to Andrew Zerbe, but no image URL was extracted, so no photos entry. Do not encourage visits to the office grounds. The story no longer says the TopoQuest source is a map database; it cites only the elevation.

Build year conflict: Register 1936 vs Forest Lookouts 1938. The Forest Lookouts page is short, with one dated line. The 2014 Forest Service record concerns a telecom tower at the Horn Mountain communications site and does not mention the fire tower, so it says nothing about whether the fire tower stands. Status is now unknown: the story no longer says the tower stands, since only the undated Pinhoti Trail listing (present tense) hints at it. A web search returned a Cheaha Mountain CCC stone tower (Bunker Tower), which is a different structure and was not used; a second search found no source for the 1938 CCC claim. Access level public reflects national forest land and a public trail; the story advises against climbing. The Skyway Motor Way wording and the Talladega County location were checked on the Register page on 2026-10-09 and are now quoted in evidence. No photos added. Not verified: staffing, fire history, cab condition, current access rules.

Thin record. The NHLR detail page is the only substantive source and it gives no build year and no status, access or staffing details. The Forest Lookouts page repeats the 1976 Decatur Daily quote and adds only the county and national forest. The Commons category gives four photos dated 2024-11-17; the photo titles suggest missing stair steps and a jeep trail, and no source says whether the tower is open to visitors. The brief's record checks out against NHLR (coordinates, elevation 1,402 ft = 427 m, USFS, 2022 registration), so no corrections. The 1976 victim is not named in the story. No photos added to the photos array: Commons files were not checked for license. Not verified: current condition and whether the tower is closed. A search snippet lists an Abel Horseblock Lookout Tower on Natural Atlas and anyplaceamerica.com; it may be the same tower under another name, but was not fetched and is not cited. The USFS Talladega recreation map PDF had no extractable text.

The Virginia origin and the 1930s date rest on the NHLR page alone. Searches found no second source. The Virginia lookout list at https://firelookout.org/lookouts/us/va/va-st/ has no Vicksville or Sedley entry in its relocated section. The search summary called the Virginia origin a mix-up; that is the register's claim, not a verified fact, and the magazine's newly constructed framing is a real conflict, not a settled one. The Lake Martin magazine article 'A Towering Legacy' returned HTTP 429 twice and was not read. The climbing article is undated in our copy; its caption says the tower was to open 'this summer', so it was likely written before the November 2025 opening. Height 33.5 m is converted from the 110 ft overall height; the cab floor height is not given. Climbing is not stated; the story says only that it is open to the public. No source found explains the Lanier name. Source 3 is about the Smith Mountain tower; the story uses it for Lanier's CRATA role and his idea to restore that tower. The source 2 title matches the page title, 'Climbing New Heights'.

The brief's record is out of date: it lists the tower as standing at Monte Sano State Park with coordinates there. Alabama Living (Sept 2025) reports it was taken down and rebuilt at Fire Tower Camp near Crane Hill in Cullman County. The camp's hiking page (undated) says climb the restored 109 ft tower, and the camp home page confirms rentals; the exact opening date and current climbing status are not confirmed. The 109 ft vs 100 ft height gap is unresolved. A Facebook snippet (not fetched, so not cited) gives a 2022 end date at Monte Sano and says the tower was sold; this is unverified and left out of the story. The Instagram posts from Feb 2026 said the tower was not yet finished; those were search snippets only and are not cited. The NASA telemetry claim is in both the Register and the marker; the 1950s date predates the 1968 tower. Coordinates not updated (no source gives the new site). No photos added; none were checked for license.

Thin record. The NHLR detail page is the main source. Its description says the tower was built in 1935 by the CCC, but its Built field says 1938; the story reports the conflict. Registry number AL 41 (NHLR) vs AL 42 (Jackson's Ramblings) is also unresolved. The Forest Lookouts page has only a header (Washington County, Alabama Forestry Commission). The 1819 News column (Thomas Kaufmann, 12.28.25) is general context about Alabama towers and is not about Jordan; it is cited only for the CCC/New Deal timeline and the general safety remark, which the story flags as not Jordan-specific. Current condition, access and staffing are unknown; status 'standing' rests on the NHLR listing and the existence of a drone video, not on a dated inspection. The brief's coordinates and elevation (81 m, 265 ft) match NHLR; the brief's '1938 built' is the NHLR Built field, so no correction is proposed. No photos added; the NHLR page's drone video is on Jackson's Ramblings and is not a photo. Not verified: whether the public may climb it.

Only one source has substance: the NHLR page. The 1949 date is from its Built field and names no builder. Two web searches and the cached FFLOS and Wikidata pages gave nothing about this tower. The record's status 'standing' is not stated by the register; no current status or visit report was found. The record's material 'steel' is not stated for this tower. The story uses the 1819 News remark about MC-39 as a steel model in Alabama, so the material claim stays inferred. No staffing, fire, access or condition information was found. Height 30.5 m is converted from the 100 ft overall height; cab floor height is not given. Suggested check: Alabama Forestry Commission records or Perry County historical sources.

Nearly every fact comes from the NHLR page, including the 2019 condition and staffing answers and the early-2020 sale. The sale is not corroborated; Alabama Forestry Commission or ADECA surplus auction records would settle it. The 'Staffed?' quote is the question label; the answer 'No' sits on the next line of the register. TopoQuest lists a 'Kennedy Lookout Tower' in Barbour County at N31.941825 W85.451608, 688 ft MSL (https://www.topoquest.com/place-detail.php?id=163350). Its point is about 30 m from the register's coordinates; its 688 ft differs from the register's 680 ft (207 m). Not used in the story. Height 30.5 m is converted from the 100 ft overall height; cab floor height is not given. The register's 2019 visit comments include directions to climb a right of way to the tower; deliberately not repeated, since the tower is privately owned. Two web searches found nothing else about this tower.

Only one register page gives facts about this tower. Two WebSearch queries found no other record; the Talladega-area names that came up (Kahatchee, Cheaha Bunker) are different towers and are not used. The Forest Lookouts Alabama index in the crawl cache does not list Kentuck. The register's 100ft figure is taken as tower height (height_m 30.5). No build date, staffing history or current access is documented, so the story says so. No photos added; the register images are already in the record. Worth a check with the Forest Service (Talladega District) on access and current condition before publishing.

The 2006 surplus, the purchase, the move and the restoration rest on the NHLR entry alone. A private commercial page about the tower appeared in search (longleafcamp.com) but could not be reached from this environment (DNS failure), and search snippets from it and other results mention a 1985 closure and a 110 ft height. Those claims are unverified and not used; the height in facts is the register's 100 ft. The NHLR 'Administered by' field names the owner, not an agency, so facts.agency records the owner. The Spring Hill link is inferred, not stated. Visiting status and current condition are undocumented. Photos: FFLOS credits Andrew Zerbe and NHLR credits a photo to a named contributor, but no image URLs were captured, so no photo entries were added.

Staffing, the 1983 locked visit and the Findley family come from one personal blog written by a former visitor whose grandfather worked as a tower man here; treat them as recollection. The 1819 News column is by Thomas Kaufmann, who also nominated this tower to the register; it is used only for statewide context. No source found gives current condition or public access, so facts omit access and status: the register has no condition field, and the earlier 'standing' status was not supported by the register text. The 1939 vs 1941 build year is unresolved. Search snippets described a 12-by-12 foot wooden cab for this tower; that is not in the fetched blog text and is not used. OSM node 358979936 shows a tower at about 132 m elevation but gives no history; not cited. No photos added.

No staffing, fire or access sources found. A WebSearch returned a 2013 Greenville Advocate item about a Crenshaw County fire tower being taken down and shipped to New York; the page returned HTTP 403 and the snippet does not name Luverne, so it is not used. It may describe this tower; the Alabama Forestry Commission or the Greenville Advocate archive could confirm. Brief's status 'standing' is wrong: NHLR and FFLOS both say removed. Brief's elevation 136.9 m matches NHLR 449 ft (137 m).

Only two sources. The register contradicts itself on the build year (Built field 1939, description 1938). Two web searches and the 2018 FFLA Alabama report found nothing else on this tower. The Rumble page is premium-only video; only its text description was read, not the video. The record's status 'standing' is not stated by the register page read, and the video calls the tower abandoned; the story now says only that the tower is near Pineview, and a recent photo should be checked before any status is published. Access is unknown and no visit facts are given. Wikidata item Q86926151 exists but has no date, so it is not cited. Worth asking the Alabama Forestry Commission for its tower records.

The only tower-specific source is the register page, which has no build date, design, height, agency or access line. Two WebSearch queries (one with the Eleanor McCain name) found no news or agency record. The Cheaha Bunker Tower near Delta is a different stone structure and is not used. The brief says standing; the register does not state current condition, so status_note records that. The reconstruction caption is undated, so no rebuilt event is recorded. Ownership is the register's administrator line only; the story does not call the site private. Worth asking the register contact for a build date and the reconstruction date before publishing.

The 1936 build date, CCC origin, McKenzie name and 1966 move come from the register page alone; two WebSearch queries found no second source, and the cached Forest Lookouts Alabama index does not list McGowin. The 1819 column supports only the general CCC timeline, not this tower. height_m 36.6 is the register's 120 ft, not a design record. The name Thomas Kaufmann matches the column's author; the story names him only as the register nominator and does not assert they are the same person without checking. Worth verifying the 1936 date and the 1966 move with Alabama Forestry Commission or Butler County records before publishing. No photos added.

Thin record. The NHLR registration (nominated by Andrew Zerbe) is the only substantive source, and its condition details date from the 2016 nomination. The Forest Lookouts Moreland page carries only a National Geodetic Survey station record with no descriptive text. Two searches for Forest Service project records, a Wikipedia article on the forest and a towers directory produced no history and were not fetched or used. Build year 1933 follows the NHLR. The 1819 News column is used only for statewide context. Current condition and public access are unknown. The earlier access level 'restricted' was not supported by any source and has been removed; the 2016 missing stairs are recorded in the visit note only. The NHLR photo credit (Billy Wayne White) has no image URL captured, so no photo entry was added.

Thin record: no build date, height, staffing or fire history in any source read. The Register page has no visit reports. The access level is inferred from 1971 survey directions (locked gate) and should be checked before publishing. The blog's Registry # 141 conflicts with the Register's AL 86.

Only one tower-specific source (the NHLR entry). The Forest Lookouts page is a header only. The Encyclopedia of Alabama gives a statewide CCC total, not tower detail. No staffing, access or post-2009 condition information was found. The 1936/1938 build conflict is inside the same NHLR entry.

Thin record: the Register and one 1942 newspaper excerpt quoted by Forest Lookouts. No staffing, access or present-condition source found; the story says so. The Register calls the tower the last CCC-completed fire tower in Alabama; the 1942 excerpt does not mention the CCC. The record's height_m 30.5 matches the Register's 100-foot figure, so it was not changed. The name Mountain Mills also belongs to a historic cotton-mill community (Wikipedia, Colbert County history); no source tied the tower to the mill, so none is claimed. Forest Lookouts' Alabama list also has a separate Barton Knob (Mt Mills) entry, which was not checked and should not be conflated.

Origin and build rest on two sources: the NHLR entry and a 1948 Anniston Star report quoted on the Forest Lookouts page (the newspaper itself was not read). Nothing after the January 2009 registration describes the tower, so present condition, staffing, access and any rental are unknown and left out of facts. The brief's coordinates, elevation and registration date match the NHLR page. The Forest Lookouts page is mostly a state index; only its Oak Grove entry was used. No photos added. Not verified: whether the tower still stands.

Register entry has the most detail and three dated visit reports (2007, 2009, 2015); the latest visit is from 2015, so current condition is not confirmed. The plaque date comes via Wikipedia; no photo of the plaque was read. Tower interior access is not described in any source. The Register's visit-report 'Staffed? No' is the basis for the staffing as_of date.

Both register pages carry the same description, so the history rests on one register text plus its dates. Build year conflicts: 1933 in the description vs 1939 in the Built field. Removal is only 'late 2010s', so no removed event was recorded. Elevation differs between the pages (263 ft / 80 m on NHLR vs 293 ft / 89 m on FFLOS); the brief's 80.2 m matches NHLR and was left alone. Corrections: status standing -> removed; the brief's 2010 removal year misread the field. No photos added. Not verified: any post-removal state of the site, and the reason for removal. A 1819 News column by Thomas Kaufmann and the Encyclopedia of Alabama CCC article were read for context but not cited.

No source found on staffing history, decommission date, restoration, or current public access/climbability for Parker Springs specifically. The built year (1937) comes from a single hobbyist survey site (Jackson's Ramblings), not an NRHP nomination or Forest Service document; treat it as plausible but not strongly corroborated. height_m (30.5) is a conversion of the 100-ft tower height stated by NHLR, not independently confirmed.

Build date, builder and staffing are unknown; no source gives them. Beyond the 2026 register entry, the history is one 1980 map listing and OpenStreetMap tags. The register's great-condition report is dated August 2025, and the same entry says volunteers did not know whether it still stands, so status is the main uncertainty. Access and drive-up facts come from the register only; check before any visit. Do not confuse this with the Payne Lake Dam control tower in Forest Service project 60498 (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/alabama/projects/60498), which is a different structure. Elevation differs: NHLR 477 ft (145 m) vs OpenStreetMap ele 153 m; the brief's 145.4 m matches NHLR. The register credits a photo to Brendon Minchew, but its image URL was not captured, so no photos were added.

Only the NHLR detail page and a general 1819 News profile on Alabama lookouts were read. Searches and the Forest Lookouts site (easternuslookouts.weebly.com/peach.html is a 404) gave nothing specific to this tower, so the history is thin. Status, staffing and access are unconfirmed; the record's 'standing' status has no source behind it. A search surfaced a peach-shaped water tower in Clanton, which is a water tower and not this lookout; it was not used. Suggest an Alabama Forestry Commission records request for fate and current status.

Origin unverified: the Rumley Lookout / Sumter County / CCC origin appears only on the NHLR page; no other source read names it. Build year conflict: NHLR field says 1936, NHLR description says late 1930s. Price conflict: Metropolis says the Forestry Commission would give the tower for a dollar; Ruth Arts says a team bought it for $10. Judson College is named only by NHLR; Metropolis and Ruth Arts credit only the Rural Studio. Start date: Metropolis says the park was ready for a student team in 2004; NHLR dates the move and restoration to 2005. Record kind 'unknown' could be 'tower' per the register; not changed, since it is incomplete rather than wrong. Search summaries about Rumley and Judson were not used. Worth asking Perry County or the Alabama Forestry Commission for the tower's original site.

Register and Forest Lookouts agree on 1937 and the 100-foot Aermotor design. No staffing, fire history or condition report found. Rootsrated article linked from the NHLR page returned no text when fetched, so it is unread. Two WebSearch calls: one returned only trail aggregators and an FS motorcycle project; no usable condition source.

Thin record. The 2016 NHLR page is the only source with tower-specific content. The Forest Lookouts page has a header only (Pine Mountain, Tuscaloosa County, Alabama Forestry Commission). Two searches found nothing usable on build year, staffing or fires for this tower. The Kaufmann column is statewide context and does not name Pine Mountain. The brief record matches the sources on county, agency, registry number, 2016 registration and elevation (979 ft, 298 m). Access and visit are left out because no source states them. Status standing rests only on the 2016 description. Not verified: current condition, whether the tower is still used for communications, and public access. No photos added; the NHLR page credits an Andrew Zerbe photo but gives no image URL.

Only the NHLR detail page and a general 1819 News profile were read. The CCC-to-forestry handoff is taken from the NHLR description plus the profile's general account, not from a source about this tower. A search surfaced a different 'Pinnacle Lookout Tower' (a 1937 CCC tower over the Cumberland River, restored 2008) that is not this Shelby County tower and was not used. Forest Lookouts had no matching page under the guessed slugs. Status, staffing and access are unconfirmed.

Thin record. Dates come from one Register page and conflict internally: the Built field says 1947 while the description puts the tornado and the first tower in 1947 and the current MC-39 in 1966. A check of the NWS 1947 Alabama tornado list found no Pickens County line, so the tornado is unconfirmed. No staffing, fire history or access sources found; the record's access 'unknown' stays unknown. The Forest Lookouts page is a header only (name and county), so it supports the Pleasant Grove name and nothing more.

Three sources agree on 1936 in some form, and the NHLR description gives 1937. The Opelika-Auburn article copy shows only its lede and a sidebar; the article body is encoded in the page and could not be read, and no publication date appears in the readable text, so the restoration has no event entry (no year). Staffing, fires, access and visit are not in any source and are omitted. The brief record matches the sources on county, coordinates, elevation (489 ft, 149 m), 1936 build, 2009 registration and agency. No photos added: the NHLR March 2024 photo has no image URL in the cached page. A search returned a Cecil County, Maryland post about a different Pleasant Hill tower; it was not used. Not verified: whether the restoration is complete and whether the tower can be climbed.

Built year (1937), agency, registration and elevation match the record. Staffing, access and any post-2012 status not found; the newest source is the 2012 decision, so 'standing' is supported only through 2012. Record elevation 173.4 m matches the Register's 173 m. The NHLR attributes the land to the Resettlement Administration, while the Forest Service history describes the Oakmulgee purchase unit as created in 1935 by a national forest commission. These do not contradict each other, but the land history is not fully reconciled. The Forest Service history gives the Pondville name as a former working circle, not the tower's own history, so it is used only for the 1936 forest creation date.

Only the NHLR detail page and a general 1819 News profile were read. A search surfaced an unnamed lookout tower on TopoQuest near the NHLR coordinates (about 1,318 ft), with no builder, name or agency link, so it was not used. A search for the Tin Shop name turned up only a volunteer fire department of that name in Roanoke, with no link to this tower. The 1949/1950 conflict is inside the Register and is unresolved. Status, staffing and access are unconfirmed.

Thin record. The NHLR page is the only tower-specific source. Two searches found no staffing, fire or access information for this tower. The Kaufmann column is statewide context and does not mention Redland; Kaufmann also nominated the tower to the Register. Build year: Built field 1949 versus description 1948, both reported. The brief elevation (547 ft, 167 m) matches the NHLR page. The OpenStreetMap node (358950411) lists a different elevation and was not used. A Wikipedia article on the Redland community has no tower mention. An anyplaceamerica.com tower page returned 403 and was not read. Not verified: current condition, public access, and when radio use began. No photos added.

Thin. The only tower-specific source is one register page, which says the tower is believed to be a 100-foot Aermotor and was abandoned and in poor condition as of 2020. Nothing found on build date, builder, staffing, fires, access or condition after 2020. Record status 'standing' is not contradicted by the register but is unconfirmed after 2020; editor may want to review it. The 1819 News figures are one columnist's estimate. Two web searches and the local cache gave no tower-specific source.

Construction year unknown: neither the Register nor the 2018 news report gives it. A Blount County museum Facebook post seen only as a search snippet says built 1949 and staffed to about 1972, then sporadically to 1985; it could not be read, so it is not used. Height: the record's height_m 33.0 does not match the Register's '100-foot steel tower' (30.5 m), though the 2018 report says the cab sits over 100 feet up, so the record may count a different height. Not corrected. Staffing 'unstaffed' rests on the 2018 report saying the tower sat empty; current staffing is not confirmed. A separate Facebook snippet about a 1931 tower on Green Knob Mountain is a different tower and was not used. Access is from a 2026 event listing and a 2018 guide, so check the park before a visit.

The register gives 1958 in its Built field but says in its description that the tower was constructed in 1957; the record keeps 1958 and the story reports both dates. No correction proposed. The description spells the hill Saunders; the heading and record say Sanders. height_m 30.5 is the register's 100-foot figure, not confirmed as cab floor. The register does not state status or condition; the record's 'standing' is unconfirmed. No staffing, fire or access sources found. Two web searches found nothing naming this tower.

Register supplies height, elevation, administrator and registration date only. No build date, staffing, fire history, condition or access source found. Two WebSearch calls returned nothing on this tower. The Forest Lookouts Sand Hill entry is a header with only county and agency.

The NHLR entry is the only substantive source; the Forest Lookouts page carries only a heading. Searches found no other account of this tower's history, staffing or access, so the access and visit keys are omitted. The brief's year (1949), registration date (January 10, 2010), coordinates and elevation check out. The 1819 News article is general Alabama context, not about this tower; the story sentence says so and names the MC-39 itself.

Removal is stated by both registers, but they are sister sites run by the same network, so they are not fully independent. No build year exists in any source read, so no built event is recorded. The 2016 'removed' event and the status correction are the main changes to the brief. Two searches found no other account of the tower or its removal. No photo is recorded: the FFLOS page credits a 2016 photo to Andrew Zerbe, but no image URL was in the cached page text.

Only the NHLR detail page is substantive; it gives registration, coordinates, elevation and height, but no build date, administrator or history. The YouTube page was used only for its title. The brief's rumble.com source was not cited because it added nothing beyond the county. Brief's elevation (146.3 m) and registration date match the register; no corrections. 'Standing' rests on the register's present tense, not a confirmed condition. anyplaceamerica.com returned HTTP 403. A second source for the tower's history would be needed to say more. Fact-check 2026-10-09: every footnoted claim and quote matched the register page; no story edits were needed.

No staffing, fire history, access or current-condition information in any source read. A Baldwin County history Facebook post on 1941 fire towers returned no readable text, so it is not cited. The blog's AL 30 disagrees with the Register's AL 29. Brief elevation 61.6 m matches the Register's 202 ft (62 m) and the OSM ele tag of 62, so no change is proposed. No new photos.

Build date and builder conflict (WPA 1938 vs Alabama Power and CCC, opening April 10, 1939). The Weebly page's Dadeville Record item is dated April 13, 1939 and reports the dedication, so the two April dates are consistent rather than contradictory. Height conflict (82 ft vs about 90 ft) and closure year conflict (1980 vs 1981) are both in the story. Current access rests on CRATA's own pages and a June 2012 reopening note; the sources read do not say whether the cab is open to climbers, so visit.climbable is omitted. Could not read: Roots Rated (0 text returned), Montgomery Advertiser (403), Lake Magazine (429); the LMRA and CRATA restoration-video pages were not read. No photos added; no staffing or last-watch date found.

Two sources only. The sources conflict on the 1940 build and on what ended the first wooden tower: NHLR says it burned before the steel tower went up, while the 1966 Tuscaloosa News item, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, says a tornado destroyed a wooden 1940 tower. The brief's 'standing' status is not confirmed by any source read; this record uses 'unverified'. The 1966 report mentions a planned steel replacement, which could be the NHLR steel tower, but that is unconfirmed. A separate unnamed tower on Yellow Creek Road north of Tuscaloosa turned up in search results; nothing links it to this record, so it is not used. Access is unknown and is omitted.

The register has no build year. The 1941 build date, the CCC attribution and the 1944 dedication come from two undated Bill Coleman Facebook posts that quote a December 1944 Alabama Conservation article; the article itself was not read. The two posts quote the article differently on who built the tower (see resolved_conflicts). The dedication year is inferred from the issue date and is not stated in the quoted passage. A Birmingham wiki timeline that search surfaced gives November 9, 1943 and a 1941 CCC build; bhamwiki.com returns 403 to our reader, so it is unverified and not cited. Access, the sanctuary's current ownership and current condition are unknown; the 2016 register entry is the only later dated source. No photos added. Not verified: whether anything has changed since 2016.

Register gives coordinates, elevation, administrator, registration date and the gate note; it gives no height, build date or staffing. Forest Lookouts entry is a header with county and agency only. One WebSearch returned nothing on this tower; the other hits were a Grove Hill tower in a different town and an unrelated 321-ft communications tower on Old Hwy 5 S, neither used.

Build date, staffing, fire history, height and access are absent from every source read. The Register's Location field reads Alabama Forestry Commission, and the Forest Lookouts index names the same agency. The Register's elevation conflicts with the OSM tag; the corrections entry asks for a survey check. A Register site-visit date (5/3/2015) is not used because its format is ambiguous. Search results for Marion County history pages were not read. Photos: none new.

One register page carries the design, build year and registration details. Correction proposed: kind 'unknown' to 'tower', for editor review. height_m 18.3 is the register's 60-foot figure where the legs stop; confirm whether that is the cab floor. The register does not state status, condition or access. No staffing or fire records found. A Michigan page titled 'Underwood Hill' in the eastern lookouts cache is a different site and was not used.

Build year, design and registration come from the Register alone; the Register's description contains a typo ('inn 1948') that is quoted as printed. Not used: a Peach Living magazine article in search results says the tower was erected in 1948 and stands 110 feet to the cab, which conflicts with the Register's 100-foot figure. It returned HTTP 403 to our reader, so it is not cited and its wording is not quoted; an editor with access could settle the height. Topo listings give the elevation as 810 ft against the Register's 762 ft (232 m); the story does not state an elevation. Kaufmann is both the Register nominator and the author of the 1819 News essay, which the story discloses. No staffing history or current condition was found, so the status is 'unknown' rather than the brief's 'standing'.

The Decatur Daily wording is as reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page; the newspaper originals were not read. The 2019 sale rests on the NHLR and Forest Lookouts pages; one WebSearch found no independent confirmation. Staffing after 1964 and any fire history are unknown. The register's elevation (1,274 ft) is not used.

Thin record: the only sources are the Register entry and one blog post. No build year, builder, design, staffing history or fire history was found. The brief's record had kind 'unknown' and agency blank, and the story says nothing on either. The September 2025 photo is credited to Will Sprinkle; its image URL and license were not checked, so no photo entry is included. A search for the official Alabama tower list (Alabama Tower 62) would be the next step. The drone videos linked on the Register and blog pages were not read.

No source documents staffing history, when fire-watch use ended, or whether the 2013-2016 restoration talk ever resulted in the tower being opened to climbers; current access/climbable status should be verified before publishing a stronger claim. The eastern_us_lookouts cache page (easternuslookouts.weebly.com/wharton.html) was checked but contains only the tower name, county, and preserve name with no additional prose, so it was not cited.

Staffing (last manned by Colbert Wright, retired 1981) and the 1981 closure rest on one blog post, so the story attributes them to the blog. The blog is also the only source for the 2016 and December 2020 videos; the Vimeo video page was blocked by a verification wall, and its 'abandoned' description seen in search results is not used. The 120-foot height is read from the Register's phrase 'one of the few remaining 120' towers', not from a measured figure. The brief's 'standing' status is kept on the strength of the 2020 videos, but no current condition is confirmed. Access is unknown; the story advises checking with the Alabama Forestry Commission and does not encourage climbing.

Two register pages only. The Wininger page names the administrator but not the builder, so the story does not say the commission built it; the Fabius page is cited only for the shared design. Brief's 'standing' is not stated on the register, so it is proposed as unknown. Searches found no staffing, fire, fate or access source, and no later condition report.

Thin record. The register and one local blog agree on the 1951 build year and the MC-39 design. The Forest Lookouts Womack Hill page (easternuslookouts.weebly.com/womack-hill.html) has a header only (Choctaw County, Alabama Forestry Commission) and is not cited. The blog says some maps call the tower the Daniels Fire Tower; the record's other_names is empty, so an editor may want to add that after checking maps. The blog's AL 48 disagrees with the register's AL 47. No readable source on staffing, fire history, access or current condition. Search snippets for a YouTube short and a Facebook reel describe the tower as still standing; those pages were not readable, so they are not used. The blog also links a Rumble video, which was not read. No photos added.

No build date in any source; the NHLR says Built Unknown and the 1954 survey description is the oldest source read. The first-flight removal is undated, so it is not in events. Brief elevation 361.5 m matches the Register's 1,186 ft (361 m) and the OSM tag of 361. The community's county (Cleburne) differs from the tower's (Independence) in the sources; the tower is about half a mile south of the settlement per the survey. No new photos.

Single register entry. No build date, builder, original site or move date. The register gives Camp Charlotte background but does not tie the camp to the tower, so the story keeps them apart. Searches and the Encyclopedia of Arkansas CCC entry and Preserve Arkansas lookout page do not mention the Charlotte tower. Leads: CCC camp records for Company 4735-C, Independence County fire-tower histories, and the ranch's own pages for when the tower arrived. Private property; do not encourage climbing.

Read: the NHLR page (it includes the 2007 update and the 2019 visit report), Central US Lookouts, the Encyclopedia of Arkansas caption and forest-lookouts entry, and Preserve Arkansas. Open conflicts: cab 12 by 12 ft (register description, Central US Lookouts) vs about 14 by 14 ft (2007 update); single-story base (register description) vs two-story (2007 update). NRHP: the register description says still listed, but the 2007 update says delisted in 2005; the story follows the delisting. The 2000 dismantling date is approximate. No source found for fire-watch years or the last staffing. Access level public is inferred from the absence of any closure, not stated by a source. Current condition rests on the 2019 visit; no newer report found. Living New Deal page returned 403 and was not used.

Current condition is the main gap. A search result (not readable) for a Facebook post from KHOZ 'Around the Table' (https://www.facebook.com/KHOZAroundTheTable/photos/the-old-fire-tower-on-boat-mountain-is-being-removed-ritter-communications-who-o/713667400762432/) has the headline 'The old fire tower on Boat Mountain is being removed' and says Ritter Communications owns the tower and lowered it by crane. The snippet is undated. fetch_text and WebFetch both got only a Facebook login page, so this is NOT used in the story and is unverified. If a human confirms removal, the story's today section and the record status (standing) must change. Suggested check: KHOZ or Harrison news, or Ritter Communications. The same snippet says the tower was manned by the Forestry Service in the early 1960s; that is also unverified. The 1956 staffing comes from the register's quote of a Harrison paper. The register's site visit (March 2022) is the last documented visit we could read. No photos added; the NHLR photo credits were not checked.

No staffing, fire, access or visit source found; the story says so. Staircase layout disagrees: Register says a diagonal internal staircase, the 1942 survey description says a stairway in the center. The Forest Lookouts index lists the Ouachita National Forest for this tower, against the Register and NGS (Arkansas Forestry Commission). Build year unknown; tower already described as standing in 1942. Current condition and access rest only on the Register's 2021 site-visit note and 2023 entry. The record has no height; 30.5 m (100 ft) added from the Register and the 1942 survey.

Single register entry with no history beyond the 2022 site visit. Name collision: US 1764 is not the Newton County Forest Service tower (US 672, us-ar-buffalo-2). Wikipedia's Boston Mountains article places Wahzhazhe Summit, formerly known as Buffalo Lookout, at 35.8637, -93.4931, which matches US 672, not this record; it is not cited here. Consider whether the US 1764 title needs a qualifier so the two do not get merged. Brief's 'standing' is not supported by the register, so it is proposed as unknown.

Do not confuse with NHLR US 1764, Buffalo Lookout Tower, Searcy County (privately owned, Aermotor LS-40), which is a different tower. The record's standing status is not confirmed by any source read: the Register entry gives no status and nothing describes the tower after 1987. No access, visit or staffing source found. The Encyclopedia of Arkansas 1935 date is a caption that credits the Register, so it is not independent. Record height_m was null; 30.5 m (100 ft) added from the survey descriptions.

The nomination text is OCR, so quotes come from the cached OCR and may differ from the printed form. Its condition description dates from the nomination (listed January 2008), not from today; 2010 is the latest status found. The record's kind 'tower' and ownership 'state' are corrected above. Agency comes from the Forest Lookouts page and the nomination's history. No visit or access information found.

Two WebSearch calls found no build date, builder, staffing or fire record for this tower. Access is not stated anywhere, so access is left unset (brief said unknown). Brief agency Privately Owned matches the Register; the Central Lookouts page lists the Arkansas Forestry Commission, so the story keeps both. Leads not yet checked: Arkansas State Archives 1955 operations map and Forestry Commission unit records for Unit 5.

No source beyond the NHLR confirms the Ed Porter rental or the tower's climbability; one WebSearch found nothing. The sale date to Porter is unknown. The 1971 survey places the station on land owned by a Mr. Permee, while the NHLR says Porter bought the land; these may or may not be the same parcel. The record's rental field is null; the NHLR rental note is undated.

Current public access is not established by any source read; the story says to check with the City of Hamburg. Living New Deal page returned 403 and was not used. NRHP nomination PDF (Arkansas Preservation) was not reachable. Second search returned no current-status source. The Register credits the Forestry Commission while the handout credits the Aermotor Company and CCC; the story reports both. Wikipedia infobox 1936 conflicts with its text and other sources.

Two WebSearch calls turned up no build record for Forum. The 1940 item is quoted on the NHLR page; the Swain Mountain tower is unverified. The Huntsville reference is Arkansas; a search hit about Huntsville, Alabama was ignored. Access and staffing are not stated, so left unset. Lead: AGFC records for the McIlroy site.

The history is thin. The 1952 Bucksnort (AFC 4-1) record is linked to this tower only by the Forestry Commission and Bradley County. The NGS record has no coordinates; it places the station about 3-1/2 miles southwest of Hermitage and 1 mile northwest of State Highway 15. The Register coordinates (N 33.418480, W 092.217680) were not checked against that position on a map. Two WebSearch calls found nothing on a Bradley County tower. The AFC Bradley County county page returned 404. Leads: AFC Bradley County office in Hermitage; 1955 state operations map at the State Archives (search result, not read).

Brief lists agency AFC. The Register says 'Administered by AFC' (cite 2), so agency is now in facts; the Register uses the abbreviation and the brief expands it. No source read says who built the tower, so the story names no builder beyond the survey note and the agency-wide CCC and AFC context. Build date, staffing, fires and public access were not found; the Register itself says the build date is unknown. The 1955 station description implies the tower stood by 1955; the story says so only as a survey note. Height conflict, not resolved: the 1955 survey gives about 130 ft (height_m 39.6 is from this figure) and the Register's description says a 100ft Aermotor; the story reports both. Locals Wandering is posted July 4, 2026 (07/04/2026) and is the only source for current standing.

The 1936 build, the land transfers and the 1954 Forest Service transfer come from the register page and agree with the Central US Lookouts summary. Current status is not confirmed: two searches and the register's Arkansas index (which tags it with no status) gave no recent visit or condition report, so the brief's standing was changed to unknown. No source read describes staffing or fire use. The register's cooperator line names the Sylamore Ranger District, which does not fit the St. Francis National Forest description; the description was used and the cooperator line was not. The Encyclopedia of Arkansas media caption for the tower was seen only in search results and was not read or cited. Checker: no source read shows the tower standing today (register page has no visit report); not applied as a status correction because absence of a report is not evidence it is gone. Checker: The story said the Encyclopedia places the tower among the register's Arkansas towers; the entry only lists Horn Lookout Tower in Lee County, so the story now says just that.

Standing status rests on the NHLR visitor's present-tense description of a 1/22/22 site visit; no later check. Access is unknown and the Register says the tower may be on private property, so no access level is set. Height is not in any source read (the 400 ft figure is elevation, not stored in facts). Cane Creek identity with the Ico tower is assumed, not stated by the Central US page, which gives only the name and county. The Encyclopedia spells the maker Aeromotor and the Register's visitor writes Aermotor; the story does not equate them. Only one search and four reads were needed; Encyclopedia used for context.

No tower height appears in the sources read, so height_m is not set. No staffing or fire history found. No access level set; the Register gives no access information. Standing status rests on the September 2020 visit only. Brief's agency (Arkansas Forestry Commission) is supported by both sources. Elevation 1,560 ft is recorded in the story, not as a facts key.

Only one short NHLR entry describes this tower. No build date, builder, design, staffing or access terms turned up in two searches or in the Arkansas lists read (Encyclopedia of Arkansas, Forest Lookouts). Do not merge it with the Iron Springs Recreation Area in Garland County, which is a CCC-built picnic area (1933) and a different place. The record's elevation (128.3 m) and coordinates were not checked against any source.

Height disagreement unresolved: 100 ft (Register, 1941 description) versus about 110 ft overall (1964 recovery). Location: 1941 description says about 4 miles east of Sparkman; 1964 note says about 4-1/2 miles east-northeast. No staffing, fire, access or visit source found; the story says so. Standing status is inferred from the 2021 visit note and 1964 recovery, not stated outright by any source. Record status and access not changed.

Only tower-specific sources are the NHLR entry and an OpenStreetMap node. Two web searches and the Forest Lookouts index stub found nothing more about this tower. The brief's access 'unknown' can now read private (appears), per the Register. The brief's elevation_m 81.7 matches 268 ft, which is ground elevation, not tower height. Register says the tower is still standing, so status is supported. Survivor counts disagree (46 vs about 40); both reported in the story.

Only tower-specific source is the NHLR entry; the Forest Lookouts index names the tower and county only. Two web searches found nothing else under this name. The brief's 'standing' status is not stated on the Register page, so it is omitted from facts; confirm before publishing. The Register gives no build date and no access note, so access is omitted. Brief's elevation_m 100.9 is ground elevation; height_m 30.5 comes from the 100ft description.

Build date and builder not found after two searches. The register gives 100 ft; the 1954 survey (Forest Lookouts page) gives about 110 ft overall and names 3 MI S PINETREE without naming this tower, so the identification is unproven. Agency: the record and the Forest Lookouts page say Arkansas Forestry Commission, but the register says the Division of Agriculture obtained the land, so the tower's owner is unconfirmed. Staffing and public access unknown; do not encourage climbing.

The build date is unresolved. The register says the CCC built it in 1938; the Camden News items reproduced on Central US Lookouts (Feb to March 1935) describe the state forestry commission planning and starting a steel tower near Chidester. The 1935 items describe plans, not a finished tower, and no source read reconciles them with 1938. The radio relay use and the 1985 end of service come only from the register page, with no second source. The 1941 survey places the tower about 8 miles north of Camden, while the 1935 notices put Chidester 16 miles west of Camden; these differences were not resolved and the story avoids both distances. An Encyclopedia of Arkansas photo caption (Poison Spring State Park) was seen only in search results and not used. No access information was found, so access is not set.

Build date and design agree across NHLR and the club page. Staffing comes only from newspaper notices copied by the club site (The Baxter Bulletin), so the keeper dates are secondhand and partial. Current access is unknown: no source says whether the tower is open or climbable, so no access key is set. The OpenStreetMap node is not cited in the story. The web search surfaced no independent 2020s source on condition. Suggest checking the Sylamore Ranger District for current status before publishing.

Height conflict left unresolved: 42 ft steel tower (register), 58 ft observation tower (Encyclopedia of Arkansas), 65 ft with a 14 by 14 cab (hiking group page). These may describe different structures or measuring points; not confirmed. Build year: 1952 (register, Encyclopedia) vs 1954 (hiking group page). Elevation: register 2,646 ft (807 m; the record's 806.5 m matches) vs Encyclopedia 2,681 ft. Current hours and climbing rules are not verified; a search snippet describes weekend hours from an older guide and was not used. The Central US Lookouts page was read, but the text returned was only an index, so it is not cited. The record already has a public-domain NARA photo on Wikimedia; no new photos.

No build date, builder or staffing found after one web search. A commercial listing for a communications tower site near the summit could not be opened (HTTP 403), so nothing from it is used. The Forest Lookouts 1990s sale date is only a decade. The Encyclopedia of Arkansas list of fourteen NHLR lookouts does not name this tower, though the NHLR shows it registered in 2023. Public access unknown; do not encourage climbing.

The NHLR narrative text says NRHP acceptance was 'October, 1995' while the official NRHP reference number's listing date (via Wikipedia/NRIS) is September 11, 1995; I used the official date and noted the discrepancy. Access status recorded as 'unknown' in facts because sources describe a locked gate on the road but say nothing about whether climbing the tower itself is permitted; did not mark it climbable. Did not use any WebSearch calls; three cached/live page reads (NHLR, Central US Lookouts, Wikipedia) were sufficient. Fact-check (2026-10-04): the summit elevation is also given inconsistently across sources -- NHLR says 1,089 ft, Wikipedia says 1,150 ft; the story follows NHLR since that is the only source the elevation sentence cites, but a human may want to reconcile the two.

Built year 1938 in the brief is confirmed by four sources (NRHP circa 1938, NHLR 1938, Wikipedia about 1938, trip report 1938). The NRHP registration form (received by the state 14 Sept 1993) says the tower was deteriorated at that time; its condition since then comes only from two 2021 NHLR visit reports and a 2020 trip report. No source found the date the tower stopped being staffed, so staffing is dated as of 2021. Access wording needs checking with the Mena Ranger District before publication, since the road-versus-hike conflict is unresolved. The brief's elevation (698.6 m) matches the NHLR's 2,292 ft (699 m). Not read: Living New Deal page (403), ARGenWeb Mena and Oden lookouts page, Grokipedia. Photos not added: the NHLR shows a 1996 photo and a September 2021 photo courtesy Travis Howk, and the trip report shows a 1963 photo courtesy Central US Lookouts, but no image URLs or licences were checked.

Build date, builder and fire history not found after two searches; no source names a builder. The register's 'owner by' is presumably 'owned by'. The register says the Forestry Commission owns the parcel, but the record's ownership is still unknown; this is a gap, not an error. Public access to the parcel is unconfirmed. The Encyclopedia of Arkansas list of fourteen NHLR lookouts does not name this tower or Round Mountain, though the NHLR registered both in 2023.

Only two pages were usable. The NHLR entry is a stub with no build date, design, staffing or history. The Central US Lookouts page for Wolf Mountain shows only the name and county in the text we could read. Two web searches for a Miller County, Arkansas tower by this name found no record; the hits were Wolf Mountain towers in Nevada County, California and Oregon, plus USGS and Komoot summit entries that do not mention a tower. The record's standing status rests only on the December 2024 register photo and is unverified. Suggested leads: Arkansas Forestry Commission records, the Arkansas digital heritage operations map, Texarkana or Miller County historical groups. Access is unknown, so no access fact is recorded.

Current staffing and public access to the tower itself are unknown. The only staffing evidence is the 2011 register visit report. The Recreation.gov listing is for a separate cabin at the base of the mountain, not the tower, and I did not treat it as tower rental. Two hiker forum threads on hikearizona.com (one saying the tower was staffed, one saying it was padlocked) could not be read (HTTP 403), so they are not used. The 1959 newspaper's 8,000 ft figure is an older press figure and is not reconciled beyond the report and register. No new photos found.

The FS trail page lists the trail under the Payson Ranger District; the NHLR page (and the record) say Pleasant Valley Ranger District. Both are districts of Tonto National Forest; this may reflect a later district reorganization rather than a factual error, but I did not resolve it and left the record's district attribution untouched. Height (~41 ft) and the 'closed to motorized travel' wilderness note come from Mountain Field Guide, a secondary aggregator that cites the Forest Service and Peakbagger; treat with slightly less confidence than the NHLR and USFS primary sources. Climbability of the tower itself (public access to the cab) is not established by any source read; left as unknown.

No current staffing, access or rental source was found for Baker Butte, so no access level is set. The first-tower date conflicts (1921 NHLR vs 1922 letter) and the 1937 foundation dispute are both in the story. The 1912-1973 items come from West Lookouts transcriptions of Forest Service letters, not from an archive. The brief's 1936 build year matches the NHLR build field, but NHLR describes the CCC as replacing an earlier tower, so the event is recorded as replaced.

Height conflicts across three sources; the story reports them. Current use rests on an undated NHLR line ('in active service'). No staffing history, access or rental source was found, so no access level is set. Living New Deal (cited by Wikipedia) appeared only as a search snippet naming a different model (MC-E4), which was not read in full and is not used. The NRHP PDF scan was unreadable.

Build year, height and the cab size agree across the register, Wikipedia and the Kaibab album. Current staffing and any fire history are not documented in what I could read; the register's 'still in active use' has no date. The NRHP nomination PDF on NPGallery (NRIS 87002478) is listed as not yet digitized, so it could not be read. A tourism listing gives the trail as a 4-mile round trip, which conflicts with the Forest Service's 1.3-mile figure; I used the Forest Service page and did not open the listing. Access level 'restricted' is my reading of the sources, not a Forest Service rule. Brief's 'access: unknown' and 'height_m 30.5' are consistent with the sources; no corrections proposed.

Current staffing and whether the lookout is open this season are unknown. The only opening statement is an undated Arizona Highways article. The record's height_m 13.7 (sourced to Wikidata) is not supported by any source I read, so it is not in facts. Summit elevation conflicts: the register gives 9,166 ft (matches the record) while 1935 and 1939 newspapers give 9,264 and 9,242 ft; a paywalled Trails Offroad listing gives 9,227 ft and was not used. The 2014 Forest Service project concerns the summit radio tower, not the lookout. No new photos found.

The history rests on one NHLR entry. No staffing, access or rental source was found, and the brief's 'permission' access level is not supported by any page read, so removal is proposed. The search budget was used up, so Navajo Nation or BIA records were not checked.

Coordinates disagree: NHLR 36.792819, -113.751968 (the brief's lat/lon) vs inventory 36.77328, -113.80833. Left unresolved and the story says so. Brief's county 'Mojave' proposed as 'Mohave'. A search summary described an older 2011 inventory listing (Semi-Active, R-6 flat design, 10 ft height); I could not find it on any fetched page, so it is not used. A westlookouts page gives the legal description 39N-14W-12; not used. No access information found in any source.

Brief height 9.4 m is not supported by any page read; 31 ft 6 in (about 9.6 m) is. No staffing or rental source was found, so no staffing key is set. Access 'public' covers trail access only; climbing status is unknown. The trail page titles it #71 but its trail log says #321; the story uses neither number. Used two web searches and about six page reads.

Build year 1939 agrees across the register and the federal record; Wikipedia's 1933 alternative is noted. Listing date for the NRHP is unsettled (Wikipedia Dec 14, 1987 vs federal record Jan 28, 1988). Rental and staffing status are NOT confirmed. The Arizona Daily Sun article on HistoriCorps restoring the tower to become a rentable cabin returned HTTP 429 on repeated tries and was not read, so no claim rests on it; it is worth a re-read. The Living New Deal page returned 403. The NRHP nomination PDFs on NPGallery are scanned, with no text layer. The Coconino NF cabin pages I read (camping-cabins and Rooms With a View) do not mention Buck Mountain. HistoriCorps Phase I has no date in the sources read. Access and visit are omitted for lack of a source. No corrections proposed; brief's 1939 build is supported.

Height conflict is unresolved: the register says 82 ft, the 1967 Coast and Geodetic Survey description (via Kemnow) says 100 ft.
