The register also says the tower 'will be transferred' to the register in 2013, which contradicts its own January 31, 2002 registration date; treated as stale text, not used. Present-day status and public access are unknown. The access level 'permission' is my judgment from the reservation location, not a source statement. The 1967 directions may be out of date. Searches for a tribal permit process found nothing. No new photos found. The Fire Lookout Association's managed-unit table, which a search snippet said lists Buckskin as Inactive with a 1963 date, could not be reached in the time budget, so it is not cited.

The 1936 build date and the 121-foot height come from the register alone. No source found names the builder, and the sources checked do not say whether the tower was damaged or spared in the 2002 Rodeo-Chediski Fire, so that gap is left open in the story. Coordinates disagree: the register gives 34.1361, -110.723044 and the Arizona list gives 34.18336, -110.66383, roughly 7 km apart. The record keeps the register point; the editor should check which is right. The brief flags a shared register number; the two sources checked both give US 202, AZ 9 for Chediski, and no other tower with that number turned up in the pages read. Two leads were not used because the pages could not be read: a firelookout.org Arizona key page returned 404 and a hikearizona trip report returned 403. Search snippets claimed a 7x7 foot cab, a Semi-Active status in an older database, and a 2014 closed-for-season visit; none is verified, so none is in the story. The register's active-service line is undated.

Brief height 15.2 m was the original 50-ft tower; the present tower is 83 ft (25.3 m). Staffing as_of 1996 comes from the registration text; no current staffing source was readable. Tonto NF social posts seen in search snippets credit the lookout with fire reports in 2024 and 2025, but those pages did not load, so they are not used. Waymarking and geocaching listings (search snippets only) give 1960 as the build year; neither page could be read, so 1960 is not used. Used two web searches and about five page reads.

The history is reasonably documented, but current status and access are unknown. The last staffing found is 1944. The NRHP nomination PDF is not digitized on NPGallery, so its text was not read. The 1913 newspaper item suggests an earlier tower, which the register does not mention; worth checking against Forest Service records. The 50 ft height comes from the lookout history site, not the register. The brief's record had no built date, so events were added. The FFLA rental list and the register's rentals page were checked; neither names Deer Springs. No photos added; licences not checked. Read budget ran about one page over the cap.

Build year 1936 is solid across three sources. Staffing rests only on a 2013 visit report, so current staffing is unknown. Current access, rental and climbability were not found in the pages read. Tower description conflicts: NHLR credits Pacific Coast Steel, while Forest Lookouts gives an MC-24 tower with no maker named. A peakbagging.com search snippet gives 6380 ft; NHLR and Wikipedia give 6157 ft (1,877 m), matching the brief, so the snippet was not used. The Dude Fire burned the Zane Grey cabin, not the lookout; the events list keeps that distinction.

Construction facts rest on the NHLR entry alone. The brief's access 'permission' is not supported by any source I could read, so access is omitted. No staffing, fire or visit source found. hikearizona.com returned 403; the westlookouts page is an index only; the San Carlos recreation pages found in search cover fishing permits and do not mention the lookout.

Construction, height, registration and the 1936 groundhouse listing rest on the NHLR entry, with the NPS record matching the 1936 year. Attributing the NPS cabin-and-sheds record to the same groundhouse is an inference, and the story says so. Current staffing, rental and climbing status were not found: a 2017 Cedar City news item and a Kaibab lookout-rental search surfaced in search but the news page returned HTTP 522 and was not quoted, and the search hits did not establish the status. The 2024 Forest Service cabin-rental results concerned other sites. Brief record checked: elevation 2654.8 m, county, agency and the 1996 registration match, so no corrections were needed. The brief has no built-year event; this record adds 1944 and 1936.

Current staffing is unconfirmed; no dated staffing record was found. Access is a judgment: the trail is a public hike, but entry to the cab is not confirmed, so the level is set to restricted. The Pocket Fire fate comes from the USFS page. NHLR gives the Peaks Ranger District, while the 2026 fire page places the fire on the Red Rock Ranger District, so the current district is not settled. The 80-ft wooden height appears only in a search snippet, and the Sedona city and AZ Daily Sun pages failed (403, 429), so no height is recorded. Read budget was exceeded (about 9 page reads) to confirm the 2026 fire fate.

Current staffing is unconfirmed; no dated record after 1950 was read, and the register's 'active service' line dates from its 2001 registration. Access level is restricted by judgment: the trail is public, but entry to the cab is unconfirmed. HikeArizona (403 to fetch_text and WebFetch) has a search snippet saying the tower has been closed to the public since 2009. That is unverified and not used in the story; check it before publishing any access claim. The AZ Daily Sun watchtower story returned 429 and the Forest Service trailhead page does not discuss the tower. Read budget was exceeded (about 11 page attempts).

Status corrected from standing to destroyed. Unresolved: the 54-ft rebuild date (1965 per Forest Lookouts, early 1970s per Peakbagging) and destroyed vs extensive damage in the 2011 fire. Two WMI Central fetches returned HTTP 429 and were not read. A Facebook search snippet says the tower is no longer staffed; not fetched, so not used. Staffing and current access are unknown; no access level is set. The brief lists Escudilla Peak Lookout as another name and says the records share a register number; no fetched page uses that name, and NHLR assigns US 826 to this lookout.

Thin record. The NHLR entry is the only source on construction; no staffing, fire or access source found. The Surgent highpoints page failed (expired certificate). The brief has no built event and I did not add one, because the sources say only early 1930s; the editor may want an approximate-date field. The Pastmaps map is dated 1955 and published 1958; the story says so.

Construction and registration facts agree across the NHLR entry, the Forest Service post and the FFLA listing. Access is unknown: the brief says 'unknown' and no source I read says whether the public may enter the cab, so access is omitted. No staffing or fire history found in two searches. The NHLR text has a typo ('Nationa Forest') and the campground page says 'lighting storms'; quotes keep the source spelling. A Wikimedia Commons photo of the tower appeared in search (File:Gentry Fire Lookout Tower in Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests (cropped).jpg) but its licence was not read, so no photo entry was added.

The core history (1936 build, Forest Service ownership, NRHP 1988, NHLR 2001, standing) is consistent across sources. Staffing history, notable fires and current access or rental status are NOT established: the only pages I could read do not cover them, and the NRHP nomination PDF (NARA) and Living New Deal page returned HTTP 403. Search snippets mention summer staffing and a historical-marker text that gives 1906 for the tower, which conflicts with 1936; neither was verified on a fetched page, so neither is used. Do not confuse with the separate 'Grandview' tree lookout (abandoned) listed on firelookout.org at 35.93278, -111.97889. Suggest checking the Tusayan Ranger District for staffing and access before publishing a 'today' section.

Current staffing and any notable fire history are unconfirmed; no source read covers either. Access is a judgment: the road and hike approach are documented, but tower entry is not confirmed, so the level is set to restricted. The 1933 build date and the 54-ft height agree across the register and PeakBagging, but PeakBagging spells the maker Aeromotor where the register says Aermotor. The West Lookouts Greens Peak entry has no event text, only the registry header, so it is not cited. Read budget was exceeded (about 6 page reads plus repeat fetches).

Two sources agree on the cabin's basic history and disagree only on 1968 versus 1969. The restricted access level is an inference from the wilderness location and the stabilization work; neither source states whether the public may enter, so the editor should confirm before publishing. No visit or trail information was found. The Park Service page is dated January 7, 2026. The record's 1969 built event is kept as a conflict rather than a correction; if the editor prefers the register date, change the 1968 event. A search returned Manning Cabin pages, a different structure, which were not used. The structure is a ground cabin rather than a tower, so climbable status does not apply.

Staffing and access are not established by any source read; the NHLR page says only 'still in active service' with no date, so no staffing or access key is recorded. The NRHP nomination PDF (npgallery GetAsset) timed out and the Living New Deal page returned 403, so the 1933 significant year rests on the NRIS asset page alone, and no source read gives a build year for the tower. A Living New Deal search snippet said 1933 but was not read directly and is not cited. Brief elevation 3046.5 m matches NHLR 3,046 m. Verification pass (2026-10-08) relabelled the 1933 and 1934 events from built to other, because neither source gives the tower build year, and added a second-source footnote.

Only two sources were readable: the NHLR entry and the FFLA Arizona list. A HikeArizona trip report for this lookout (photoset ID 63934) may cover access, but the site returned HTTP 403, so it is not cited. A Surgent highpoints page failed on an expired TLS certificate and was not read. Staffing and public access are unknown and the story says so. The record lists ownership as unknown; the reservation setting suggests tribal, but no source I read says so. No new photos found beyond the NHLR photo already in the record.

The record's built 1953 comes from the NHLR Built field, but the NHLR text and the grcahistory page both describe 1953 as a remodel of the 1927 tower; the 1909 crow's nest is the first lookout. Current access to the tower is not in any source read, so the visit fact is limited to the public trail. Unstaffed as of 2009 is inferred from the NHLR statement that the tower is no longer used for fire detection and the 2009 NPS statement that the towers are inactive; no current staffing source was found. The FFLA and NHLR coordinates differ by about 538 m (record conflict); I did not check which is right. The NHLR photo is already in the record; no new photos checked.

Coordinates disagree three ways: NHLR 34.162250, -112.220170; FFLA 34.16244, -112.29272; record (OSM) 34.162531, -112.270441. Not corrected; a surveyed point would settle it. The trail guide invites readers to scale the tower ('you'll even be invited to scale the Horsethief Lookout'); that is not verified, and the story does not encourage climbing. No 2026 staffing or closure source was found. The Horsethief Cabin (a separate 1939 building) appeared only in a search snippet and is not used. Verification pass (2026-10-08) corrected the source name in the story and replaced the vague distance with the computed figure.

Height not recorded: NHLR gives '30 steel tower' with no unit, so no height_m is stored. The 1958 build date rests on the NHLR page alone; a search snippet from a firelookout directory row also gives 1958 but could not be read directly and is not cited. Staffing and access are not verified; the NHLR page says only 'in active service'. An undated hiking-forum post saying the lookout is not in use was not read and is not used. Brief coordinates (33.9811, -111.7978) match NHLR and FFLA; no correction proposed. Verification pass (2026-10-08): the Forest Service project page does not say summit or working, so those words were removed from the story; the 1958 replacement year is flagged as inferred above.

Current staffing rests on a 2018 personal blog and on undated Arizona Highways and onX listings, none from the Forest Service; verify with the Coconino National Forest before publishing staffing as current. The Forest Service Coconino recreation page was readable but did not mention Hutch Mountain. Climbing is described as by permission of the lookout on duty only; the story says not to climb without it. The Arizona Highways article and the onX listing are undated in the pages read. An undated memo from a Long Valley district ranger, describing the earlier cabin as a substandard 10 by 10 ft, appears on the westlookouts page and was not used. The 31 ft figure may be the tower height or the overall structure; I read it as tower height for height_m. No new photos checked. The westlookouts page's 1936 entry says a 30 ft MC-24 replaced the lookout at Mahan Mountain, which conflicts with the NHLR's 1936 31 ft MC-24 at Hutch; the story follows the NHLR for Hutch and does not mention the Mahan entry.

Date conflict unresolved: register and NRHP say 1936; a March 1937 newspaper item says the lookout will be built soon. Design conflict unresolved: NHLR says L-5 groundhouse. A Living New Deal page (HTTP 403 here, so not verified) reportedly says L-4, and the NRHP nomination PDF is scanned with only its cover in the text layer, so its body could not be checked. The westlookouts items are transcriptions of the Prescott Evening Courier, not the paper itself. The 2020 visit report is a volunteer report, not an official inspection.

The register's 2020 visit report (Michael King, October 9, 2020) says 'Staffed? No'. The GrandCanyon.com listing says the tower is generally staffed mid-May to mid-October, which overlaps the visit date, so the seasonal picture is unclear. Height: markers and Wikipedia say 80 ft, the register says 100 ft; brief's 24.7 m is in the corrections list for a human to decide. Builder: CCC versus Kanab contractors is unresolved; the NRHP nomination is a scanned PDF with no text layer on NPGallery, so it could not be read. The climbing claim rests on Wikipedia and a tourism listing; no Forest Service page was read, so the climb is not confirmed by the agency. Brief's elevation 2478 m matches the register.

Build year 1959 and the 54-foot tower with CL-100 cab agree across NHLR and Forest Lookouts. Staffing and access rest on one Forest Service trail page (it carries a July 22, 2025 date line; what that date marks is not stated), which says the tower is used in peak fire season and visitors are welcome; no staff names or fire history found. The brief's access 'unknown' is superseded by the Forest Service statement. No rental listing found; the NHLR rentals page read did not name Juniper Ridge. A Facebook post about the lookout being staffed for the season turned up in search but could not be read, so it is not used. Record height_m 16.5 matches 54 ft. Record lat/lon match NHLR coordinates. No corrections proposed. Climbing status is not stated in any source read, so no climbable flag is recorded.

NHLR and NPS agree on the 1940 date, the CCC build, the 82 ft 6 in height and the inactive status. Access is unknown because no source describes a route, trail or visitor rule. The unstaffed status rests on the 2009 NPS article and NHLR wording, not a current check. The peak-bagging photo is cited only for its date; its license was not checked, so no photo was added to the record.

Current operational status is genuinely disputed between sources: NHLR (page last updated 2016) describes the tower as in active service, and Wikipedia separately attributes a 'open to visitors when staffed in summer' description to the Forest Service -- but checked directly, the USFS Kendrick Mountain Trail #22 page itself says nothing about staffing or visitor access, so that claim should not be cited to the trail page. Wikipedia also says the tower looked damaged and likely abandoned as of mid-2024, with no cited source for that claim. Worth a human check (e.g. a recent trip report or current USFS fire lookout roster) before updating the tower's staffing/access fields. The tower record's 'kind' field (two_story) comes from FFLA's '2-Story Cab' classification, which doesn't obviously match NHLR's description of a flat-roof cab on a 10 ft tower -- plausibly just differing naming conventions rather than a real conflict, so no correction proposed, but flagging it.

Good primary-register coverage (NHLR + NRHP nomination metadata + FFLA list), but nothing on named lookouts, specific fires, visitor access, or current staffing/climbability turned up in cache or the three web searches used. The elevation figure conflicts between NHLR (8,467 ft) and the NRHP record (8,250 ft) and should be looked at by someone who can check the actual nomination PDF or a topo map. Height is also given two ways (48 ft vs 49 ft) by the two registers. No cached page existed for this specific lookout outside nhlr/ and ffla/; fflos (abandoned-sites register) has no AZ Lake Mountain entry, consistent with it still standing and in service.

Height conflict: register says 46 ft, 1989 USFS report says 45 ft 9 in; the story says so and does not pick one. The 1932 letter's 40-ft proposal is quoted on the West Lookouts Arizona index page, not a letter scan. Current status, access and staffing were not found; the 'inactive' wording comes from the 2001 register entry. The NRHP date is the NPGallery 'Date Published' field, matching French Wikipedia (not cited). The NRHP nomination PDF was not opened, so the builder is unconfirmed (Wikimapia credits the CCC, not used). The register says 'National Register of Historic Sites', which is a wording slip for the NRHP. The register spells the district 'Morman Lake'. Record has no height or access data to correct. Verification 2026-10-09: story said 'National Register of Historic Places' as the register's wording; the register says 'National Register of Historic Sites', so the story now says 'the National Register'. Added evidence for the 1932 letter date and the 'Nominated by' credit, both checked on the source pages.

Dates and location agree across NHLR, NRHP and Forest Lookouts: 1928 replacement on Lemmon Rock, 1988 NRHP listing, 1997 NHLR registration, June 2015 closure to visitors. The current status is not confirmed: the latest notice read is the 2015 closure and no reopening was found. Design is thin: the sources read say only lookout house, building, architect unknown; a search snippet from the GVRHC Lemmon Rock PDF describes a ground-mounted L-4 structure, but that page was not read because the page-read budget was spent (not used in the story). The NRHP nomination PDF returned HTTP 403 and an Arizona Daily Star article returned HTTP 429, so neither was read. Wikidata lists elevation 8,773 ft against NHLR 8,720 ft (2,658 m); the record's 2657.9 m matches NHLR, so NHLR is followed. A Historical Marker Database snippet calls it the oldest lookout still in use on the Forest; not used because the page was not read. Record kind 'ground' is consistent with the NRHP building record but no source read states it in those words. Record access 'unknown' should now read closed (2015 notice), not confirmed for today.

Height is the register's 123 ft; not converted because the register does not say whether that is to the cab floor. 'Tallest fire tower in Arizona' is the register's own claim, unverified. The 'still active' statement is from the register page, which gives no date for it, so staffing is left out of facts. Access 'restricted' is an editorial call for tribal land, not a source term. The 2016 vandalism outcome was not found. The 1989 SW Region report has no Limestone entry (grep found none). Counties are spelled Navajo (register, FFLA) and Navaho (West Lookouts). The register's 'Fort Apache-White Mountain' spelling is in its Location field. Record coordinates match the register exactly; the FFLA list is about 0.0003 degrees away.

Record access was 'unknown'; now 'permission' based only on a travel site (RoadScout), not an official source. Confirm the permit rule with the White Mountain Apache Tribe before relying on it. Staffing and fire history were not found in any source read. The register's 'continues in active service' is undated. Height conflict: register gives 80 ft for the 1934 tower, RoadScout gives 60 ft. An FFLA Facebook repost of the register text appeared only in search results and was not used. RoadScout says 'Climb to the top' and that access to the tower varies; the story advises against climbing because no official source gives a climbing rule. The story previously said no source mentioned climbing; that was wrong and is corrected.

Current staffing/access status is only as current as these pages (dates on them unclear), so the tower record's staffing/access fields are left 'unknown' rather than overwritten; story says staffed 'each fire season' per source wording. No photos beyond the one already in the tower record were found within budget.

Every history fact rests on one register entry. The 1932 date and wooden cab were not corroborated: a WebSearch found no McKay-specific source, and the MC-24 towers it surfaced nearby were 1933. The 'still active' claim is from the register page, which gives no date for it, so staffing is left out. Access 'restricted' is an editorial call for tribal land. The register's 'McKay Peak Lookout' title matches the FFLA 'McKay Peak' name; the record's name 'McKay Lookout' is fine. Record coordinates and elevation match the register. Suggest a tribal or BIA records check, or the West Lookouts McKay page if it exists (not cached, not read).

Brief height 213.4 m is wrong; the tower is 60 ft (about 18.3 m). Current access, staffing and rental status could not be found. Agency is left out of facts: the pages read confirm Prescott National Forest but not the current administering unit. The NRHP nomination PDF (S3) returned 403, the NPGallery asset pages carry no readable text, the Living New Deal page returned 403, and the Facebook pages were unreadable. A 1944 'Twenty years ago' column on Forest Lookouts repeats a 1924 notice and is not counted as a separate event. Page reads for this tower went over the per-tower cap because of failed nomination fetches. Used two web searches.

The 1956 claim about a forest fire is cited to Wikipedia only; the reference Wikipedia cites was not opened. The newest staffing evidence is the 2013 GVRHC summary; check the current season status before trusting it. Access 'public' means trail access on foot, not a cab tour; no source states a cab-entry rule. The NHLR and GVRHC agree on the 1916, 1922 and 1966 towers.

Status is unconfirmed. The record says standing and the 2014 register visit form says good condition, but Wikipedia's short description says 'Destroyed fire lookout house' with no supporting text. The NRHP listing (Moqui Lookout Cabin, 1988) has a 1925-1949 period and 1932 significant year, which do not match the 1952 tower; the nomination PDF (NARA s3 link returned 403) and the NPGallery GetAsset link could not be read, so it is not known whether the listing covers the 1952 structure or an earlier cabin. The Wikipedia body describes a groundhouse with a 14x14 ft footprint, while the register describes a cab on a metal tower. A surgent.net excerpt about a 1954 inspection was in search results only (the site's certificate had expired) and is not used. Access is unknown; no access key set. Height 83 ft converted to 25.3 m. The 2014 comment about the author's parents is a visitor's personal note, not an official staffing record; the commenter is not named in the story. Story wording was changed from 'stands' to 'is in' and from 'at this site' to 'in the Blue Ridge area' because the link between the 1988 listing and the 1952 tower is unconfirmed.

Record height_m is 15.2 (about 50 ft); the register and the 2013 summary both give a 53-ft tower, so facts.height_m is set to 16.2. Not a record correction, but worth checking. The record's status_note cites FFLA; FFLA was not read, and the cab-removal claim rests on the GVRHC summary. The GVRHC summary is dated 2013 but has a photo captioned 2014, so the story now says the platform photo is from 2014 and says no later source gives the current state; it no longer says the tower still stands. Register says the cab is metal; the 2013 summary says wood R-6. The newspaper items come through a fan site (westlookouts) and were not checked against originals. No public-access source was found, so no access key is set. The early structures (1926 station, 1929 bid, 1937 50-ft tower) are not tied to the 1958 tower in any source read.

The build dates (1936 original, 1983 replacement) and the 2002 registration come from the NHLR detail page only. Standing status comes from the firelookout.org listing. The date the 1936 tower reached the museum is unknown, so no relocation event is set (events need a year). The NHLR museum page URL the record links as '../us-az-mount-ord-at-rim-country-museum/' returned 404, and the Go-Arizona and Payson Roundup pages returned 403 and 429, so the museum's account (whole tower or only the top section) is unresolved. Search snippets (not used) mention a 2013 forum thread about decommissioning and a rotating camera; they were not verified on a fetched page. Access and staffing are unknown. Suggest checking with the Rim Country Museum (Payson) or the Tonto National Forest Mesa Ranger District before publishing a 'today' section.

The move date is not in any source read; the register gives none, and no museum page was found. The City-Data listing is undated. A search snippet (not read, not used) gives the original tower as 60 feet tall, and a museum video is described as showing the original lookout cab; whether the whole tower or only the cab is at the museum needs checking. Original-tower facts come from the register and Mountain Field Guide. The record's 'public' access level rests on the museum listing, not a current hours check.

History from 1911 to 1976 comes from newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; those items were not checked against the original papers. The NHLR page is the only source for current status ('remains in active service', undated). Access level is not stated in any source read, so access is omitted; the record's access 'unknown' stays. No trail or visit information found. The Forest Lookouts page has a 1996 'National Register' entry whose text was cut short in the page output, so it is not used. Height 30 ft converted to 9.1 m. Record elevation_m 2419.5 matches NHLR 2,420 m. Record tower kind matches the NHLR description. No corrections proposed. Search results and listing sites about current access were not read, so nothing from them is used. The Forest Service Bradshaw Ranger District page was not read.

Height 22.9 m is converted from the register's 75 ft; the brief had no height. Elevation in the brief (2793.5 m) matches the register's 9,165 ft; Dangerous Roads gives 9,179 ft (2,798 m) and was not used. The April 25, 2009 registration date and the July 4, 2009 ceremony are both recorded; they are not in conflict. Staffing is not stated in the fetched pages. Public access status is not confirmed; the only road detail comes from a travel guide. The Abbey claim rests on the travel guide alone. The Forest Lookouts North Rim page gave no tower detail in the text fetched. The 'summit' location comes from the travel guide only.

Brief access 'permission' is not supported by any source read, so no access level is set. Brief agency matches the NHLR administered-by line. NHLR 'in active service' is undated. Two WebSearch queries found no history of the tower. An undated KTAR article about an Oak Ridge wildfire was not linked to the tower and is not used. Staffing, fires and visitor status are unknown.

History rests on the NHLR detail page alone; the FFLA list gives status only. Two web searches found no independent history, staffing, fire record or access rule. Search snippets gave other elevations (2,590 m; 8,525 ft) that I did not confirm from a fetched page, so they are not used. The record had no build year; 1934 is added from the NHLR. Access is left out of facts because no source states a visiting rule. Coordinates differ by under 100 m between NHLR and FFLA.

A hiker trip report in search results (hikearizona.com) says a locked chain-link fence blocks the tower. That page returned HTTP 403 to fetch_text and WebFetch, so the claim is unverified and not used. Another unverified search claim about private ranch land near Chevelon Butte is also not used. The standing label rests on the FFLA list, which carries no date. NHLR gives no current condition. Access is left unset. The 1966 build and Aermotor 1040 model come from NHLR alone. No staffing, fire or Forest Service record was found.

Current staffing and climbing status are not established by any source read; the story says so. The 1959 history comes from a compiled newspaper log on westlookouts.weebly.com; the original clippings were not checked. The brief's access 'unknown' is changed to restricted based on an undated Forest Service alert. The 1952 memo and 1959 newspaper quotes are secondhand via that compilation.

Only two sources, and the history is from a 2002 register entry. Two web searches found no builder, date, staffing or fire history beyond the register. The register gives two mountaintop heights (8,102 ft in the description, 8,113 ft in the elevation line); the record keeps 8,113 ft (2,473 m). The 1930 build year is a decade placeholder, not a source year. No visiting rule is stated in the sources, so the access level is 'unknown'. Current status is unverified; FFLA's 'Standing' does not say the tower is staffed.

Current access and rental status are not established by any source read; the only visit report on the register is from 2010. The record's point (34.36717, -111.01275) is about 1.4 km from the register's coordinates (N 34.377000, W 111.022250); not changed, a human should check which is right. The 1913 to 1952 history comes through newspaper quotations collected on the Forest Lookouts page, not the original newspapers. The LS-40 model name appears only on the Forest Lookouts page. The NRHP nomination PDF did not come through as readable text, so the nomination itself was not used. Height correction is proposed, not applied. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the first-tower sentence now cites both sources, and the 1921 to 1925 sentences are reworded to the sources. A March 1914 Albuquerque Herald item also credits C.H. Kissam, deputy forest supervisor, with building a 100-foot tower in the Sitgreaves forest; the story gives the credit to the 1921 Winslow Mail report and does not reconcile the two. The tower record at data/towers/az/us-az-promontory.json still shows height_m 35.1; the correction in this file's corrections array has not been applied there, so a human should decide it.

Thin record. The NRHP nomination PDF on NPGallery is marked not yet digitized, so the 1939 significant year and any staffing, use or closure history could not be checked. Staffing and rental status are not found in any source read; NHLR page shows no visit reports. Not read: Living New Deal (403), Heritage Index (403), Grokipedia (not used; unreliable mirror). The brief's 2452.1 m elevation matches the NHLR's 8,045 ft (2,452 m). The brief's NRHP number 87002451 is confirmed by NPGallery. The NHLR's 'MC-39' model differs from another mirror's 'MC-40', which was not used. No photos added. Worth a second pass against the digitized nomination if it appears on NPGallery later, or from the Forest Service Alpine Ranger District.

No build year is given beyond the Forest Service's early 1980s, so no built event is recorded. The 1913 plan is a newspaper report of a plan, not confirmation that a tower was built. The access level 'restricted' is our judgment from the trail being open and the lookout being an active staffed lookout; no source says whether the cab is open to visitors, so change it if the Tusayan Ranger District says otherwise. Record name, coordinates and elevation match the register. The Forest Lookouts page also carries a 1972 newspaper report of a violent death at the lookout shack; not used, because it concerns private individuals and says nothing about the lookout itself. The Wikipedia article repeats the register's design text and is not cited. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the earlier draft's sentence that an earlier structure may have stood on the butte but the sources describe none is removed, because a 1972 item on the Forest Lookouts page calls a 'Forest Service fire lookout shack on Red Butte', which predates the early-1980s tower. The story now says only that the sources do not say when a tower first went up. The 1972 item is not used in the story, and its crime report is not used at all; an editor may add the shack, without that detail, if wanted. The directions now name Forest Roads 320, 340 and 340A, as the Forest Service trail page gives them from Tusayan; the earlier draft named only 340A.

Four sources, but the 2020 summary says it was compiled from the FFLA and NHLR websites, so it is not fully independent of them. Access: no source says whether visitors may enter the cab; the summary says the forest road ends at the lookout, and the 2010 hiker walked it. hikearizona.com returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Search snippets gave other hike distances (about 9 miles round trip) from pages I did not open, so they are not used. NHLR and FFLA coordinates differ by under 1 km. The NHLR line about listing until 2023 is not used. Access level is left out of facts because the sources do not state one.

Two web searches and the FFLA rentals check found no current visiting or rental listing, so the story says the sources do not say. The 1931 original comes only from the register's description. The 2011 fire fact rests on posts quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; no independent fire report was read. The FFLA list is undated, so standing status is as of an unknown date. The record's built 1965 is the replacement, so an editor may want to keep the 1931 and 1965 events as added here.

Thin record. The 1960 date appears only in parentheses in the register description, so it is kept as a probable build year. The record's material 'steel' is not in the register text read, which describes a wooden cab on a metal platform; verify before keeping it. The register's 12-foot tower height looks low for a lookout at this elevation and may be a height above the platform; verify before using. Two web searches found no operator, fire history or visiting information. A search snippet attributed a 1960 date to an FFLA row, but the FFLA pages read do not show it, so it is not used. The Navajo Parks rules page was read; the permit page surfaced by search returned 404 and is not used.

Record height 91.4 m (300 ft) matches no source; see corrections. Build year: the register and a 1929 USFS photo say 1929, but a 1928 newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts calls the steel tower recently completed. Left at 1929, unresolved. Staffing and cab access are unconfirmed: the register's active-service line is undated, and the rangeoflight.net trip note is undated. The photo url is the Flickr page, not the direct image file, which I did not extract. Forest Service picnic-site page read: no lookout content. HikeArizona returned 403, so the trail distance is unverified and not used. Access level set to unknown: no source gives a restriction, so the earlier restricted value was unsupported.

Rim conflict is unresolved by coordinates: the record's lat/lon come from the register. The 1926 'fire lookout established at Signal Hill' is second-hand, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page from a Park Service Director's report; the original was not read, and it may be the same site as the 1929 tower or an earlier one. The record's material 'steel' is inferred from the LS-40 model name; no source read says steel. Access and current condition are not verified beyond the 2009 'inactive' statement and the undated FFLA 'Standing' list. One web search was used and found no visiting information.

Almost all history and design detail rests on the NHLR detail page; the FFLA indexes add only standing status and register number. No staffing, access, visit or fire sources were found: hikearizona.com (trail page on Signal Peak) returned 403 to both fetch_text and WebFetch, and no Wikipedia article exists for this lookout. Facts omit access and staffing because no source supports them; NHLR's 'active station' wording is not read as staffed. height_m converts NHLR's 59 ft. The FFLA index coordinates (33.29317, -110.83597) differ from NHLR's (33.29312, -110.83595) by under 10 m; no correction proposed. A search hit for a Washington Signal Peak lookout (nhlr.org/lookouts/us/wa/) is a different tower and was not used. No photos added. Peakbagging's Arizona table (revised 2024-10-02) codes the structure A, meaning good condition and capable of being staffed; that is a building condition, not a staffing record.

Build, cab remodel and registration come from the NHLR page alone. The 'staffed' status rests on one July 2005 magazine mention and is not current. The article's climb rule is general Forest Service practice, not stated for this tower. The lookout named in the article is left out of the story. Search snippets citing an Instagram repost, a Georgia tower and a separate Arizona list were not used. Access and current condition are unknown beyond the FFLA standing label, which carries no date.

The azrock.org 2022 post was read but not used: it calls the tower wood and stone and no longer in use and gives a 7,255 ft peak, both at odds with the other sources. Current staffing rests on an undated blog and an undated Forest Service page, so a dated source would strengthen it. Flickr photos (alanenglish) turned up in search but were not read or added. The CCC attribution comes only from the blog.

Brief's record (1935 built, NHLR 2004 registration, NPS agency, unknown access) checks out. Access can move from unknown to public for the hiking trail, but whether visitors may enter the cabin is not documented. Sources disagree on build details (stone base in the register vs frame on masonry in the narrative) and the narrative also has a 'by 1937' summary that is compatible with the 1935 finish but less precise. Summit elevation (NPS 7,310 ft) differs from the register's lookout elevation (7,238 ft). No specific fire at the lookout was found. The 2008 NRHP date is Wikidata-only. The Forest Fire Lookout Association list shows coordinates 32.01414, -109.32508, slightly off the register's 32.01111, -109.32639.

Nearly all of the history rests on one register entry, plus Wikidata for the county. No newspaper, Forest Service or tribal source was found, and the latest staffing date is 2011. Access is listed as unknown: the story says no public visitor information was found, and it does not infer permission rules. Photo candidates not added: a 2008 Panoramio photo on Wikidata (license not checked) and the register's 2008 photo credited to Chris English (license not stated). Three web searches were run for this lookout, one over the two-search budget.

Current access and staffing are unverified. 'In active service' comes from the 2003 register entry. I set access to restricted on that reading, so please check with the Bradshaw Ranger District. The Waymarking page did not render. Name variants: Tower Mountain (register, West Lookouts) and Towers Mountain (trail guide). The 1924 tower and 1933 tower are not clearly the same structure. No notable fires found in these sources.

Build year (1937), height (32 ft) and standing status agree across the Register, Peakbagging and the FFLA county list. Staffing rests on Peakbagging's code table (AS), not a staffing roster; as_of is the table's revision date. No source names a specific fire, a staffing history or a visitor rule. The access and visit notes rely on the onX trail page, which is commercial, and do not say whether the cab can be entered or climbed. A 1936 benchmark disk under the tower is mentioned on the Peakbagging photo page; not used, since no source ties it to the 1937 build. A Wikipedia Turkey_Butte URL returned 404. The Peakbagging table gives Turkey Butte a usually-staffed code; no recent staffing confirmation was found. FFLA index coordinates (35.03206, -111.90419) differ from the Register's (35.032000, -111.903300) by roughly 80 m; no correction proposed. No photos added.

Closed status rests on the register's wording ('closed to public access'); the register page carries no date, so current status should be confirmed with the Kaibab National Forest Williams Ranger District or the Army before the access note is trusted. The NRHP listing 87002481 is titled 'Volunteer Lookout Cabin' and is a building with significant year 1939; whether it refers to the tower, the earlier wooden lookout or another structure is not stated in the sources read. The record does not show the NRHP listing; a human should decide whether to add it. The 1921 newspaper items name the trail builder H.S. Perry; no further detail was pursued. Record height 9.1 m matches the register's 30 ft; coordinates and elevation match the register. Flickr and tripbucket search snippets repeat the register's closed-access wording; they were not read and are not cited. No photos added. Fact-check 2026-10-08: 'contractor' is replaced with 'successful bidder' (the Williams News wording). The Volunteer Mountain location now cites the Forest Lookouts page too, and the 1930s start-date sentence cites both sources. The 1988 listing is confirmed by NPGallery's date-published field (1/28/1988).

Tower fate is disputed. The Weebly page says it was destroyed; the 2020 NHLR visit and the GVRHC hiking-club report both describe a standing steel frame. The story reports the dispute. Height: the record gives 13.7 m, but both the register and the hiking club give 46 feet (about 14.0 m); a correction is proposed. Model (MC-40 vs CL 100-106) and elevation (9,984 vs 10,029 ft) are unresolved and both are reported. The Living New Deal page and the NARA nomination PDF returned 403, so the NRHP nomination text itself was not read; the CCC architect claim comes from the NPGallery record. Staffing and the trail note are from the May 2020 register visit only, not checked since. The GVRHC PDF publisher name is taken from the domain and was not confirmed from the document. Read budget: seven read attempts, one over the six-read cap (two of the attempts were 403 errors).

Thin record. No visit report, staffing record or fire history was available: the register page has no visit section, and the FFLA list gives only the status 'Standing'. The NRHP nomination text could not be read (NARA PDF returned 403). Search snippets of the nomination, which I could not quote, give conflicting figures: about 45 ft Aermotor HC-40 with a 7 ft cab in one, and 99 ft Aermotor nC-40 with a 7 ft cab in another. Both differ from the register's 46 ft LX-25; this is unresolved and the story uses the register's figure. The proposed height correction (13.7 m to 14.0 m) assumes the register's 46 feet is the right figure. Leads not read: a Western News article of 2025-09-05 about volunteer restoration of historic Arizona lookouts (may cover this tower); a 1964 newspaper item describing a three-person fire-watch crew (historic staffing, snippet only). The Living New Deal page returned 403 and the weebly page for West Peak returned 404. Read budget: six reads, all used.

Only the NHLR detail page gives history: 1962 build, 2022 registration, nominator, site description. The FFLA index gives standing status and the longitude conflict; the Peakbagging table gives the A condition code (good condition, capable of being staffed), which describes the building, not staffing. No staffing, fire, rental or visitor-rule source was found. Searches for Wade Luther and BLM Arizona Strip returned nothing specific to the lookout. A Whitney Pass Road near Whitney Pockets (aravada.com) is a road name, not linked to the lookout. The wchsutah.org Aravada Farm page failed with an SSL error and was not read. NHLR's cabin photos (courtesy of Wade Luther) are not added: their license is not stated. Facts omit height and visit fields because no source gives them.

No build date, builder or staffing years were found in any page read. HikeArizona search snippets give 1930 construction and a 1984 Dry Lake replacement, but HikeArizona returned HTTP 403 and was not used. The NHLR Dry Lake page describes a different, earlier 54-foot tower, not Willow. The FFLA asterisk key (read 2026-10-09) means the structure stands with the cab no longer in place; the earlier wording "marked as standing" ignored the asterisk and was corrected in the story. Access needs a San Carlos Apache Tribe permit; the story does not give a contact.

Brief record checks out: 1936 build, 2001 NHLR registration, USFS agency, 46 ft (14.0 m) height. The NRHP nomination PDF itself was unavailable (HTTP 403 on the NARA S3 copy), so the design and NRHP details rest on the NPGallery metadata, Wikidata and the NHLR page. Staffing status is not given by any source read; the only staffing evidence is the 1912 timeline entry. A Facebook group post says the tower has not been regularly staffed for some time, but it is undated and was not used. Living New Deal also credits the CCC with the 1936 build; not fetched. Access is unknown; the brief's unknown stands. Sources differ on the tree-stand start (register 1910, timeline 1912 stationing) but they are not contradictory. Photos on Wikidata (Woody Mountain Lookout Tower (full).jpg) have no fetched URL and were not added. The 1936 current-tower date is inferred from the register's wood-tower span ending 1936 'when the current tower was built', not from a stated build field. The timeline has no entries after 1936.

Brief height_m 24.4 is 80 feet; corrected to 18.3 m (60 feet) per NHLR and HistoriCorps. Elevation differs: NHLR 6,192 ft, HistoriCorps and Campflare 6,225 ft; not in facts or story. The closed-to-public status rests on an undated third-party Campflare listing that cites no Forest Service page; check the Eldorado National Forest before relying on it. The Eldorado cabins page grep found no Alder Ridge mention. A 2000 news item on the Forest Lookouts page reports a death at the lookout; it is left out of the story as not needed for the history. No source read gives staffing or fire history, and no source confirms a rental has opened. No photos added.

Brief's record checks out on 1966 build, NHLR US 1147 / CA 112, San Mateo County, and standing status (FLA). Brief's 'They share a register number' conflict: Wood Butte, Oregon is listed in the FFLOS register as US 1147 (OR 495) in data/towers/or/us-or-wood-butte.json, while Allen is NHLR US 1147 (CA 112). These are different registers, so the numbers may just coincide; I did not verify this against a single register. Brief's coordinates (37.38709, -122.29501) match the FFLA list, not the NHLR point. Register text gives the tower height as '51" 6" high', which is probably 51 ft 6 in; I did not add height_m because the reading is uncertain. Register says it was closed in 1981, which I recorded as staffing 'unstaffed' as of 1981; the register does not use the word 'staffed'. Access is unknown; the register is silent on visiting. Register photos are credited to Scott McClintock; no image URL was captured, so no photos were added. The register's Salinas origin is not confirmed by the other sources read. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story's 'dry spell' wording was replaced with the source's 'unseasonably dry weather', and the 1956 item is now footnoted in the story.

Correction proposed for height_m (15.2 to 18.3). Access and visiting status were not found in any source, so no access key is set. The Stanislaus album dated 2022 is the most recent source. The 1932 Kling item is the only staffing name found. No notable fires found.

Build date conflicts: NHLR says 1914 (first service); the plaque says the original lookout was built in 1924 and the current structure by the CCC in 1935. The story reports both. Registry conflict, not in the story: the firelookout.org California list (https://firelookout.org/lookouts/us/ca/) gives NHLR US 1180, CA 115 at 38.88230, -120.05465, while NHLR's own page gives US 518, CA 56. The brief's number matches NHLR and was kept. No source read describes the buildings after the June 2010 photo captions, so the current condition is unknown; closed/standing rests on NHLR's undated description. Access is inferred from the Forest Service road page, which does not say whether the buildings are open. No photos added: the Weebly captions cite a July 1941 National Archives photo and June 2010 photos by Ron Kemnow, but give no image URLs. OpenStreetMap way 905267264 (Angora Fire Lookout, tower:type observation) was checked but not used. Budget: 9 distinct pages read against a 6-page budget (the CEQAnet and Forest Service pages were needed for the fire date and access), plus 2 web searches.

Brief status_note ('cab is gone', FFLA) is not verified: the cached FFLA California index shows Standing* and 3-Story Cab with no note text, and the register says only that the roof blew off. The Kern County Fire Department Facebook post could not be read. The 1940 lease is the only ownership history, and the current owner is unknown. The 1954 fire items are the only staffing evidence.

Access level and climbability are not stated by any source read, so the access and visit keys are left out. The FFLA California list at firelookout.org/lookouts/us/ca/ codes the lookout as a 2-Story Cab, Standing, NHLR US 182, CA 7, which matches the record's kind and the register. The record's $500 figure comes from cr-rest-2020.pdf, not the cr-ca-north-2020 report, which gives no amount. The 2021 staffed mark is five years old. A WebSearch turned up a trail-guide snippet saying the modern lookout is manned during fire season, but that page was not read, so it is not cited.

Two substantive sources agree on the 1993 restoration, 1994 registration and the 1990 condemnation; they disagree on build year (1932 vs 1934). The 2026 staffing claim comes from a single article (kymkemp.com) that appears to repost a Forest Service item; treat as seasonal staffing as reported. Sources read do not say whether the public may visit or climb the tower; rental status not found. The Register visit report from 2007 records staffed yes but was not cited. Elevation in a peakbagging entry (6,960 ft) differs from the Register's 6,891 ft; the Register figure is used. Height 8.8 m in our record is unsupported; see corrections. No photos added.

Distance from Quincy is disputed: the register's 2005 visit says 6 miles east, a 1937 Plumas Independent item says about 12 miles east. Not resolved; the story reports both. The record's 'built 1934' is the register's construction-start date; the newspapers show the permanent station completed in November 1937. A human should decide whether the built field needs a correction. The register's 11' figure is not labelled (cab, tower or height), so no height_m is given. The record's event 2025 'restored' overstates the FFLA report, which lists the work as ongoing; it is recorded here as 'other'. The FFLA California list at firelookout.org/lookouts/us/ca/ agrees with the register: Encl. Tower, Standing, NHLR US 601, CA 72.Access level is not stated by any source read, and the last register visit is from 2005, so access and climbability are left out. Staffing 'unstaffed' rests on the 2005 register visit, which is old. The 1994 notice names the Quincy/Greenville Ranger District; the register now names the Mt. Hough Ranger District.

Two sources only: the NHLR entry (a 1939-43 recollection in a January 2003 visit comment, a September 2004 comment on closure and dismantling, and a June 2020 visit report) and one June 1938 Mountain Democrat item quoted on Forest Lookouts. The 1937 build year is the register's; the 1938 item shows the site in use by then but does not date construction. The 1939 and 1943 staffing dates come from the recollection and are approximate. The lineman's-steps tree is reported as the writer's memory and appears in the story only as that memory. Current closure and dismantling status were not checked; two web searches found nothing further. Record height was blank and is filled from the register (80 ft = 24.4 m). Staffing as_of is now the 2020 visit report, not undated.

The name in the record, Babbit Peak Lookout, matches the register, so no name correction is proposed; the 1929 and 1965 items use Babbit and the 1930 to 1960 items use Babbitt. The record has no built year; the 1929 newspapers support 1929 as the build year (construction was announced for July 1929 and the building was in use by late August). That is recorded as an event, not a correction. The 1928 and 1929 papers place the station on Bald Mountain. Identity with the register's Babbit Peak is inferred, not stated, and should get a human look. The newest staffing record is the 2011 register visit; the 2007 and 2009 FFLA reports describe staffed use but not current status. A web search turned up a 2025 Sierraville Ranger District page that does not mention Babbitt Peak; search snippets were not read, so nothing from them is cited. The FFLA list agrees with the record: Encl. Tower, Standing, NHLR US 515, CA 53. Access level is not stated in any source read; left out. No new photos were added.

Construction dates conflict for the first structure (1942 vs about 1943) and the current tower is 1950 in most sources. Status data is thin: the fire-lookouts.org page was last updated in 2013 and Peakbagging.com's closure date (1986) has no other source. No source read gives a current visitor policy for the cab. Elevations differ by about 260 ft depending on whether the lookout or the summit is meant. Access conflict: the NHLR's October 1991 note says accessible to the public; Peakbagging says private land. Settle before the access note is treated as final. No staffing or notable fire found in the pages read. Brief's access was unknown; now closed per the Forest Service page dated Aug 2026, so recheck.
