A Klamath NF Facebook post mentions ALERTCalifornia cameras at the historic lookout; the post was not readable, so it is not used. The Register's photos (credited to the Nancy Hood Collection and the Siskiyou County Historical Society) have no URLs captured, so no photos are added.

Status: the Forest Lookouts page labels it Removed with no date or source; both FFLA lists say Standing, Ground type, no register. The 1971 item is a warning about budget cuts, not a closure. An earlier note that the statewide list showed an enclosed tower with NHLR US 1382, CA 205 was wrong: that number belongs to Scott Bar Mountain (Siskiyou). One web search found nothing about a removal or this lookout. No staffing after 1956 found. No photos. Do not encourage climbing.

The brief's Boucher Hill duplicate claim and 2017 refurbishment both come from cr-ca-sierra-2018.pdf, which returned only 5 characters of text, so they are unverified and left out of events; the Boucher Hill claim does not appear in any page read. The locked-gates and radio-repeater sentences on the Register carry an MVT 10/91 note, so they may describe a 1991 visit. The Forest Lookouts Shadequarter page held only navigation text. Public access is marked restricted from the Register's description, not from a current visit. The FFLA list shows the tower as standing; no 2025 visit report was found.

Current access and visitor status were not found in any source read, so no access level is given. The 2008 FFLA report's trailer date (1973) and the Register's 1960s date are both kept. The 'moved to Oregon' claim in the record's 2007 event is not in any page read and is proposed for removal. The Register's photos (credited to Ron Kemnow and Fred Johnson) have no URLs captured, so no photos are added. The 1914 staffing entry relies on a single 1914 newspaper item as quoted by Forest Lookouts, not on the newspaper itself.

Record kind two_story is not confirmed by these sources; they describe a 14 by 14 foot steel cab on a 10 by 10 foot concrete block base. Staffing as_of uses Wilderness Portal's 2026-06-19 verification date. Fire-lookouts.org's access and staffing details are reported alongside Wilderness Portal's rather than overriding them. No specific fire at the tower is named in the sources read. No photos added: the NHLR photo captions have no image URLs in the pages read.

Record access 'unknown' can now read 'permission' (NHLR and Monterey County Now agree). The source_pages entry for a 2017 NYT article returned HTTP 403 and was not used. The OpenStreetMap way only tags the tower as an observation tower, so it is not cited. Staffing 'unstaffed as_of 2011' rests on the Peakbagging text; no source gives the year it was decommissioned (the article says 'sometime in the 1980s'), so no decommission event is recorded. Possible photo lead: archive.org item casbcfm_001261 (Sept 1955), licence not checked, not added.

Register number conflict, not resolved: the NHLR page for this lookout prints US 594, CA 65 (kept in the record). The firelookout.org California list (fetched from cache) shows NHLR US 883, CA 93 for Sierra Buttes and US 594, CA 65 for a Sierra Peak in Orange/Riverside, so one of the numbers may be wrong. The brief's conflict note says the two share a number. The Forest Service trail page also shows a phone line with 'Open by appointment only'; that appears to be a district office contact, not the lookout, and was not used. Current staffing and visiting rules are unverified: the last dated staffing source is 1992, and the 2024 Ukiah article is a visitor account. The 1954 storehouse loss is not the lookout itself. The 1926 report relied on telephone messages and is hedged in the event note. No photos added.

Brief height_m 18.3 is unsupported and is proposed for removal. Build year: NHLR says 1931, the 1986 bulletin says the steel tower came in 1934; both are in the story. Access is unknown: no source read says whether the public may visit, and the brief's access field was left unset. The 2019 Cal Fire notice proposed removing an abandoned residence and a communications tower; the Forest Fire Lookout Association California list (source 7) shows it as Standing, and the 2020 and 2025 notices show it in use, so the tower's current role is clear but its visitor status is not. The Sierra Vista weebly page has many 1931 press clippings; only the three quoted in the story were read. Elevation: NHLR 2,785 ft (849 m) is used by the brief and not repeated in the story. No photos added.

Current status is the main gap. The newest dated source is the fire-lookouts.org page updated March 1, 2013, which contradicts its own 2010 and 2012 entries. The Yosemite.com listing is undated and the Peakbagging photo caption is from 2002. Check the Sierra National Forest before publishing. The county correction is a spelling fix. The brief's 'built 1951' is the present cab, not the first structure; consider noting the 1900 origin in the record.

No source read states the lookout's status or staffing after 2019, and the camera post is undated in the cached text, so current status rests on it plus the 2019 register entry. The firelookout.org California list has a 'Gone' status on the row just above Slater Butte, but that row's coordinates (41.00268) are not Slater's (41.85805) and Slater's own status cell is cut off in the cached text, so it was not used. The Gaia GPS road listings (1.7-mile road) were seen only as search snippets and were not used. The register numbers (US 1378, CA 201) match the brief. No access or visit information was found, so no access or visit key is set. No photos added.

Brief's 2003 'restored' is not supported; sources say reopened and rededicated. Cab size conflicts (14x14 ft in NHLR vs 365 sq ft in ANFFLA); the blog's 365 sq ft is the whole structure. Brief omitted the 1980 closure and 1970 helicopter delivery. Access 'public' is inferred from the hike-only trail and volunteer staffing; no official Forest Service access statement was found. Staffing as_of is the hiking guide's update month, not a staffing schedule. Photos not added.

Access, staffing and current condition are not in any source read; the access key is omitted rather than guessed. The FFLA Southern California list (firelookouthost.org/southern-california) has a Smith Mtn row, but its columns are jumbled in the cache, so it is not cited. The 1964 Built field and the 1944 BC-301 caption conflict with the description; the story flags both. Height 18.3 m in the record matches the 1931 60-foot tower plan, so it is proposed for removal. The status key was removed: no source read gives the current condition, and the story says so. Pending a Cal Fire San Benito-Monterey Unit or Los Padres NF source for access and status. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story's 'best-known item' claim was removed as unsupported.

Two Smith Peak lookouts exist: this Tuolumne tower (Stanislaus NF) and a separate Plumas County tower near Lake Davis. The brief's source page smith-peak.html is the Tuolumne page and is correct for this record. The Plumas story (us-ca-smith-peak-plumas-national-forest) states that the Tuolumne tower burned in 1987; this record confirms that from NHLR, the Forest Lookouts page, and the 1988 Merced Sun-Star item it quotes. Staffing evidence is dated 2012 (PDF) and undated (NHLR, present tense); the 2024 visitor report describes the access road only and does not confirm staffing or visiting rules, so current access is unverified. The Roaming Civic page was read only for the access-road passage. Photos on NHLR are credited but no licence was seen, so none added. The 2012 report is the only source for the catwalk and roof work.

Record source_pages includes smith-peak.html, which is the Tuolumne Smith Peak; proposed correction above. The register says the cabin sits on a '9 foot enclosed timber tower', which is unclear and was not used in the story. Current staffing ('staffed as_of 2020') rests on the register; the Sierra REC article has no date in the cached text. Pages about Smith Peak near Groveland (the 2024 Roaming Civic post and a 1931 'administrative site' claim in a search snippet) concern the Tuolumne tower and were not used. No fire events attributable to this tower were found in the newspaper items read.

No access or visit information was found in any source, so facts.access and visit are omitted; the record's access 'unknown' stands. Height was not found. The no-rental line comes from an undated citlink.net copy of a CAL FIRE list; confirm on a current Cal Fire page. Peakbagging and the register disagree on the forest (Lassen vs Plumas) and on staffing; the story reports both. The July 2026 fire report says near the lookout, not at it. The register's photo credit (Ron Kemnow, 2008) is noted but no image URL was found, so no photo entry.

The 1974 record date is correct for the current tower; the first station dates to a CCC build in 1934 (Redding) and a 1920 mention. Height 6.1 m comes from a 1977 NGS description of about 20 feet, converted; the register gives no height. The 1947 discontinuation is known only from a reprint of a Weekly Adin Argus item on the Forest Lookouts page; the original paper was not checked, and the closure may have been seasonal. Access is 'public' per the register, which is undated; no recent visit or staffing report was found. No fire events were found in the sources I read. Grokipedia says the station dates to the 1920s; it is an AI-generated page, so I did not use it. Photos are credited on the register (Ron Kemnow, 2008; Fred Johnson) but no image URLs were found, so no photo entries.

Status is disputed and not resolved. The register says the tower remains, the FFLA California list marks it Standing*, which its key defines as a tower with the cab no longer in place, and the FFLA 2012 chapter report says the site no longer exists and is a repeater site. The register's text is internally inconsistent about the cab: a 732-6A cab tops the tower with a repeater antenna attached, yet the cabin and storage structure are said to be removed. The FFLA key therefore adds a cab-gone reading that conflicts with the register's 732-6A entry; the sources do not settle it. The 1977 newspaper item predates the 1982 build date, so an earlier lookout may have stood here; the sources do not say. The access note is from 1991. The site carries high RF exposure; the story advises against climbing. One web search added only CEQA notices and a repeater reference.

No public access or visit information was found, so facts.access and visit are omitted; the record's access 'unknown' stands. The record's kind 'two_story' is not stated by any source; the register describes a 14 by 14 ft cab on a 10 ft brick base, so the kind may be a shorthand worth checking. Height was not found. Builder (CCC vs district) and base material (brick vs concrete block) disagree across sources; the story reports both. The conversion to a communications facility is undated. The register's 1949 photo credit (Los Angeles Times) is noted but no image URL was found, so no photo entry. The 1974 end-of-staffing date (district history) and the 'at least 1962' register line are consistent, not in conflict. The Forest Fire Lookout Association list is a chapter page; the 'comms fac.' row is the only source for conversion.

The first-tower dispute is the main issue. The Mountains Foundation (1922 80-ft tower on the peak; 1934 damage and replacement) conflicts with the 1933 newspaper transcriptions (80-ft wooden tower at Grass Valley collapsed January 1933; steel tower on Strawberry Peak begun May 1933) and with the register's 1933. The newspaper text comes from a transcription page quoting The San Bernardino County Sun; I did not check it against the original paper. The corrections proposal depends on that. Access is set to public because the Mountains Foundation says it was open for the 2025 season, but the Forest Service copy showed a temporary-closure notice and a winter closure, so re-check current status before publishing. The staffing as_of date is undated because the register page is undated.

Brief height_m 95.4 is wrong; the tower is 30 feet (9.1 m) per NHLR and the 1930 plan, so the record is corrected. Access is unknown: no source read confirms whether the summit road or the lookout is open to the public today, so no access level is set and the story says to check with the Modoc National Forest. Staffing has no current source; the last mention is a 2007 photo note about possible summer volunteers. The 2025 Cal-North report says forest staff and the report author discussed relocation or restoration; no decision is recorded. The 1929 fire is named for Sugar hill, but the sources read do not say whether it reached the summit. Facebook group posts found in search were not used. No photos added.

The 1931 build date rests on the NHLR 'Built' field; no second source gave it directly. Web search results pointed to Girard Ridge Lookout (Shasta-Trinity, 1931) and to Washington State Sugarloaf lookouts; those are different towers and were not used. The record's material 'wood' came from the design and is not stated by any source read; the register describes only the 8 ft concrete tower. The FFLA list has a separate Tuolumne 'Sugarloaf' (enclosed tower, gone) that is not this lookout. No source read gives a current access level, so access is omitted. The staffing 'no longer staffed' is inferred from the 1954 closure clipping, which says closed and does not explicitly say never staffed again.

Brief's 1972 build date corrected (see corrections). Height conflict left open: 30 ft (NHLR) vs 50 ft (1934 newspaper). No public-access or visiting source found, so access and visit keys are omitted. Staffing evidence ends at the June 2008 CAL FIRE list. Brief's agency wording matches the weebly header.

District: the register (OCR 'ldyllwild') says Idyllwild Ranger District and the Forest Service page says San Jacinto Ranger District with an Idyllwild office; the story uses the Forest Service name and cites both. Closure status is the main open question: the Forest Service page (temporary-closure notice, closed-for-the-season banner, posted hours) and the Mountains Foundation (currently closed) are both undated copies, and the record says public. The access level is set to closed; re-check before publishing. Elevation disagrees across sources: register 8,752 ft (2,668 m; the record's 2,667.6 m comes from here), Mountains Foundation 8,828 ft, Forest Service 8,846 ft. The record is left unchanged. The 77-year figure is not explained by any source. It would be close to 77 years if counted from the 1917 cabin, but that is my inference only. The 2017 chapter report spells the peak Taquitz, and it says America Core kids (the record says youth crews); the story says young helpers. The register text has typos (ldyllwild, suppports) that I left out of quotes or copied as printed.

Record built year 1931 stands as the start of construction; the completion year (1931 or 1932) is worth a human look. Radar end year is disputed (1967 vs 1970). Peakbagging's claim that the lookout was used in WWII for enemy plane spotting is unsourced and left out. No source found confirms staffing or road status after 2012; a 2024-25 search returned only general fire-season news. A Lassen News item on the Thompson Peak Initiative (a Cal Fire grant) appeared in search results and was not read.

Built year 1933 comes from the register only; the August 1934 newspaper item calls the lookout new, which fits. 'Still standing' is the Forest Service's own line on an undated trail page. No source read says whether the cab is open to visitors or climbable, so access level and climbability are left out of facts. The Ojai Valley News hiking column returned HTTP 429 and was not read. Record name, coordinates and elevation match the register; no corrections proposed. The weebly page spells it Thorne; the register and Forest Service use Thorn. No staffing after 1958 was found.

No page I could read says whether Timber Mountain is staffed now or open to climbing, so the story says so and no access or staffing keys are set. A search snippet hinted at Forest Service staffing and a 2022 blog visit, but snippets were not read pages and are not used. The 1912 platform is 'may have' per NHLR only. The 1932-1945 history comes from one compiled history site quoting newspapers and Forest Service records; not checked against originals. The 30-foot height is the NHLR's tower height; the total height of the cab on it is not given. The brief's build year (1966) and elevation check out.

Coordinates and elevation disagree. The record (from the register) has 35.849955, -118.572367 and 8,218 ft (2,505 m). Fire-Lookouts.org gives 35.5101 N, 118.3421 W and 9,292 ft; peakbagging.com also says 9292 ft. The 1937 and 1946 newspapers give 8,200 and 8,550 ft. Left unchanged; a map check is needed. Staffing: the 2025 brochure says a Forest Service employee resides in the tower; Fire-Lookouts.org (undated) says it is no longer staffed, and in the same paragraph says it is currently staffed. The access level 'restricted' is my reading of the gate note; check current gate policy with the Forest Service before editing. 1947: the register says not in active service, but a July 1947 newspaper item names two lookouts on Tobias. 1936 (Fire-Lookouts.org) and 1937 (newspaper, 'will be manned June 10th') differ on when manning began. District: the register and Fire-Lookouts.org say Hot Springs RD; the 2025 brochure says Western Divide RD. The 1954 burning was Sunday Peak Lookout, not Tobias. The 1947 item names Etha Rice and the 1951 item names Bea Rice; the story keeps each name with its own date and source. The story now states the fire-lookouts.org staffing conflict in full (no longer staffed, and staffed 5 days a week in the same paragraph).

Build year is circa 1940 (register) and believed 1940 (Tehachapi News); the California lookouts history page quotes a June 1936 notice planning a Tollgate lookout, so the first plan may predate the 1940 build. Staffing status is 'unknown': no page states today's status. 'unstaffed' would only be an inference from the Tehachapi News wording that staffing ran until the 1970s. The 1954 fire is quoted from a newspaper transcription on the California lookouts page (Bakersfield Californian), not the original paper. The preserve acreage differs between sources. The article's own date is not shown in pages read; the 2022 dates come from the register's photo captions.

The 1973 closure rests on a single visitor's comment on the NHLR page, so it is marked as one account. The 6.1 m height is the 20 ft tower alone, per the NHLR description. Current access is not documented in any source read; the 1973 'long, dusty dirt road' comment is historical and not used as current access. A web search summary mentioned a 2015 trip report describing the lookout as locked and shuttered; it was not fetched and is not used. Wikipedia's Tomhead Mountain article has no lookout history. The only survival source is the NHLR page; no second source for the South Fire damage was found.

Height is disputed: the register and a July 1938 newspaper say 20 feet, a June 1939 newspaper and Carey's quote of a 1945 forest history say 30 feet. The record's height_m 9.1 matches the 30-foot figure and was left unchanged; it is not in facts. Access level 'closed' rests on Carey's 2012 post (public access prohibited since 1959); no current Forest Service notice was checked. The FFLA California list marks this site 'Standing*' and the meaning of the asterisk was not found. Newspaper quotes come from the Forest Lookouts compilation, not the original papers. Used 1 WebSearch and about 8 page reads, two over the per-tower budget, to get the access and height evidence.

The NHLR page gives the tower as 41 ft and the CCC build as 1934-35; I used those. A web search summary mentioned a 45-ft tower from a trail guide and a Groveland office phone number; neither was fetched or verified, so neither is used. The sources do not say whether the 2009 cabin restoration and the 2012 rental plan are the same work, and no source read confirms the current condition or whether the public can visit. The record's 'abandoned' is from the 2012 report and is dated to that year. The height 12.5 m is the tower only, converted from 41 ft.

Brief height_m 12.2 is wrong; NHLR gives a 60-foot steel tower, so the record is corrected to 18.3 m, with the 1937 65-foot figure noted. Elevation 2103.1 m matches NHLR's 6,900 ft. The Forest Lookouts page has nothing after the August 1937 item, so the story is thin on 1938 to today; the 2002 photo captions are ambiguous about whether the lookout was replaced and no date is given. Access is unknown: no source read says whether the public may visit. Blog and trip-report pages found in search were not used. A further search for post-1937 Turner Mountain history (tower replacement, the 1913 house, current use) would be the next step. No photos added.

Status 'standing' is from the record and the 2026 news reports (which call it a 30-foot tower); I did not visit the site. Height 30 ft converted to 9.1 m. Open question: the 1932 station versus the 1966 tower. The sources read do not say whether they are the same building; the built-1966 event cites only the 2026 news report, not a source that links the two. The Feb 2026 photo caption said the cameras would soon go in, while the 31 Mar 2026 report says they are active; the story gives both. The Forest Lookouts clippings are a secondary compilation of old newspaper items; I did not check the originals. Access changed from the record's 'unknown' to 'private' on the register's wording. Registered date from the register page (Feb 2, 2020). Fact-check 2026-10-08: the 1932, 1935, 1938, 1956, 1989 and 1990 dates were confirmed on the Forest Lookouts page and added to the evidence quotes.

Staffing 'staffed' as_of 2019 is the register's undated present-tense text, taken with its 2019 registration date; no current staffing schedule was found. The Forest Service district page I checked had no lookout listing. The 14-ft tower height is converted to 4.3 m. Access left out of facts: the sources read give no current visiting rules (the only visiting statement is from 1971). The 1934 CCC date is from the register; the Forest Lookouts page repeats it from a Klamath NF history volume that I did not read directly. Record fields other than these were not checked. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the 1951, 1961, 1963 and 1971 dates were confirmed on the Forest Lookouts page and added to the evidence quotes; the story now says 'an earlier lookout' because the register says 'earlier', not 'first'.

Record height_m 121.9 (about 400 ft) is not supported by any source I read; it looks wrong for a peak lookout, so I left height out of facts. Please verify before publishing. Record 'standing' is not confirmed by any text read: the register photos run to 2017 and the page does not say whether the cab stands now. The 2026 status is unknown, so the story does not say the cab stands. Access: the Forest Service describes the roads but says nothing about the cab; access level was left out. Sources disagree on forest administration at the summit: the register names the Tahoe, while the Forest Service route page places the road at the Tahoe-Toiyabe junction. Search snippets (not fetched) mentioned an early-1930s first lookout, a boarded-up cab, and differing summit heights (8,431 to 8,455 ft); none was used in the story. The 1958 clipping is from the Reno Evening Gazette as cited on the Forest Lookouts page. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the 1986 survey date is in the register text and now appears in the evidence quote; the 1958 date and Reno Evening Gazette attribution were confirmed on the Forest Lookouts page; the Forest Service page does not use the word 'dirt', so the story and trail note now say OHV routes.

Two minor date conflicts (build year 1935 vs 1937, and burn month August vs September 2009) are noted in resolved_conflicts; both resolved toward the more corroborated/specific NHLR figures. Did not verify current-day staffing schedule beyond the 2023-era Edison article, which may be slightly dated.

1934 build date rests on the registry alone; no newspaper or Forest Service record was read. The 1969 smoke report is quoted second-hand on a hobby page. Access is inferred from one trail report (6.5-mile fire road); no official rule found. Height corrected to 20 ft per registry and trail report. Status 'Demolished' on Angeles Adventures conflicts with the rest; kept as standing (cab gone). The brief's 'unknown' access replaced with 'public' on the basis of the trail report and no closure found. Staffing 'not staffed' as of 1987 comes from the registry's wording.

Register and Forest Lookouts page carry the main facts. The Forest Lookouts page is a compiled set of newspaper clippings and survey notes, not a primary record. Current status (2026) is unverified: the newest visit report is 2011, and no current staffing, open-to-visitors or rental source was found. Access level left unset because no source says whether the tower is public. The firelookout.org California list shows Weaver Bally as a standing tower under NHLR US 1060, CA 105. An earlier FFLOS number, US 1790, CA 36, sits on that list's Warm Springs Mountain row (Los Angeles County), not this lookout, so it was removed at fact-check. A WebSearch returned AllTrails and Peakbagging pages, which describe the road as needing a high-clearance 4WD vehicle and give elevations of 6,990 and 6,971 ft; these were not read and are not cited.

Proposed corrections are for human review, not applied. The record's NRHP 78000295 and other name point to the Prospect Peak Fire Lookout in Lassen Volcanic NP; Wikipedia and the 1977 nomination both describe that structure as abandoned on Prospect Peak in the park. Unresolved: Wikidata Q14683716 puts its coordinates at the West Prospect site (40 35 38 N, 121 22 45 W) and records a 1981 'structure relocation' for the NRHP lookout, while Wikipedia gives 40.573 N, 121.345 W for the park lookout. Check the NRHP location and any move before accepting the registers correction. Current status and access are not verified: the search also returned an ALERTCalifornia camera page and a syncrosafari page saying the tower is still in service, but neither was read (page budget). The weebly header says Shasta-Trinity NF; the register and 1955 inspection say Lassen NF and Hat Creek District. The record's kind 'two_story' was not checked against the register's 'enclosed timber tower' with a cab on top. The story now says the NRHP listing 'appears' to belong to a different structure, because the Wikidata coordinate conflict above is still open.

Identity unknown. The OSM way (1477386021) carries name Wilson Tower, emergency=fire_lookout and tower:type=observation, but no ownership, height or date. No register, Forest Service or news source found for a Wilson Tower at these coordinates. Two web searches (Siskiyou and Shasta-Trinity; Wilson Mountain). Search results surfaced other places named Wilson Mountain or Mount Wilson (Los Angeles County, Arizona, Virginia) and Shasta-Trinity lookouts (Girard Ridge, Little Mt. Hoffman, Hirz Mountain) that do not carry the Wilson name. The name may be local or informal. A human could check the Klamath and Shasta-Trinity ranger districts or search for a nearby peak name.

Height 32.9 m is converted from the register's 108 feet. The register also mentions 29-foot towers of another type, which we did not attempt to reconcile. Staffing as_of is 2015 because the register's staffing line is undated; the 2015 Cal Fire post is the newest dated item read. The Placer County lookout page returned HTTP 403 and was not used. Access level is not stated in any source, so none is recorded. Verification 2026-10-08: the 1947 date is now worded as the register's own account (materials stored until 1947, when manpower was available to build), not as a confirmed completion date; the climbing advice was removed because no source supports it.

Current access and rental status are not stated in any source read. The NHLR entry is dated 2017 and the Peakbagging photo is from 2011, so the status is at least several years old. The 1962 hire is known only from an Oakdale newspaper as quoted on the Forest Lookouts site; the story now says she took a summer job as a fire lookout, which is the newspaper's wording. The rental finding is negative: the FFLA California list (checked 2026-10-08) shows ten rentals, none at Woods Ridge. Staffing as_of is 2017, the NHLR's status date. Verification 2026-10-08: the advice to ask the ranger district and not to climb the tower was removed because no source supports it.

Brief's 2022 entries for the cab door and stair treads: the 2022 report gives no year ('last summer'), so the event year is the report year. Brief's 2021 solar date is supported ('As of 2021'). Staffing is as of the 2020 article; current staffing unknown. Material (wood vs steel) and gate location disagree across sources and are flagged, not resolved. The Dangerous Roads guide is third-party; confirm the gate and winter closure with the Dolores Ranger District. Pages read: 6 (NHLR, Forest Lookouts, the 2022 PDF with two greps, the Journal article, Dangerous Roads). Searches: 1. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the register puts the gate 0.3 mile below the tower and the story now says so; the 2019 batteries were being replaced and the story now says so; the 2020 article is dated only by its 50th-anniversary reference, so the JSON no longer gives a month.

Access, visiting and rental status are not in any source read, so no access or visit keys are set. Staffing is from the 2019 Register review only; no current staffing source. No fire history found. Record kind 'platform' is proposed as 'tower with open cab'. The NPS page is for an ancient tower with a similar name and does not mention this lookout. Park Point Lookout, the park's other lookout, was not researched. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story no longer calls the Forest Lookouts summary 'earlier' (its date is not given) and says towers were mainly built in the Classic period, rather than 'around' those dates.

No independent source beyond NHLR and the FFLA Colorado list was found in the cache or a quick check; both agree on name, location and standing status (FFLA uses 'Deadman Mountain'). The NHLR page is unusually detailed for a short tower (CCC predecessor, 2004 visit narrative, 2019 condition note, Sprint cell-site encroachment), so confidence is medium rather than low despite having only one substantive source. Worth flagging: do not confuse with the unrelated 'Deadman Mountain Lookout' in Wyoming, which also appears in the raw cache and is a different structure.

Stair count: Wikipedia gives 143 stairs for the last stretch of the trail; the NRHP nomination counts 243 steps up the whole stairway. Staffing: the first documented staffing is Helen Dowe (1919-1921), so the story no longer says staffing began with the 1912 station. Built dates: the NRHP nomination (first station 1912, 1919 tower, 1951 present lookout) and Wikipedia agree; the register's 'constructed in 1912' for the cab conflicts, and the correction proposal relies on the nomination. Wikipedia gives the NRHP listing as both 1991 and June 13, 2003; the NPGallery record supports 2003. Elevation differs: register 9,702 ft (2,957 m; the record's 2957.2 m), Wikipedia 9,748 ft (2,971 m). Visitor numbers in the register differ (over 15,000 a year in one passage, about 40,000 a season in the 2019 note). The 2025 chapter report says the lookout was not staffed in 2025 and will not be in 2026; the staffing record is updated accordingly. Whether the cab is open to visitors is not established by these sources, so the access note stays cautious. The record's 2013 'frame-off restoration' and 2015 roof claims come from chapter PDFs I did not open; I cited the register's 2013 renovation instead, and the 2015 roof is not in the story. The 2022 stair work is the chapter writer's understanding, unconfirmed by the district.

Two registers agree on design and dates. The access statement rests only on onX, a trail-guide site, so confirm with the San Juan NF Pagosa Ranger District. No staffing history or notable fires found in the sources read. NHLR Lookout.aspx?id=915 returned HTTP 500 and was not used. No rental listing found. A search result about a prescribed fire on Eight Mile Mesa was not read and is not used.

Build date disagrees across sources and is left open: NHLR detail gives 1911, its description gives 1912, and Forest Lookouts gives plans c.1907 and construction 1908-09 under Ranger Jack Cammann. Staffing also disagrees: Forest Lookouts gives 1910-14 with abandonment, but a 1919 guidebook it quotes describes a man stationed there in dry periods; the abandonment year 1914 is the end of that range. Record height_m 274.3 equals 900 ft, which matches the trail's elevation gain from a search summary, not a structure height. It is omitted from facts; the record field should be checked. Record items not found in pages read and left out: the $500 FFLA grant (2008), the 2015 restoration and removal from the high-risk list. A search summary of Wikipedia mentions a 2015 cupola rebuild by Historicorps; not read, not used. NHLR gives registration December 7, 2007, but a chapter report says three lookouts including Fairview Peak were added to the register in the year it calls this year, with June dedications; that report's year was not confirmed in the text read. Access rests only on the 2019 survey; no current closure or rental notice was read. No photos added: NHLR mentions a July 2024 photo by Ian Roberts but no image URL was retrieved. Budget: six page reads and two web searches used.

Coordinates (38.040996, -105.012697, elev ~2252m per OSM) fall in the Wet Mountains near Greenhorn Mountain/St Charles Peak/Lake Isabel, San Isabel National Forest area, but no cached or web source ties a named lookout to that exact point. Checked every cached NHLR and FFLOS Colorado entry's coordinates (both index pages) and none are within a reasonable distance of this node. Three WebSearch queries (generic coordinate/region search, San Isabel NF fire tower history, named Wet Mountains peaks) turned up nothing specific to this structure. Possible the OSM 'Fire Tower' label is generic (e.g. a different kind of tower, or a genuinely obscure/undocumented lookout) rather than a proper name — worth a human look if better aerial/historic-map sources become available.

Core history (1908 stone shelter, 1933 damage, 1939 rebuild, c.1942 enlargement, 2014-2017 restoration, 2018 vandalism) is consistent across the NHLR, Forest Service, Historic Routt County and Colorado Preservation pages. Open points: the NHLR elevation (10,759 ft) differs from the 10,839 ft given by the agency and two other sources; the exact year staffing ended is not recorded; the History Colorado page (which gives about 1947) returned no text when fetched, so it is not used. The brief's NHLR registration date (September 1, 1997) was confirmed on the NHLR detail page. No photos were added.
The cohost-co firelookout.org page listed in the brief's source_pages returned a 404; dropped from sources. No specific named fires found in available sources.

Core history rests on NHLR and the West Lookouts newspaper quotes. The 1915 end of staffing and the lightning abandonment come from one 2014 hiker blog, so treat them as medium. Access is inferred from hiker accounts; no Forest Service statement was found. The 1919 guide quoted on the West Lookouts page describes old road access that is not used in the story. No rental listing for Leon Peak found; the Next Summit article's rental lookout is a different site.

Exact height_m and precise CCC construction dates beyond 1940 were not found; RIDB only says 'built in the 1940s' while NHLR gives 1940 specifically, so I used 1940. No conflicting built-year sources requiring a resolved_conflicts entry. Status/climbability for independent day hikers beyond the paid overnight rental is not documented in the sources read; left visit.climbable unset rather than guess.

The brief's kind 'ground' may be wrong. The NHLR visit form asks about stairs and a walkway around the 'LO', which suggests an elevated cab, but no source states the height or structure type, so the record was not changed. Dates rest on NHLR (1939, 2009), the 2009 NFP success story, and the December 1939 Mesa Verde Notes. No current staffing schedule was found; the NHLR visit reports are from 2009 and 2019. The 2009 success story names the fire management officer differently in the caption and body, so no name is used. The Wikidata and OpenStreetMap pages in the brief were not read. The parkcation.com trail page was seen in search results but not read.

The brief's events omitted the 1916 build and the 1948 end of use; those are added here as events, not corrections. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced by a 'public' level based on visitor accounts and the absence of a closure in the sources. Official Forest Service access status was not checked, so please verify before publication. The 2019 condition note from NHLR conflicts with the SummitPost restoration claim. The 1919 newspaper item is quoted second-hand on Forest Lookouts. height_m is omitted because the sources give no tower height. No new photo URLs were added.

The 2010 NPS success story is the best history source and agrees with the NHLR description on 1951, the mid-1950s tower and 2002. The NHLR Built field of 1964 is unexplained and should not be used. Current staffing rests on an undated NPS overlook page. Visiting rules were not found; confirm with Dinosaur National Monument before any visit. The 2010 PDF also says the cabin was used until the mid-1950s, which is consistent with the register but not repeated in the story.

Build year and design rest on the register alone (one source, 2010). The status conflict is real: the register describes the tower in the present tense, while the Colorado list (undated row) says Removed. No newer source was found; the Southern Ute Indian Tribe is the authority on current condition. Two searches gave no staffing, fire or build history, so none is in the story. The 50 ft figure is the register's stated tower height; a separate cab-floor height was not stated. The record's point is about 2 km east of both register coordinates; the location and status corrections are proposed, not applied. Tribal land with no public access: the story does not encourage visits.

Unresolved: builder (Wikipedia says CCC labor, Conservancy says local contractor) and last year of use (NHLR and Conservancy say 1969 or late 1960s, Wikipedia says 1978). The NHLR's own build dates conflict (summary 1934, history 1933). The NRHP nomination PDF host was unreachable from the crawler; the NPGallery asset page was read instead. Forest Service and firelookout.org pages failed to load and were not used. History Colorado page returned no text. The Conservancy access statement is undated; confirm current access with Rocky Mountain National Park before publishing. No rental information found.

The 1945 build year rests on the register alone. A search result summarised an FFLA Colorado page (firelookout.org/cohost-co/soda.html) as giving 1962, and quoted a 1962 Mesa Verde forestry report second-hand. That page returned 404 in our fetch and the report was not reached, so neither is cited. Please check before publishing; if confirmed, the build year and the story need revising. Coordinates conflict: the record uses the FFLA point 37.12861, -108.46667, and gives the register point as 37.07307, -108.27353, about 18 km apart; the register's coordinates were not in the text read, so this is not resolved. Kind: the record says platform, FFLA says Crowsnest, and the register describes an open cab on a 22-foot steel tower. Height is not recorded as height_m because the register does not say whether 22 feet runs to the cab floor. Staffing and current condition are unknown. Access is on tribal land with no contact given in the sources. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story previously called the Ute Mountain Ute Agency a 'tribal agency'; the register names it only as a cooperator, so the story now says just that.

Two register-level claims conflict on where the cab is today: FFLOS says CSU's Environmental Learning Center, while the 2012 FFLA report and Forest Lookouts say Running Deer Natural Area. The story reports both and leaves the status 'standing' for the cab. The City of Fort Collins Running Deer page returned no text when fetched, and a search snippet gives a 1967 removal date that could not be checked against the page, so neither is used. Hiker and booking pages were not used. No photos added; the 2016 Coloradoan gallery was seen only in search results.

Height is not set: the Register gives only the lower 30 feet used, not the overall height. No staffing, access, visit or fire history appears in any source read, so those keys are omitted. The Register does not say who moved the tower from the Apache National Forest. Status standing rests on the 2019 condition review. The cooperator evidence quote now includes the name Mesa Verde National Park, as printed on the Register page. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story no longer says the wooden platforms are 'due for replacement'; the Register says they 'could use replacement'.

Core build, registration and design facts are from NHLR. No source after 1961 covers staffing, and nothing found says whether the tower is rentable or open to visitors. The NHLR page does not mention rental. The 1944, 1961 and 1964 items are Vernal Express clippings transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page; originals not checked. NHLR id=892 page returned HTTP 500. Height conflict (30 ft vs 19 ft 6 in) is unresolved. Wikipedia Zenobia Peak article has no lookout content and was not cited. Grokipedia not used.

The end date of fire use (1988 per the register, seventies per Cold War CT) and the fate of the original tower (described as standing in the NHLR text, removed per the 2017 visit report) are unresolved. Living New Deal (search snippet only; the page returned HTTP 403) lists a demolished CCC steel tower at Mohawk State Forest, which is unverified and not used. The Cornwall Historical Society page shows a 1924 photo of Henry Bouteiller at the tower, courtesy of Jean Bouteiller, but no image URL was retrieved, so no photo entry was added. Current condition is only as recent as the January 2017 visit report.

height_m 24.4 is our conversion of the register's 80 ft. Casali Companies is the contractor for the 2018 work, and its page is self-description, so its restoration claims are only its own. The 1911 quote from the town map PDF comes from extracted text with broken columns; check it by eye if it matters. No staffing history or fire events were found in the sources read. The town or a local history collection may hold staffing records.

No build date, designer or owner name is confirmed. The only build claim is an unverified forum reply (2008). The OpenStreetMap record (way 428652238) names a private owner; that name is left out of the story on purpose. The Connecticut former-lookout register (8 sites) does not list this tower. A land-records check in Canton (summit parcel) would give the owner of record and may date the tower. The 2008 forum post says the tower stood then; the 2021 blog implies it still does, but neither is a current inspection. Access is private: the story does not encourage visits.

No build date, designer, cost or design history for the tower was found in two searches and about five page reads. The station history covers the Red Hill buildings (designed and built 1930-1935 by Alexander Blair) and does not mention a tower. The NRHP record for the station (NRIS 07000698) mentions no tower. The record's elevation_m 65.2 is the NHLR ground elevation (214 ft), not tower height; height_m 30.5 is the register's 100 ft converted, and the cab-floor height is not stated. Staffing as_of 2016 is the register date; 1999 is the last regular staffing. A towerdex entry for a Highlands County structure in Venus was seen in search results but is unverified and not cited. The travel-blog 'water tower' at the station is not a fire lookout. Visit: no climbability or trail info found.

No build date, design, height, or staffing found in the two sources read. The NHLR 'Elevation' of 27 ft (8 m) is ground elevation, so the brief's elevation_m 8.2 is not a tower height. The map's 1957 photogrammetry suggests the tower stood by then, but that is an inference, not a stated date. The Eastern Lookouts Ashby page has only a name and county, so it was not cited. Page reads: 6.

Thin record. The register gives the design, condition and registration; no build date, builder, staffing, fire history or access rules were found in two searches, a Florida lookout report grep, and the cached register and Eastern Lookouts pages. The record's elevation_m 39.3 matches the register's 129 ft site elevation, not tower height; height_m 30.5 is the register's 100 ft converted, and the cab-floor height is not stated. The Eastern Lookouts page gives only the county and a legal description. A White Springs Carillon Tower in Hamilton County appeared in search results; it is unrelated and not cited. Access level left unset because nothing in the sources states it.

Thin: a short Forest Lookouts entry (county and 2005 sale), OSM construction tags, and a general FDACS surplus notice that is not specific to this tower. No build date, height, builder, photo, or post-2005 record found. The Carrabelle Wikipedia article and the city history page do not mention a tower. Editor should decide whether the 2005 sale makes the record's standing status wrong, and whether to keep this record as is.

Thin record. The register gives the design, condition, elevation and registration. No build date, builder, staffing, fire history or access rules were found in two searches and about five page reads. The USGS well record USGS-291414082560985 is named DOF-CEDAR KEY TOWER (ROSEWOOD TOWER) and sits about 57 m from the register's coordinates (29.237940, -82.935888 vs 29.2374648, -82.9356754, our calculation); it is cited in the story as a possible same-site lead, not a confirmed identity, and the register itself does not mention Rosewood or DOF. The 'Suwannee' in the register name is unexplained. Search hits that were not used: an 80 ft LS-40 in Colfax, New York (not Florida); a 1801 Cedar Key watchtower (not a lookout); the Dunnellon ranger station. height_m 24.4 is the register's 80 ft converted; cab-floor height not stated. The brief's elevation_m 6.1 matches the register's 20 ft site elevation, not tower height.

The build and replacement history rests on one undated tourism flyer (about 2021, from the file name and its '91 years' phrase) plus a one-line Eastern lookouts entry. The NHLR page has no build date. Climbability is not stated by any source, so it is left out; the fence is the only evidence. Eastern lookouts names Apalachicola NF, which conflicts with NHLR and the flyer; treated as an error. Social-media photo posts were not used.

The Riverbend article is paywalled: fetch_text returned 403 and WebFetch returned only the opening. The move's destination, reason, timing and the tower's build year are all unknown. Re-check the full article before publishing any move detail. The NHLR page gives no build year and no access information. The Commons photo (March 2024, CC BY 4.0) is a new find.

Thin record. No build year, height, staffing, fire or access information appears in any source read. The Wikipedia and marker pages cover the community, not the tower. The register does not state 'standing' outright, so the record's standing value is not confirmed here. The Commons photo description does not confirm that it shows this tower; check before using it as a tower photo. Consider a state (FDACS / Florida Forest Service) records search before publishing more.

Current status is the main gap: no dated source read confirms the tower stands. Search snippets not read or cited: a Weebly listing line with a 1937 National Archives reference, and a social-media comment saying East Tower (Taylor) and Olustee Tower are different towers, which would be worth checking before any name merge. The Flickr photo has no image URL retrieved, so no photo entry was added. The onX page is a commercial trail guide, used only for road access.

Thin record. Neither the register nor the Forest Lookouts page gives a build year, staffing history, fire history, or access rules. The FDACS page describes the forest's wildfire history but does not mention the tower. The OpenStreetMap point for the tower was checked but is community-edited and not cited. One page read ran over the per-tower budget because the first grep pass was partial. The register prints the elevation as 133 ft (41 m); 133 ft is 40.5 m, and the story uses the register's printed figure. Verification 2026-10-08: the steel-tower description is now attributed to Forest Lookouts, which is the only source that says steel; 'northern Baker County' was corrected to Baker County in northern Florida; the advice to ask the Florida Forest Service and not to climb was removed because FDACS does not support it.

Register page is the only substantive source. The brief's 2017 News-Press article (news-press.com, story 99520472) returned HTTP 403 and is not cited; the register links to a 2017 article under a 'Their watch has ended' title, but nothing shows it concerns this tower. The register gives no build date and says the tower may have stood in one or two earlier places, so 'standing' applies to the 2024 site only. A web search for Golden Gate turned up an unrelated Naples tower (a 2000 antenna structure from a tower database, not read and not used). Brief elevation 5.5 m matches 18 ft in the register. Access is omitted because no source describes it. Photo captions were read: two captioned 1990s and credited to the Florida Forest Service, one captioned 2024 and credited to Brad Eells, and several more credited to Eells without dates. Image URLs were not captured, so no photos array. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the story no longer says nobody recorded the build date, and its photo sentence now covers only the captioned photos.

Height (85 ft, 25.9 m) and the 1936 date come only from a blog quoting a Water Atlas PDF that was not opened; verify before publishing a stronger claim. NHLR's '52 ft (16 m)' is labeled Elevation, so it is ground elevation, and the brief's elevation_m 15.8 is that figure. Climbing status of the tower is not documented. Page reads: 7 (one over the cap), because some pages were re-read to get full text.

Thin record. NHLR is the only tower-specific source: location, elevation, registry number, registration date and administrator. The Forest Lookouts page is a stub with name and county only. No build year, designer, staffing, fire history or access/visit information was found. The Scribd history (a user upload of a 2006 Division of Forestry compilation) is general context on the 1930s tower network and does not name this tower. Florida Memory image pages (items 140289 and 106202) returned HTTP 403, so any photo captions there are unread. Wikidata has a bare label only. The NHLR Florida index shows no rental or visit data for this tower. Recommend a Florida Forest Service or regional newspaper check for the build year before a fuller history. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the register never uses the word standing; the story now attributes only the present-tense placement to it.

Thin record. NHLR is the only tower-specific source: location on SR 20, elevation, registry number, registration date and administrator. The Forest Lookouts page is a stub giving name and county (spelled 'Putnum'). Wikipedia supplies only community context. No build year, designer, staffing, fire history or access information was found. Do not use archive.org item casbcfm_001263 ('Hollister Division of Forestry headquarters', 1956): it is a San Benito County, California photo, a different place. A cached page describing a Hollister fire ('Black Tuesday') has no Florida link and was excluded. Florida Memory item 106202 (Florida Division of Forestry 'fire tower' photo) returned HTTP 403, so it is unread and cannot be used to date the tower. The Scribd history is general context and does not name this tower. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the register never uses the word standing; the story now attributes only the present-tense placement to it.

Thin record. NHLR is the only tower-specific source: site description, elevation, registry number, registration date and administrator. Conflict to check: the same NHLR entry uses present tense for the tower yet calls its site a former Division of Forestry site, and the sources read do not say whether the tower itself remains as described. The Forest Lookouts page is a stub with name and county only. No build year, designer, staffing, fire history, access or rental information was found; the NHLR Florida index has no rental or visit data for this tower. Wikidata has a bare label only. The Scribd history is general context and does not name Homosassa. Tampa Bay Times and Lakeland Ledger tower articles returned empty or HTTP 403, so they were not used. Recommend a Citrus County or Florida Forest Service check of the current condition before any status is assigned. Fact-check 2026-10-09: status moved from standing to unknown because the register never uses the word standing.

No build date, staffing schedule or public-access information was found in the sources read; access is omitted rather than guessed. The Register's 100-foot figure is used for height_m, following the convention in other records. The booklet is a Scribd copy of a Division publication, not checked against an original; it is cited only for the Dixie County background, and its text never names Jonesboro. Site described as mostly abandoned by the Division, with the tower still used occasionally. Abandoned has no year, so it is left out of events. The footnote 2 title follows the Scribd page heading.

Single source: the NHLR entry was the only page read that gives a build date and design. The NHLR 'Elevation' of 103 ft (31 m) is ground elevation, not tower height, so the brief's elevation_m 31.4 is ground elevation. The Lakeland Ledger 2015 article on Polk's aging towers returned HTTP 403 when fetched; its search snippet suggests the tower near Lake Pierce was 'barely hanging on', which would change the status. Check it before publishing. The FL DEP Broussard Catfish Creek Preserve plan says park access is from Firetower Road south of Lake Hatchineha Road, but it does not confirm the tower's location, so it was not cited. Page reads: 6.

The 2005 purchase year is inferred from a January 7, 2006 article saying one year ago, and it is shown as inferred. The News Bulletin 2015 article is paywalled after its first paragraph, so only the registration sentence was used. No design or height is given in the sources read. No dated source confirms the tower's current condition beyond the undated city page calling it the fire tower beside the center. Climbing access is undocumented.

The record's point (29.115192, -80.948894) is not described on the OSM page itself. No NHLR or former-site entry matches it, and the OSM entry gives no name or history. The Florida tower list at tnlandforms.us (revised 2016) has no tower within about 6 km of the point; its only nearby entry is labelled 'gimlet' with no lookout attached. The OSM entry (way 264235672) was last edited about nine years ago (changeset 48449176). Suggest checking aerial imagery or the Volusia County GIS to see what structure is there. If it is not a lookout, the record should be removed. The Tiger Bay Road drill tower is a county training structure, not linked to this entry. The story is short because there is nothing more to tell.

One detailed source (Forest Lookouts, quoting the Bradford County Telegraph for 1939 and 1942) plus an OSM point. The page's 100-foot height is used for height_m (30.5 m). The OSM ele value 64 is a map elevation, not tower height. Waymarking pages for this tower exist, but their text did not cache and were not cited. A WebFetch summary of one page mentioned a May 2023 visit log but no condition, so it is not used. Today's condition and access need a Florida Forest Service contact or a recent site report.

Single-register history: every built, design and registration fact comes from the NHLR page; the Eastern US Lookouts page has no details for Magnolia. The Florida Memory and Lakeland Ledger pages returned HTTP 403 to fetch_text, so they were not read. Who holds the land is unclear: the register says ownership reverted to adjacent landowners and names the LDS church as administrator. Access is marked private on that basis; confirm before publishing. The register gives height only as a 100 to 120 ft range, so no height_m is entered. The record's county, agency and 1933 build year agree with the register.

Thin record. NHLR says little is known. The only substantive source is an urban-exploration photo tour (Abandoned in 360, August 2025) that uses hedged language ('likely', 'perhaps') and gives a 1953 completion, a Florida Forest Service builder and a guessed 100 ft height; those are attributed in the story and not put in facts as verified. The mid-2000s closure (the article's only dated support for it is a wall map marked Spring/Summer 2008), the 1999 tower count and the staffing narrative in that article are not used as facts; the story attributes the closure to the photo tour. The link between the NHLR 'Marion County Airfield' tower and the photo tour's Dunnellon Ranger Station is inferred from names and location; no page says they are one structure. Museum of Florida History returned HTTP 500 and floridamemory.com returned 403; not retried. Access, visit and staffing are unknown and left out of facts. NHLR credits a photo to David Viero, but the image and licence were not checked, so no photo entry was added. Two web searches were used. Fact-check 2026-10-08: story now says registered (NHLR 'Date Registered', not accepted), gives the Dunnellon Army Air Field as the name the field was known by, and attributes the mid-2000s closure to the photo tour without implying a record.

Every fact here rests on one Register entry. No build date, staffing, fire history or access information was found in the two searches and page reads. The record's standing status has not been checked against anything newer than the 2016 rehab. Height_m uses the Register's 120-foot figure, following the convention in other records. No photos were located.

Thin history. The NHLR entry is the substantive source: it gives the 80-foot height, the standing-since-1935 date, the Indian Mound location, the USFWS administration and the 2014 nomination by Brian Pippin, but no build date, builder, staffing or fire history. The Forest Lookouts page has little more than a header. The OpenStreetMap node gives height 25 (units assumed metres) and ele 2; facts height_m 24.4 is the NHLR's 80 ft converted, and the OSM tag is not used as a fact. The refuge fact comes from the FWS page (refuge establishment, 1931) and is not tied to the tower in any source. The Friends of St. Marks history timeline has no entry for the tower. The floridamemory.com item on a St. Marks refuge fire tower was not readable (HTTP 403). Access, visit and staffing unknown and left out of facts. The NHLR photo is credited to Brian Pippin; no photo entry added. Two web searches and about six page reads were used. Fact-check 2026-10-08: story now says registered (NHLR 'Date Registered', not accepted) and describes the Forest Lookouts page as carrying little more than a header.

The WPTV report carries no date in the copy read, so its 50-year figure and the drought-season staffing read are undated. Staffing is coded 'emergency', the closest schema value, for the severe-drought watch described; the report gives no schedule for other seasons. The Register and the report use different agency names (FDACS and Florida Forest Service); neither source says how they relate, so both are reported as written. No build date found. Access is omitted: neither source describes public visits.

The 1931 build date and Forest Service credit come from the NHLR page and the Eastern US Lookouts page, which agree. The HMDB marker's CCC claim conflicts with that date and is unresolved; the story says so. Current climbing access is not confirmed by any official source. The only climbing statement is in a Komoot trail listing, a third-party app whose text may be generated, so verify with Osceola National Forest or Florida State Parks before publishing the access level as public (floridastateparks.org returned HTTP 403). The marker's listed coordinates are within roughly 15 m of the register's, so the marker sits at the tower. The record's height_m of 30.5 agrees with the register's 100 ft, but the register does not say whether that is to the cab floor, so it is not restated as a fact. A USFS page on the Olustee Experimental Forest timed out and was not read.

Two cached sources agree on Lee County, the 100-foot Aermotor design, the 1961 assembly or erection, the Florida Forest Service role and the 2024 registration. Both News-Press articles (2015 and 2017) returned HTTP 403 from fetch_text, so they are not cited. Search snippets from them mention the 1961 acquisition and that this is the only standing fire tower in Lee County; they need a cached copy before staffing, fires or the SR 80 location can be added. The brief's 'built 1961' is kept, but the sources describe assembly or erection in that year, not an original build date. Access is omitted because no source states a visiting rule.

Very thin: a short Forest Lookouts entry (county and agency) and an OSM height tag. Two web searches and a Wikipedia check (Palmdale, Florida) found no tower history. The 60.96 m height is a volunteer map value, not verified. Contact the Florida Forest Service before publishing the status or height as fact.

Only two thin sources, and the build date and builder are unknown. The register's WPA claim is the nominator's own belief ('I believe'). A Florida Memory catalogue entry titled 'Gate entrance and tower at CCC camp in Pine Top' (floridamemory.com/items/show/62708) appeared in search results and points the other way, but floridamemory.com returned HTTP 403 to fetch_text, so it is not cited; check it by hand. The 1957 article's state-built line covers the headquarters buildings and does not say whether the tower was one of them. Access is marked restricted only because the tower sits at a forestry station. Note for the team: the 'A Legacy Remembered' CCC marker (hmdb.org m=55674) surfaced in a Pine Top search, but its coordinates and text place it at Olustee, not Pine Top, so it is not used here. The record's ownership 'federal' is the main correction proposed; the agency field already reads Florida Forest Service.

Single readable source: the NHLR detail page (cached). Unresolved conflicts, not in the story: (1) A Waymarking page (wm5GXN_Punta_Gorda_Lookout_Tower_PID_AD7808) cites a 1982 Florida DOT description of a steel tower about 110 feet high, about 8.5 miles southeast of Punta Gorda on the northeast side of US 41 northbound. That conflicts with NHLR's 100 ft and forestry-station siting. fetch_text could not read the page body (only the title was cached), so nothing from it is quoted; a human should check whether it is the same tower. (2) The record's news-press source (2017 Lee County fire-towers article) returns HTTP 403. A search snippet describes the Caloosahatchee Forestry Center tower in Lee County, so it is probably not a Punta Gorda source; not cited. (3) The Forest Lookouts Weebly index lists PUNTA GORDA under Glades County, but only in navigation text with no body, so it is not used. Not verified: construction date, builder, fire history, staffing, public access. The record's ownership 'federal' is contradicted by NHLR (correction proposed). No photos added; the record's NHLR photos are all rights reserved.

Thin record. The 1958 fire item is quoted from The Evening Independent on an enthusiast site; the page dates it October 12, 1958. I did not check the newspaper itself. The 2005 bid appears only on that same site (dated September 14, 2005); I found no buyer, sale record or government auction listing. The 2015 report excerpt is headed '2015 & beginning 2016'. It lists Salem #268 (standing) and #318 (removed) but names no county, so it is not known whether either is this Taylor County tower. The status 'standing' in the record comes from the OSM and eastern lookouts records; no dated source I read confirms it. The FFLA Florida caches in data/raw/ffla have no Salem entry. The title and publisher for source 2 come from the URL and search results, not the document cover. Suggested checks: a Florida Forest Service public-records request for the 2005 sale and tower history; the Florida lookout association about Salem #268 and #318; OSM node 10012727105 (tagged tower:type observation). No corrections proposed.

Original build date is not in any source (register gives no year for the State's build). Brief's access 'unknown' corrected to closed. The Weebly Flagler page (Wadsworth record) attaches a 1959 Southside rename to a Flagler County tower; that conflicts with the park history. The Florida chapter report asks whether the Jacksonville Heights tower was re-erected as Southside; unverified, not used. No new photos added.

One map feature and no other record. Status 'standing' in the record rests only on the map point; no photo or second source confirms it stands, so verify before publishing that status. The name is generic. No owner or operator identified, and I did not trace the mapper's edit history. Firehouse report (2010, Lake County) is background only and is not linked to this structure. Searches for 'The Fire Lookout Tower' in Lee County found nothing. Visit: private, nothing to visit.

Only the NHLR page describes this tower in text. The 2015 Commons photo is matched to the register's location by our own comparison of coordinates, not by its caption, so treat it as likely rather than confirmed. No build date, staffing or access terms were found. Florida Memory item 326330 (a Florida Forest Service building and fire observation tower) returned 403 and was not read.
