Photos not added, though University of Idaho Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness History Project items (sbw019, sbw087; 1938 photographs) surfaced in search and could be checked for license and use. The 1930 cabin date is consistent across three sources.

The brief's height_m 4.3 is not supported by any page read; it matches the 14-foot footprint, so a correction proposes removing it. Elevation (6,844 ft, 2,086 m) and the 1933 build and 1967 abandonment agree across sources. Staff names come from firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts; Idaho Fire Lookouts adds Larry Johnson (1935) and Mr. Malcom Smith (1945), which firelookout.com does not list. Spelling of the design name differs ('Nez Perce' on firelookout.com, 'Nez Pierce' on WillhiteWeb). The Idaho Fire Lookouts page includes reader comments, which are not cited. Access and trail details come from a hiking guide and a personal site and are dated 2021 to 2023, so check current road and trailhead conditions before publishing. Photo credits (Tyler Nyman, Carol Elam collection) have no image URLs, so no photo entries were added.

NHLR lists the tower as available for rental despite the extremely difficult approach (boat + 6-mile/5000ft hike); worth confirming current rental arrangements with the Salmon-Challis National Forest before publishing that as an active booking option. Build year (1933 vs 1934) unresolved across sources.

Height and elevation figures differ slightly between NHLR/idahofirelookouts (7,667-7,681 ft; 72 ft tower) and Wikipedia/NRHP nomination (85 ft ground-to-cab). Did not independently pull the NRHP PDF itself (John F. Elliott, 1992) for primary confirmation; Wikipedia's summary of it was used instead.

The tower record's 'conflicts' entry lists firelookout_com as giving a built year of 1928, but that page's actual text matches nhlr exactly (1916/1928/1950 sequence) — likely a mis-extraction when the record was built. Recommend the conflict be cleared rather than left open; no new correction filed since the record's 'built: 1950' field is already right. Fact-check 2026-10-04: removed a sentence claiming secondary listings 'collapse' the three build dates and citing recreation.gov for the full 1916/1928/1950 sequence — no evidence quote supported that framing (recreation.gov's page does independently state the same three dates, confirmed by spot-check, but the sentence as written made an unsupported claim about other listings). Also rewrote the 1950-cab sentence, which copied the nhlr.org description almost verbatim.
Consider updating the record's 'built' field or adding a note that 1980 is the current tower's build year, with the site's lookout history going back to 1931.

Location: the record point (47.60944, -116.05861) matches the Idaho site pin for the nest. firelookout.com and the Forest Association index give a camp point at 47.62906, -116.05026, about 2.3 km away; not changed. Kind is 'unknown'; a tree-built nest may fit 'tree', editor's call. No staffing record. Kresek's book was not read directly; its 2010 claim is second-hand via the Idaho site.

Build year is 1930 in four sources and 1933 on firelookout.com, which may be a copy of the Burton Peak cabin's date (also 14x14 and 1933); this is not confirmed. Elevation differs: 8,608 ft in the register, 8657 feet on the two other sites. No staffing names were found; Idaho Fire Lookouts says none are documented. The 2021 Dixie Jumbo Fire material is in Keeping Watch's collection; no source read says the fire reached the cabin, so the story does not say so. The hike-in is inside the wilderness and no trail distance was found; check with the Payette National Forest before publishing visit advice. Keeping Watch pages carry images with no direct image URLs, so no photo entries were added.

Current condition rests on a 2003 register visit and a 2016 Forest Service list. No newer visit report was found, so check the site before any public claim about its state today. The 1920s cupola has no exact year. The Jimmy Clarke death comes from a hobbyist site citing a book and is included with attribution only.

Build year conflict: HABS gives privy 1934, tower 1935, cabin 1936-37; NHLR gives 1935; Idaho Fire Lookouts and Keeping Watch give 1934. The story says so. Restoration vs acquisition: NHLR says a private party restored the top 20 feet in 2007; Keeping Watch says removed and acquired by a private party in 2008. Both are reported, not reconciled. Borlaug's Nobel year: NHLR says 1974. From memory, his Nobel Peace Prize was 1970. That is not supported by a fetched source here, so the story omits the year. A human should check the register's wording before it is reused. The HABS report is dated April 1996 (its cabin-extant finding predates NHLR's 2000 burn date; not a true conflict). Record 'ownership' is 'unknown'; NHLR names Richard Holm, Jr. as owner, which could be a correction, but it is a gap rather than an error, so not proposed. The record's coordinates and elevation (1556 m) are for the current Payette Lake site, not the original Cold Mountain site (about 8,084 ft per HABS). A separate record us-id-cold-mountain exists for the original site, which FFLA lists as Gone; the two may need linking. Access level 'private' comes from NHLR owner and Keeping Watch's 'home of a private party'. No photos added; NHLR photo in the record is all rights reserved.

The cupola date (1924 vs 1931) and tower height (50 vs 53 ft) conflict across sources. The brief's 1924 built event refers to the cupola and is corrected to 1955 for the standing tower. Restoration status is unverified since the 2020 reporting. Check on site before any public claim that restoration is under way.

NHLR's own description is internally a little inconsistent (mentions a 1936 gable-roof L-4 being moved in 1953 after earlier saying the log cabin replaced the frame cabin in 1931, without saying when the L-4 itself was built relative to the log cabin). idahofirelookouts.com's staff list is informal/crowd-sourced (note the comment thread correcting the Anderson staffing dates) but is the richest source for named observers.

Status is unresolved: the statewide index says Tower Standing, while two detailed pages say abandoned in the 1940s and do not confirm the pole remains. The abandonment is dated only to the decade, so no event was entered. No staffing history or fire found. Neither detailed page gives a visit date. The Idaho Panhandle roll-call PDF (ppolinks.com/forestservicemuseum/2022_1_11.pdf) lists Smith Creek district as Copeland in 1927; not cited, worth checking if the station's name history matters.

Current record's 1953 build year is confirmed as the current-structure date; the 1929 first-tower date is additional context not currently in the brief. No photos found beyond those already credited to the Fire Lookout Museum on existing source pages (not newly sourced here, so omitted from photos).

No recent condition report was found, so current state and access are unverified. The 1972 and 1981 fire-use dates conflict. Do not confuse with the town of Custer, Idaho. A 2026 Challis visitor guide mentions a 1981 National Register listing for Custer; it is unclear whether that refers to the town or the lookout, so I did not use it.

Built year: 1940 in the register, firelookout.com, the Forest Lookouts page and the Idaho list; the Idaho News 6 feature (undated in the cached copy) says 1941. Elevation differs across sources (register 6,706 ft, Idaho list 6694 ft, news feature about 6,800 ft); the record's 2044 m follows the register. Staffing as_of is 2024, the latest known-staff entry on the Idaho list (2021 Brig Malessa, 2022 Ezekiel Morphis, 2024 Stuart Morris); the 2021 evidence previously quoted the 2024 name and is corrected. The news feature is undated, so current staffing is unconfirmed. No source states an access level, so access is omitted. Record kind two_story and elevation are consistent with the sources.
Build-year conflict (1934 vs 1936) left unresolved per two-against-one source split. No structure height (as opposed to elevation) was found in sources, so height_m was omitted.

Idaho Fire Lookouts lists many more named seasonal staff (Odell, Black, Walters, Baker, Voll, etc.) between 1946 and 1972; only a sample is named in the story to keep it readable, with full list available in the source. Cabin footprint (15x15 vs 14x14) differs slightly between NHLR and Recreation.gov; both are given rather than resolved.

Disputed: the register dates a gable-roofed L-4 ground cab to 1926, while firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts date a cabin to 1926 and the L-4 cab to 1930; not resolved. Elevation is 7,461 ft in the register and firelookout.com but 7,641 on Idaho Fire Lookouts (may be a typo; not explained by any source). The record's location differs from Idaho Fire Lookouts by about 580 m; not checked here. Nothing read says whether visitors may enter the cab. The trip report is from 2013 and the road and trail details may be out of date. The 2021 staffing as_of comes from the June 9, 2021 Idaho Fire Lookouts article; the Keeping Watch page is undated. The Forest Service page in the tower's links (fs.fed.us, Nez Perce-Clearwater) did not resolve. A web search snippet mentioned a 2012 volunteer program start and a 2013 Forest Service description; neither was read, so neither is cited. Recommend checking current volunteer staffing and trail conditions with the Powell Ranger District before publishing.

Height: the record's height_m 3.0 has no source. 10 feet is the concrete base height (about 3.05 m), so the record may be using the base; omitted. Base material conflicts: concrete in the register, firelookout.com and the Idaho list (which says 10′ concrete base); cinder block in the Forest Lookouts page. Current condition is unknown beyond the roof loss reported by firelookout.com; no later visit report found. The access level 'restricted' is my reading of 'available for emergencies' and 'Hike-In Emergency Status'. Forest name: the register and Idaho list say Nez Perce National Forest, firelookout.com says Nez Perce/Wallowa Whitman. The 1968 vs 1968–1969 construction dates differ slightly between the register and the Idaho list. The Idaho list's known-staff entries run from 1932–1933 to 1978–1980 with gaps, so 1932–1933 is not the only staffing record.

Current condition unknown: the last visit report is 2010. Forest name conflict: the register says Salmon-Challis; firelookout.com, the Forest Lookouts page and the Idaho list say Salmon National Forest. The record's height_m 3.0 has no source in the pages read; omitted. Log base year conflicts (1944 register, 1943 Idaho list). The 1950s dates are decade-only, so the 1950 event year is a placeholder. The 1982 history says the road never reached the lookout while the 2010 visit report describes a road to it; both are recorded. No access level is stated, so access is omitted. The 1982 history's 'fell into disuse before many of the Depression-era lookouts' is kept as a paraphrase without a 'were built' reading, which the excerpt does not support and which conflicts with the 1935 build and 1950s last use.

Access level 'restricted' is my reading of conflicting evidence: an OHV route listing allows vehicles, and a 2024 visit found the gate open despite reports that it is locked. No official Forest Service access statement was found. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives the 1958 cab as '40 R-6', which looks like a typo for 20 ft; firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts give 20 ft. Forest Lookouts cites Kresek (1932 and 1958 dimensions) but that book was not read. The Trailforks page returned HTTP 403 and was not used. No new photos. The story no longer advises against climbing the tower: the sources say the bottom stairs were removed and the tower is unstaffed, and the story says no official rule was found.

Elevation conflict is unresolved: the register gives 5,548 ft (1,691 m), while firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 5,709 ft (about 1,740 m). The record keeps the register value. The 41-ft height is from the register and the 1959 survey note; the height to the cab floor is not stated. No source read says whether the public may visit, so access is left unknown. Staffing as_of is omitted because the sources give no date beyond the 1980s and the 2020 register text. No new photos. The distance from Canyon Ranger Station is cited to firelookout.com only; the register does not give it.

Unresolved conflicts left for a human: (1) steel tower year, 1948 in the register, firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts versus a 1949 annual report entry (quoted on Forest Lookouts), which the story reports as a disagreement; (2) tower origin, army or WWII surplus versus 'designed for the U.S. Air Forces' in the 1958 report; (3) cab, 7x7 metal cab in the register versus a 14x14 cabin midway up in the 1958 caption, which may describe the 1933 live-in cab; (4) status, 'active' in the register versus emergency status on two sites. Record design was null and is filled from the register. No source read says whether the public may visit; the association homepage does not mention public visits. No new photos.

Record height 2.1 m is wrong; sources give a 100-foot tower (proposed 30.5 m). Status is disputed: NHLR (undated page) says used as needed by the Elk City Ranger District, while the Forest Service page (updated June 4, 2025) says not currently used by the agency and not accessible to the public. The story reports both and does not resolve it; the NHLR wording may be older. An Idaho County Free Press feature on the lookout (idahocountyfreepress.com, 88-year-old lookout tower article) was returned by search but could not be read (HTTP 429); it may say more about current use and should be checked by a human. Elevation: see resolved_conflicts. Access is closed per the Forest Service; no climbing advice given.

Brief's elevation (2010.8 m / 6597 ft) matches both NHLR and Wikipedia exactly. Brief's access field was 'unknown'; proposed 'restricted' based on hike-in, staffed, wilderness-area status. Idahofirelookouts staff list had some garbled text (e.g. 'AbaStaffed') from page formatting; used only the clean names/years. Al Koenigs is recorded in 1925 and 1927 (not 'late 1920s'); Tommy Reed is recorded only in 1956, not 'much of the 1950s' -- story corrected to match the source's actual staff-year entries.

Record height 12.2 m matches the 1932 40-ft pole tower; the standing 1958 tower is 41 ft (proposed 12.5 m). Build year: 1932 per NHLR, Idaho and Forest Lookouts; a Priest River Experimental Forest storymap appeared in search with 1933 and a 1951 rename, but its page returned no text and it was not used. Current staffing rests on a Jan 2022 Idaho Fire Lookouts post and an undated firelookout.com line (staffed in summer); no current Forest Service source was read, and a 2020 IPNF post about access limited to staffed lookout towers appeared in search but was not readable. Access level left unset because no source states public visiting rules; the record's access 'unknown' stands. Elevation and forest-name conflicts are in resolved_conflicts. Staff names come from newspaper items quoted by the Forest Lookouts and Idaho sites; no new photos were recorded.

Four pages plus the firelookout.org list agree on the 1918-20 platform, the 1933 cabin and the 1988 move, but disagree on the 1988 destination and on elevation. Both are reported in the story. The brief's 'None relocated' event is wrong and is corrected. A firelookout.org listing also has a separate 'Gold Fork Valley' entry at 44.67137, -115.83580 marked Ground Gone; it is not clearly the 1918-20 site, so it is not used. Staffing is documented only by two 1935 and 1945 newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, and the originals were not read. Access is left unknown; only the 'Drive-Up' label is recorded. No notable fires were found. Height is not recorded.

Built date conflicts (1929 vs 1934); story uses 1934. Rental status unconfirmed: firelookout.com says planned; forest camping page lists one unnamed lookout. Access is unknown in the record and no visit info was found, so no access block. Search results also showed a different Granite Mountain Lookout on the Payette NF (NHLR, 1955 L-4 tower) and one on Mount Baker-Snoqualmie; neither is this record and neither was read.

Record height 3.7 m is wrong; the present tower is 20 ft (proposed 6.1 m). Name collision risk: two other Idaho lookouts are called Granite Mountain (Idaho Fire Lookouts southern-idaho page: 1923 camp, 2003 NHLR, North Fork Ranger District; north-idaho-panhandle-region page: 1932 cabin and 1934 L-4 tower, destroyed in the 1950s). Neither is this Payette tower and their facts were not merged. Current staffing is unverified for 2026: the staff list shows a 2026 entry and the 2025 visit confirmed a staffed season, but the FS guide (undated in the copy read) says unmanned. Staff names were deliberately left out of the research file; the staff list includes current seasonal staff. Access: the trail is public and non-motorized; no source describes rules for entering the tower. The NHLR page shows photos (1953 USFS, 2017 courtesy Keith Lanom) but no image URLs were retrieved, so no photos are recorded.

Build year conflict (1923 vs 1924) noted in the story. No documented staffing list beyond Maclean. Access level set to public/hike-in since it sits in designated wilderness with no restriction mentioned, but it's a serious approach, not a casual visit.

The brief listed status as plain 'standing'; sources indicate it's specifically on emergency-use status rather than seasonally staffed, so I added status_note and staffing accordingly. Idaho Fire Lookouts visit post includes several Fire Lookout Museum photos already credited there; not treated as new finds here since they're attributed to that site rather than a fresh source.

Built history is consistent across sources. Access and rental status are not established: the only access signal is the Idaho Fire Lookouts Drive-Up tag, so no access block was written. That page also shows a Staffed tag next to Drive-Up, but its text ties the staffing to a 2020 fire. The Nez Perce National Forest may now be Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest; the sources use the older name, so check before publishing. Forest Service list PDF fs.usda.gov/media/259202 (as of 2010) was read but not cited. It lists Green Mountain for emergency use, but the table text was too garbled to quote.

Conflicts not resolved: base height 8 ft (register, Idaho Fire Lookouts) vs 10 ft (firelookout.com); design R1/L-4 (register) vs L-4 (others); the 1963 two-story house with an R4-80 cab (Forest Lookouts only) is not reconciled with the 1935 L-4. The 1959 survey wording on Forest Lookouts (14 ft square, wooden, concrete base) fits either account. Current status is thin: Idaho Fire Lookouts says 'Drive-Up Emergency Status' with no date shown; the Idaho Climbing Guide says 'no longer in use' with no date shown. Whether the cab is open to visitors is not stated anywhere read. A web search snippet mentioned an onX listing saying the lookout is no longer manned and an Idaho Statesman item on the road loop; neither was read, so neither is cited. The record's height_m of 3.0 is near a 10-foot base but the register and Idaho Fire Lookouts say 8 feet; not changed. Recommend a Boise National Forest check on current status, road access and the 1963 house before publishing.

Full staffing history is thin in these sources (only one named staffer, Kris Anderson 1983, found clearly). The brief's flagged build-year conflict did not materialize across the three sources checked; could not reach the dead Nez Perce NF link listed in source_pages to check further. No evidence of a rental program; it reads as an actively staffed lookout.

Disputed: the L-4 date (1934 on firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts; 1940 on the register and Idaho Fire Lookouts), the base date (1959 base build vs 1960 completion), and the wilderness name (register: Frank Church neighbour; Keeping Watch: Selway-Bitterroot). Elevation: the register's 8,116 ft (2,474 m) matches the record; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 6727′, not used. Access level omitted: drive-up is supported, but no source states public or closed status, so a visitor check is advised. The 2025 staffing rests on one source. The Keeping Watch page says 'Built: 1930', which is the first platform, not the current cab. No source read describes the lookout as burned, moved or abandoned. Record height_m 3.0 is not confirmed; sources give a 10-foot base only. No new photos recorded.

The Forest Service page (fs.fed.us, Nez Perce-Clearwater) failed to resolve, so the agency fact rests on the register alone. Height and first-structure dates conflict across sources. The 1948 known staff entry predates the 1954 tower. The register and firelookout.com give an L-4 cab for the 1954 tower; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives a flat cab. No current public access rules were found. Keeping Watch (UIdaho) gives only a coordinate and a link, so it is not cited.

The record's design L-4 applies only to the 1932 cabin; the current cab is R-6 (correction proposed). The record's kind two_story with height_m 3.0 is left as is: sources describe a 10-foot base under a flat-top cab, so the kind label may need a look. Access level is not set: the only signals are the Hike-In tag and the McCall Life hike description, with no closure or permit information found. The McCall Life feature centers on one staff member's personal experience; the story uses only lookout facts and names no one. Known-staff names on Idaho Fire Lookouts are omitted on purpose.

History is consistent across four sources, and the 1961 date is backed by a Forest Service statement quoted in the climbing guide. Access is upgraded to public from the register's 'Open to public use'. The record's county 'Idaho' is left alone, since it follows the convention used for the other records. Current condition and staffing are not reported after 2012; the climbing guide and firelookout.com pages are undated. Forest: the register says Lolo/Clearwater National Forests and Idaho Fire Lookouts says Lolo / Clearwater National Forest, so they agree. No wilderness designation year is stated in any source, so the story gives only the 'three years' relation. No new photos recorded.

Staffing history is thin — only two documented years (1939, 1981) across both sources checked, with a large undocumented gap in between. firelookout.com (not cited, consistent with others) also lists it as built 1935, 30-foot timber tower, staffed every summer, confirming the other two sources without adding new facts.

Built year (1938) and L-4 design agree across three sites. The 1939 newspaper item calls the lookout newly constructed, which fits 1938 but reaches us only through the weebly page. Status (standing, abandoned) and access rest on a 2004 NHLR visit report and undated summary pages; no 2025 or 2026 visit was found, so re-check before publication. Staffing as_of is the read date because Discover Sawtooth is undated. No staffing history after 1960 was found beyond 'into the 1970s'. The brief's access value 'unknown' is replaced with restricted. No corrections to the brief's record.

Elevation conflict: the register gives 4,189 ft (1,277 m), which matches the record's elevation_m 1276.8, while Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 4248′ (about 1,295 m). Record left as is. height_m is not filled: the register gives a 41-foot wooden tower but not whether that is to the cab floor. Unreconciled: the 1932 newspaper (60-foot poles, under construction) against the about-1933 L-4 date. Staffing as_of 2021 comes from an Idaho Fire Lookouts page dated December 30, 2021; firelookout.com is undated. Access level omitted: 'Hike-In' is supported, but no source states public or closed status. The 1977 newspaper item calls the peak a granite peak, which does not fit a timber tower; the story does not repeat that. No new photos recorded.

Fact-check pass 2026-10-04: the original research omitted John Crawford's 1976-2008 staffing stint, which idahofirelookouts.com's known-staff list actually gives in full (1976-2008 Crawford, 2009-2010 Zimmerman, 2011-2013 Gilley, 2014-2015 Anderson, 2022-2024 Crawford again); the story previously implied Crawford's 2022 return was his only tenure. Corrected in both files. The 1929 log-cabin build year on NHLR versus the 1928 cabin/pole-tower date on idahofirelookouts.com may refer to the same construction episode.

Staffing status conflicts across sources; the 2015 end date rests on the NRHP nomination alone. The nomination PDF was read by grep excerpts, not in full. Access 'restricted' is a judgement from drive-up plus an active Forest Service detection site; no visitor policy was found. Do not confuse with the Washington Indian Mountain Lookout (nhlr.org/lookouts/us/wa/indian-mountain-lookout/), a separate tower with a 1953 replacement. Idaho Fire Lookouts' known-staff list is partial and was not used beyond 1942. No photos with a verified URL and licence were found. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the West Mountains line now describes the view from the lookout, not its location; the 2021 staffing post is dated in the story; the off-limits advice was replaced with a sourced statement.

idahofirelookouts.com has no documented staffing history for this lookout; the Weebly site supplied strong newspaper-sourced staffing detail instead. No current rental or regular staffing was found; status_note reflects firelookout.com's 'available for emergencies' description, which may be dated.

Dates (1928 patrol point, 1932 cab, 1948 last staffed, 1949 abandoned, 2020 NHLR) agree across sources. Thin points: the Forest Lookouts page is an unsigned compilation, and the 2019 condition report is one visitor's report. Access 'public' is a judgement: no closure or permission found, but the site is hike-in with no trail. No notable fires were found in the sources read. Do not confuse with a Facebook post for a 1932 L-4 cab 27 miles north of Weiser, Washington County, elevation 7589 ft, which is a different tower. firelookout.com credits photos to Shawn Ogden and Luke Channer, but no URL or licence was found, so no photos are listed. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the condition findings now have evidence quotes from the NHLR form fields; the distance and the advice not to climb are sourced or marked as our judgement.

The 1927 quote comes from the Forest Lookouts transcription of the Idaho Statesman, not the paper itself. Staffing as of 2020 is from the register, and Idaho Fire Lookouts names a 2025 staffer. The register and firelookout.com disagree on whether the current structure is one or two stories. The record height of 3.0 m is the 10-foot concrete base, not a tower height.

Only three pages were read. The Clearwater Story PDF (foresthistory.org) and the NFSL history PDF were grepped for Junction Mountain: the NFSL file had no match, and the Clearwater Story matches are for the Junction Mountain landform and a 1907 survey, not the lookout. Staffing is undocumented in every source found, so a staffing history would need the Kelly Creek ranger district or Clearwater NF records. The 1955 date is the register's Built field; the 1931 date comes from the register's description and firelookout.com. Current status rests on 2014 register photos and a 2025 summary with no later visit. height_m 16.2 converts the register's 53 ft. No access level is set because no source says whether the cabin is open or closed.

Four pages and one climbing guide were read. The register's Built 1935 and the 60-ft figure agree across three sources, and the 70-ft figure is a single quotation of a 1982 book, so treat it as disputed. The staffing record is built from newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts site, not from the newspapers themselves; the 1932 item predates the 1935 steel tower and is the earliest staffing shown here. Abandonment has no date in any source, so no event is recorded for it. Access is set to public from drive-up wording and the absence of any closure notice, not from a Forest Service statement. height_m 18.3 converts the register's 60 ft. The brief's record had no errors to correct. Idaho Fire Lookouts' Boise National Forest label appears to be an error. The Salmon-Challis Facebook post surfaced in search but its text was not read, so the naming of Jules Renaud is not used.

Watchman spelling (Gwilliams on firelookout.com, Williams on idahofirelookouts.com) is unresolved. The newest source is the 2020 Register entry, so current staffing and condition are unconfirmed. The brief's height_m of 3.0 is dropped from facts pending editor sign-off. No photos added.

Minor year conflict (1956 vs 1957) for the current cabin's construction, noted in the story and resolved_conflicts. Staff list on idahofirelookouts.com is extensive; only representative names used in the narrative to keep prose readable. Fact-check pass (2026-10-04): the 'nine miles north of Shoshone Camp' and '1 mile northwest' distance details were cited only to single sources in the draft though confirmed on additional sources (idahofirelookouts and recreation.gov both give the 9-mile figure; firelookout.com gives the 1-mile figure); the 1956/1957 build-year sentence was missing its NHLR (cite 1) footnote even though NHLR is the source of the 1956 date and dimensions. All three citation gaps fixed in the story.

Fact-check pass 2026-10-04: the original research under-cited idahofirelookouts.com's known-staff list, crediting Alexia Cochrane only as unspecified 'relief' staffing and omitting Chester "Chip" Beaty, Jeanne Kellar Beaty (1949-1950, and the 1953 book "The Lookout Wife" about Jeanne's time there), and Margie Cook (1974). The full list is now in events/evidence and the story names them. The 1920 Frank Hall newspaper accounts are strong evidence for an early lookout presence predating the first built structure by three years, worth flagging if the record's earliest date needs revision.

Staffing history is undocumented across all consulted sources; story omits a staffing section rather than guessing. Minor height discrepancy (55 ft vs 53 ft) noted but not resolved — no source explains it.

Current status is unclear. Idaho Fire Lookouts says a restoration was planned for 2026 and an L-4 cab is set for replacement in 2025/26, which conflicts with its own 2019 dismantling entry. The SAH Archipedia and Library of Congress pages returned 403 and were not used. SummitPost is out of date (says a 1977 tower is still used). The register's visit report dates to 2006. The record's L-4 design and 15.2 m height describe the 1939 pole tower, not the standing cupola.

The 1933 build year and the 1985-89 save-and-restore story agree across NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts. Elevation and forest name conflict across sources (see resolved_conflicts). Wikipedia's CCC claim is unconfirmed by the register or the other lists; check Wikipedia's refs before adding it. Do not confuse with other Lookout Mountain towers: Idaho Fire Lookouts' west-central 'Lookout Mountain Lookout' (1933 14x14 log cabin, moved 1975) and its northern-Idaho Lookout Mountain are different sites. The trail is a difficult hike and the summit is a lightning hazard; the cab itself is on emergency status. No notable fires were found in the sources read. NHLR photos (courtesy Luke Channer) have no licence shown, so none are listed. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the 1961 staffing event no longer implies this tower was staffed that year; the story no longer says the trail went 'up' the forest road.

Minor conflict on pole-tower height of the 1937 structure (45 vs 50 ft); both figures are now attributed to their sources in the narrative rather than stated as a single number. Elevation conflicts slightly between brief (1907.4m) and rec.gov (6,414 ft = 1955m) but not asserted as a specific figure in the story. Fact-check pass (2026-10-04): draft had stated the pole height as a flat '45-foot' figure sourced to both NHLR and firelookout.com, but NHLR actually gives 50 feet, contradicting its own citation -- fixed to attribute each figure correctly. Draft also said staffer Diane Young served 'around 1970'; idahofirelookouts.com's staff list actually dates her 1975-1978 -- fixed.
No source after the 2011 registration describes the current condition or any visit. No staffing history found. The 2000 abandonment date rests on one site. No photos added.

1956 vs 1957 last-staffed/abandonment discrepancy left unresolved in the story per guide instructions. NRHP nomination PDF (84001178) not pulled this pass; could firm up build details and exact staffing dates if more budget is available.

Current condition rests on a 2018 visit report and an undated climbing guide. The only current-condition source is the Idaho Fire Lookouts post dated September 29, 2023. No 2024-2026 status found. Brief elevation (2058.9 m) matches NHLR's 6,755 ft. Brief label 'abandoned 1969' is contested, so the story reports both labels. Access is public on the sources read; no closure notice was found. No fire history and no rental listing appeared in the pages read. Budget used: 6 page reads, 2 searches.

Design is described two ways: two-story concrete base with a frame cabin (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts) versus a concrete building with an observation room (Forest Lookouts Idaho). Both are noted in the story; not resolved. Access evidence is from a climbing guide dated as of July 2017; no current road status found. Staffing is undated. No notable fires found in the sources read, so no fire events are recorded. A BLM Owyhee Field Office closure notice dated 2026-09-19 appeared in search results (blm.gov/sites/default/files/docs/2026-09/20260919_OwyheeFieldOfficeClosure.pdf); it was not read and may not concern South Mountain, so check before adding any fire event. The record's height_m is absent because no source gives a total height.

The date the cab was moved is not given by the register, and a search did not find it. The register (2020) says the residence cabin stayed at the original site. The 2016 climbing guide describes a 1930s cabin still on the summit; it may mean the residence cabin, or the lookout cab before it moved. The sources do not settle this. Height: the register says 72 feet and the guide says 75 feet. The record's coordinates and elevation (1,529 m) are the museum's in McCall, not the original summit; the guide gives the summit at about 45.108 N, -115.775 W and 6,628 ft, which belongs to the record for the original site. A search result named a different McCall museum lookout (Sloan's Point); not verified and not used. The 2008 chapter report calls the damaged building 'the Split Creek Point cabin' and does not say whether it was the lookout cab or the residence cabin. The record status standing is kept, with a status_note added because the tower is gone. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story previously said the report did not name a cabin; it does, so the story now quotes that wording.

Main open question: Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 2010 as the year it was abandoned, yet the same page is tagged Actively Staffed, and the Keeping Watch interview and firelookout.com describe current summer or funded staffing. No dated source resolves it; the story reports both. The Keeping Watch item metadata gives Date Created 2021-09-25. The Forest Service Selway-Bitterroot lookout table (fs.usda.gov/media/259187) lists Spot Mtn. at 9 miles northwest of Magruder R.S. with a two-story log cabin (1922) and a 10 ft pole L-4 (1934), but its status column is ambiguous, so it was not cited. The Lynx Fire call-in is described on Keeping Watch but is not recorded as an event. The 2017 Eagle Creek evacuation is tied to the tower by the interview and a photo caption, so it is recorded as a 2017 fire event (corrected in fact-check 2026-10-08). Record height_m 3.0 matches the 10-foot concrete base, not the total tower height; no source gives total height, so height_m is omitted. Record elevation 2445.7 m matches the NHLR 2,446 m figure. Reader comments on the Idaho Fire Lookouts page were not used as sources. Trail length is not given anywhere in the sources.

Brief lists kind=tower/status=standing, but the historic 53-ft L-4 tower cab collapsed and was removed in 2014 (see correction). What's rentable today is the separate restored ground house. Design field left as L-4 since both the (removed) tower cab and the (standing) ground house were L-4 type; editor may want a status field update to reflect the tower/groundhouse distinction. Fact-check pass (2026-10-04): draft named 'Robert and Wayne McCormick's families' as 1951 staff, but neither firelookout.com nor idahofirelookouts.com lists a Robert McCormick -- only Wayne McCormick (1951) is documented -- fixed to remove the fabricated name. Also rewrote the 1950-tower sentence, which closely echoed NHLR's own wording ('53' CT-2 treated timber tower with standard 1936-model L-4 cab'), into the story's own phrasing.
Brief's status field 'standing' is consistent with sources (structure exists, under restoration, not destroyed); added status_note to flag it is not a routinely staffed or open lookout.

Early history conflicts across three sources (1933 vs 1940 first cab; 1938 replacement vs 1938 lightning loss). The 1981 present cab, BLM ownership and fire-season staffing agree. The 2.4 m height in the brief has no source; the 24-ft figure comes from a 1959 NGS station description on the Idaho Lookouts page and describes a structure older than the 1981 cab. The 2022 rename is reported only by a climbing guide and should be checked against a federal name record before publishing. Staffing after 2015 is not documented. Visitor access rules were not found.

Build-year chronology (1920s camp -> 1935 L-4 -> 1954 current cab) is consistent across sources. Fact-check (2026-10-04) found the original 'Hollenbeck in 1932 vs 1960' conflict was an error: the 1932 entry on idahofirelookouts.com belongs to a different person (Herb Uttley), and both Idaho Fire Lookouts and Firelookout.com actually date the Hollenbecks to 1960. The story and this file were corrected to drop the false conflict. No source gives current public-access status beyond 'used as a communications vault', so access is inferred as restricted rather than confirmed closed/open.

Brief height_m 3.0 is the 10-ft concrete base, not a height; removed. Brief design R-6 is supported. Summer staffing is undated. The 2001-2002 Mullikin entry is the only named staff. Forest name: register says Salmon-Challis, the other two say Salmon National Forest. Current condition and access are not confirmed by a recent source. No fire or rental record found. No photo URLs captured.

Brief height_m 3.0 has no source; removed. Brief status standing is changed to abandoned, the status all three sources give; no source describes its condition after the 2015 photo, so standing is not asserted. Build year conflict (1934 vs about 1945) is unresolved. The climbing guide quotes a 1982 Bing Young history; the primary text was not read. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists no staff. A rental or current-condition check would need a fresher source.

Lineage is consistent: NHLR says the 1959 cab was replaced in 1983, and the Airbnb listing and Small Home Tours say a 1959 lookout left Stranger Peak in 1983 (Idaho Fire Lookouts says 1982). The Washington record (us-wa-stranger-mountain) says the 1983 cab went to Colville in 2008; the two records should be checked against each other so the Stranger Mountain facts match. The Washington record's 1994 staffing refers to the mountain, not this cab, so it is not used here. Unverified: a June 2026 BoiseDev headline (seen only in search results; the page returned 403) says the owner has listed this property for sale. It is not in the story; check before publishing any status change. Elevation of 4,729 ft from Idaho Fire Lookouts is not a facts key, so it is left out. Idaho Crystal Peak (gone) is about 1.5 km from the Crystal Ridge coordinates. No new photos with usable URLs were found.
Consistent, well-documented staffing history and an active-use status make this one of the more straightforward entries. Only wrinkle is the 1932 vs 1933 build-year discrepancy, noted in the story.

Brief design L-4 is the 1935 cab; corrected to R-6 for the current cab. Brief height_m 6.1 kept; sources disagree (20 ft vs 15 ft). Brief agency Idaho Department of Lands is confirmed. Staffing is volunteer-based; the Idaho Fire Lookouts page is dated 2021. Access and rental status are not stated. Keeping Watch (University of Idaho) and an IDL page were seen in search results but not read. Brief elevation_m 1919.6 agrees with the register's 6,298 ft (1,920 m).

Staffing is disputed: firelookout.com and Daytrip Northwest say staffed every summer, Trails Off Road says unmanned, and none is dated. The brief's height_m 3.0 has no source among the pages read, so it is omitted. The 1994 SITPA history names a Sunset Mtn. lookout but gives no location; the story flags the uncertainty rather than linking it. No rental listing turned up; no Boise NF or recreation.gov page was read. The event dated 1940 is a SITPA-era event that may belong to another mountain.

No source gives a specific year staffing ended; firelookout.com's 'emergency status for several years' phrasing was used as-is. Sources conflict on tower height (20ft vs 30ft) -- flagged in resolved_conflicts and in the story rather than resolved. Removed an unsupported 'network'/'Upper St. Joe country' characterization and an unsupported 1930s-1960s service-span claim from the story; neither was backed by a source quote.

Build year of current cab disputed (1954 vs 1958). Date staffing ended not found in sources. Brief's kind 'ground' fits the 1922 cabin; the current cab sits on a concrete base and the Forest Lookouts page calls it two-story, so consider kind two_story. No fire at this lookout was found. No rental found. The 1958 'Swan Home' clipping on the Forest Lookouts page is a different place and was not used. The FS page says 'Last updated September 21, 2026' and carries a header notice 'UPDATED Sept. 19 - Crooked Fire Area, Road, and Trail Closure'; the notice does not name this site, so the reason for the site closure is not confirmed. The Forest Lookouts page is the only source with clippings for the 1920s to 1940s staffing.

The NHLR coordinates (N 43.306, W 111.921) fall outside Lemhi County and do not match the brief's lat/lon (44.885, -114.216). The Rex's page location (24 miles southwest of Salmon) fits the brief's coordinates, so the brief's coordinates were left alone; the NHLR coordinates look wrong. The elevation conflict (7,414 vs 9,960 ft) is not settled; check USGS before relying on either. Access and permission are not stated on any page read. Read budget used: the Trailforks trail page returned HTTP 403.

Current status is not confirmed. A search result titled 'Thorn Creek Butte Lookout Tower [CLOSED]' on AllTrails could not be opened (HTTP 403), so it is not relied on; verify before any visit. No Forest Service page for this lookout was found. Not on the FFLA rentals list as far as the grep showed. The 1974-1982 staffing dates are the only dated staffing. The brief's access 'unknown' is now 'restricted' on the basis of the sources' emergency-only language, which is a judgement call. A 2026 Crooked Fire closure near Idaho City appeared in search results but was not checked against this site.

Build dates conflict: 1962 (NHLR field, firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts) versus 1962 or 1965 (NHLR description) and 1965 (Forest Lookouts). Cupola date 1933 versus 1922. Elevation 8,656 ft (NHLR) versus 8652 ft (firelookout.com). Staffing is seasonal and undated. No notable fire was recorded in the pages read. The brief's events for 1962 and the 2020 registration are supported. One search snippet, not read, described a jeep trail to within about 5 miles of the summit; it is unverified and not used. Current 2026 access was not confirmed.

Staffing is dated: Idaho Fire Lookouts gives a page date of September 3, 2021 and a staff list running to approximate 2008 to 2023, so current staffing may differ. Access level is not stated on any page read; the story asks visitors to get permission first. The brief's height_m 3.0 is the 10-foot base only and is proposed for removal. The 1922 vs 1956 build-year conflict is recorded in resolved_conflicts.

The brief's height_m 1.8 has no source among the pages read, so it is omitted. Concrete base 1950 (NHLR, Idaho Fire Lookouts) versus 1956 (firelookout.com). Elevation 8,082 ft (NHLR) versus 8086 ft (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts). The association's name is spelled Protection on the NHLR and Protective elsewhere; the story uses Protective. Current staffing is unconfirmed: the association's undated employment page names only Brundage and Lookout mountains. No closure or rental notice was found. The brief's events for 1921, 1977 and 2020 are supported.

Three conflicts need an editor's call: the 1932 structure (L-4 vs R-1), the 1964 base (concrete vs cinder-block), and elevation (10,337 vs 10,394 ft). Current staffing is contested. Access is set to public on the Chamber's visitor listing; the cab's interior is not described, so confirm with Salmon-Challis NF before treating the cab as open. The brief's height_m of 3.0 is the base height, not total height. No rental found. The FS page names three staffed lookouts and does not name Twin Peaks, but it does not say which unstaffed lookouts remain.

Record's built year 1828 is a typo in NHLR's data field; 1928 is used. Sources disagree on end of use: Idaho Fire Lookouts says abandoned 1968, Forest Fire Lookout says not used since the 1970s. The cabin burning in 2012 rests on Forest Fire Lookout alone; the Idaho writer's 2012 photos show the cabin still standing. Access is unknown. The tower has broken ladder rungs and missing platforms; the story does not encourage climbing. Forest name differs between sources (Salmon vs Salmon-Challis). Idaho Fire Lookouts post dated January 16, 2023. Staffing history rests on that one site.
Brief's location conflict (NHLR vs RIDB coordinates, a few hundred meters apart) not addressed here since it concerns map data, not the narrative. No new photos found.

Elevation conflict: NHLR says 5,890 ft; three other sources say 5,981 ft. Correction proposed, editor to confirm. The 1968 date is the current structure; earlier lookouts from the 1920s, 1932 and 1934 are noted but the 1920s date is only a decade. Only two staff names are on record (1974, 1977). Rental status is disputed (Forest Service list vs two web sources). The Hike-In Emergency tag is read from the Idaho Fire Lookouts header. No height_m in the record; sources give a 10-ft tower. Post dated October 2, 2025.

Build year conflicts (1931 first tower vs NHLR 1961) and the staffing schedule differ across sources. A WebSearch snippet mentions a 2000 Burgdorf Junction Fire spotting role and fire-wrapping; not verified on a fetched page, so left out. Current record height_m 3.0 is the ten-foot block base, not total height. Access left restricted; no source documents public climbing or rental.

Fixes to the record: height_m 9.1 is the 1931 pole tower; the current 53-ft tower is about 16.2 m. Access moved from unknown to closed per the Forest Service page (updated 2025-02-19); the search snippet of a camping listing and a trail guide were not read and are left out. The 1931 pole-tower height appears as 30 ft in NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts. No documented staffing history exists. The earlier fs.fed.us URL in the queue record does not resolve; the fs.usda.gov page was used instead. The 16 vs 38 mile discrepancy from Pierce is unresolved and reported as such.

Tower standing, cabin gone, lower stairs removed, climbing not safe (Idaho Fire Lookouts). Abandonment has no exact year; sources say the 1950s. Only two named lookouts: L.L. Hydron (1935, secondhand via Idaho Fire Lookouts' citation of the Bonners Ferry Herald) and Burt Callahan (1936). Forest name differs between NHLR/FS (Idaho Panhandle) and Idaho Fire Lookouts (Kaniksu). Record access 'unknown' is now public trail access; the tower is not to be climbed. Build year: 1934 vs 1934 or 1935.

No source read supports an access level (public, restricted or otherwise), so the access key is omitted. Staffing is seasonal per firelookout.com, undated. Build year 1933 (three sources) vs 1934 (one). Register date 2011 (NHLR) vs 2020 (Idaho Fire Lookouts). Known-staff names come from one site only. Record access 'unknown' should stay unless the Boise National Forest answers. No rental found. Record fields otherwise match the sources.

Access 'public' rests on one map site (TopoZone) plus the 2016 visit report; treat it as provisional and check with the Challis National Forest. Build year 1935 (four sources) vs 1936 (Idaho). Elevation 9,556 vs 9,546 ft. Staffing end 1943 (TopoZone) vs 1946 abandonment. Record coordinates match NHLR and TopoZone; the record's conflict note about Idaho Fire Lookouts coordinates (about 0.5 km off) is not visible in the pages read. Cabin is a ground cab, not a tower. No rental found.

Access 'restricted' is inferred from the Forest Service's active-lookout and respect-the-space wording; no source says the cab is closed to visitors, so the story says so. Elevation: the record's elevation_m 2085.4 follows NHLR (6,842 ft); the Forest Service gives 6,826 ft (about 2080.6 m). Editor to decide whether to change it; not proposed as a correction. The 2006 crash is relayed secondhand through Idaho Fire Lookouts from a Forest Service Facebook post, which was not fetched directly. Staffing 2026 is from the trailhead page's last update (May 2026). No rental found.

Build year 1941 agrees across three sources. Access (key from the caretaker) rests on a single 2024 blog post; no official access rules were found, and the Illinois DNR page I tried returned an unrelated park, so it is not cited. Surviving-tower counts differ: NHLR says two state towers remain, the 2024 blog says three in Illinois. The blog's count of about 30 Illinois towers differs from NHLR's 10 state plus 7 federal; not used. No staffing or fire records found. Fact-check 2026-10-08: a reader comment on the 2024 blog (dated June 7, 2026) lists a park phone number; it is unverified and not used. The story no longer says the sources give no phone number. The blog's two missing windows are a visit-time observation; the caretaker's replacements are a separate general remark.

Thin record. The NHLR entry gives registration and refuge background but no tower history; the Forest Lookouts page has only a heading; no build date, height, builder or photos were found in two searches and seven page reads. Standing status comes from the FFLOS Illinois list. The brief records Forest Lookouts coordinates (40.363, -89.9911) that differ from NHLR and FFLOS (about 40.3646, -89.9999); the Forest Lookouts page I read showed no coordinates, so that difference is unverified and was not used. Access is unknown.

Access depends on the Forest Service page as read on 2026-10-08, which still showed the site temporarily closed for repairs that were to start May 11, 2026. No reopening notice was found, so check the access line before publishing. The 40 ft vs 60 ft height of the 1934 wooden tower is unresolved; the story shows both. The c.1942 description (40 ft) conflicts with the 100 ft steel tower of 1938; the story says so. The cab status rests on the FFLA list's Standing* note alone; no photo of the cab was read. The 2020 closure year is inferred from the report's 4 January 2021 date line. The NHLR page does not mention climbing; the platform visit rests on the Forest Service release saying the platform offers visitors views. No staffing dates, notable fires or rental listings were found in the sources read. No new photos were added; the existing NHLR photo stays in the record.

The NRHP nomination (Schroeder, 2002) was not readable; the catalog.archives.gov PDF returned no extractable text, so NRHP details come from Wikipedia. Build year (1934 vs 1936-1938) and height (80 vs 100 ft) conflict across sources. The closed status comes from Clio's reading of a park map and should be checked with the park office. The 2017 visit report is the most recent condition evidence found.

The build year and builder are unknown. The register says before 1940, and the 1939 magazine point is an inference from the Indiana Fire Towers site, so the story says 'implying'. Ownership is disputed: the register says state-leased land, while Indiana Fire Towers is unsure it was ever state property; the story shows both. The June 2024 visit sentence now carries footnote 2, and the 'outside the property' wording was replaced with what the author actually wrote (not on public property, could not get right up to it). Unread lead: a 2022 FFLA Indiana chapter report by Teena Ligman, linked from the Indiana Fire Towers page, which the site says has a story and pictures of this tower. The access line is private: the register says visiting without permission is illegal, so do not invite visits. No photos added; the NHLR photos stay in the record.

Built 1935 by CCC is supported by two sources (NHLR and a hobby site repeating the Living New Deal date). The brief's record had no built event; this adds it. The 2009 restoration money is spelled AARA in the sources and ARRA in the brief record; the story uses the sources' spelling. Current climbing permission is unconfirmed: the only climbing statement is a hobby site, and the DNR map gives no tower rule. Height and staffing dates are not in any source read. Agency is recorded as Indiana Department of Conservation per the Forest Lookouts header; that is an older name and the DNR map is the current state publisher, so check the agency field before publishing.

Build date disputed (1935 completion vs a 1935 to 1952 window). Access 'closed' rests on a June 2022 map legend read by Indiana Fire Towers; no current access source found. A Forest Lookouts page also quotes a December 31, 1938 Vincennes Sun Commercial item about a tower 'being re-erected near Stendal' in Pike County State Forest; the item does not name Hartwell, so it is not used. Living New Deal returned HTTP 403 and was not used. Grokipedia was not used.

The DNR closure notice is undated in the cache, so the closed status is as of the last read and should be rechecked before publication. The May 2025 fire comes from Facebook posts cited by a personal enthusiast site; the story attributes it to that site. The brief's height_m of 12.2 m is not supported by any source read. Indiana Fire Towers also describes a personal climb in 2021; that is not used and is not encouraged. The 1989 accident report is not in the story because it does not name this tower. The old NHLR Lookout.aspx page returned HTTP 500 and was not used. One websearch.py search was run. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the 1927 two-tower statement is now shown with the geodetic-survey context from the same page; the observer detail keeps the fall-and-spring qualifier; the still-standing and not-climbable status is footnoted.

Current public access/climbability status is unclear from sources consulted; the brief's record also listed access as 'unknown' which matches. Wikipedia's claims are cited to a single footnote source [1] on that page which was not independently retrieved here; treated as generally reliable given specificity but flagged for anyone who wants to verify the underlying reference.

Location and access disputed: The Outbound says the tower was moved to Brown County State Park and can be climbed; Indiana Fire Towers and the register say it stands on IU land with no public access. The story does not encourage climbing. Build year (1930 register vs 1931 contemporary sources) and height (75 vs 80 ft) also disputed. Nothing found on staffing or notable fires.

Only two readable sources. The build year is disputed: NHLR says 1935, while Mark A's wall photo note (circa 1937) and the 1936 map point later. A Living New Deal search snippet gives 1934, but that page returned HTTP 403 and is not cited. An AP/Herald-Times search snippet describes the tower reopening after a decades-long closure, but that page returned HTTP 403 and no closure or reopening is cited here, so an editor should check it by hand. The brief's access 'unknown' can be updated to public (NHLR, as of 2025). No staffing history was found in the readable sources.

The brief's agency 'State Forest' is not an agency, and none of the readable sources names the agency that administers this tower, so the agency fact is left out. The access level 'restricted' rests on Mark A's note that the gate is usually locked; the Visit Bloomington post says the tower is available again. The 2026 'restored' event is dated only by the April 2026 post, so its year may not match the renovation. No Living New Deal or Facebook sources were checked for this tower.

Record height 30.5 m (100 ft) corrected to 26.2 m (86 ft) per NHLR and Indiana Landmarks. Living New Deal (about 100 ft, completed 1934) and Wikipedia (90 ft) appeared only in search results and were not read; not used. Clio is a student-created entry (2020) that cites WBIW Aug 2020, not read; its reopening date and closure length are reported as Clio's claims. Access marked public from Clio and Indiana Landmarks; no current park page on hours or climbing was read. NHLR visit form leaves the staffing question unanswered. Current elevation_m 234.7 matches NHLR 770 ft (235 m). No new photos added.

The 1938 build year rests only on a personal resource quoted by Indiana Fire Towers, so the event is kept with that caveat. The 1938 date falls before the 1941 depot founding, a gap no source read explains. USFS says the tower was used until the mid 1970s but gives no exact year, so no dated event was added for that. No staffing or notable fire was found in the sources read. Status and access come from Indiana Fire Towers' February 2025 visit; nothing newer was checked. The Register's Lawrence County entry disagrees with Indiana Fire Towers and the Forest Fire Lookout Association list (Martin); the brief's county was not changed. Not verified: any restoration, closure or change since February 2025.

The Structure 44 link between the southern tower and the Forest Service's Fire Tower Three is an inference from two sources that name Structure 44 and JT21; the story says the pages appear to describe one tower. The 1942 build year comes from a personal resource; the 1946 entry is from survey-mark descriptions. Standing status rests on the Forest Fire Lookout Association list alone, and no 2025 visit note names this tower as standing. No staffing, fire or visit history was found in the sources read. Not verified: the current state of the repeater antenna or any change since February 2025.

The name is spelled Waggoner by FFLA and Indiana Fire Towers, and Waggoneer by the NHLR; the story uses Waggoner where it quotes or names the cemetery. No build year is found for this tower. The 1939 tower near the lake is linked to this site only by inference, and the story says so. The Forest Service numbered list does not map cleanly to this tower. The 2025 condition is consistent between the NHLR photo caption and the Indiana Fire Towers text. Not verified: any further demolition after February 2025. The story also reports the 2004 satellite image on the same Indiana Fire Towers page, which appears to show the whole tower, beside the 2025 photo that shows the cab missing.

Build date and origin of the water-tank tower are unknown; the sources conflict on whether it began as a Forest Service or a Navy tower. Cab removal rests on the FFLA Standing* footnote, not on a site photo we checked. Access and climbing status come from one Indiana Fire Towers visit report (February 2025). The brief's 'NSA Crane' name is the Register's title; the Register's location line reads Naval Weapons Station Crane.

Construction sequence before 1941 is disputed between the NHLR (CCC 1937, fire, 1941 rebuild) and the sign and hobbyist survey (1932 erected). Staffing, fire year and official access status were not found in the pages read. Climbability rests on one hobbyist site and needs confirmation with the state park. Living New Deal page returned 403; Wikipedia O'Bannon Woods page had no tower text in the fetched output. Agency left out because the NHLR administered-by value did not appear in the fetched text.

The 1935 vs 1939 build date is unresolved. A Living New Deal search snippet and a Facebook snippet (CCC Camp S-93, 1935-1936) were seen only as search results, not read, so they are not cited. The brief's access 'unknown' can be updated to public (reopened 2019). OpenStreetMap tags height=30.5 and access=yes, but the OSM text splits the tag values across lines, so OSM is not quoted; height_m 30.5 is supported by the 100-foot figure in Indiana Landmarks. Current climbing status rests on Mark A's undated notes. The brief's 'Well's County' spelling is an OSM variant.

Height disagrees: 80 ft in the register and in the 1954 notice, about 85 ft in the 1947 datasheet for the Borden tower (before the move). Not reconciled; the story says so. The 1954 newspaper notice is read only through the register's quotation, not the Jackson County Banner original. No staffing dates, fire incidents or rental listings were found in the sources read. The 1937 Borden mention comes from the Borden page's account of a Division of Conservation annual report; the Clark County location is the Borden page's, not the 1937 report's, and the story now says so. The access line is private and not accessible; do not suggest visits.

Record height 27.4 m (90 ft) is corrected to 24.4 m (80 ft) per the register and 1932 steel-tower reports, but the 1946 NGS description says about 108 ft, so the height is not settled. The builder is disputed: the register says CCC 1931-35, the hobbyist survey quotes a wooden tower first and a later CCC steel tower. The 1932 site is also described two ways: about 1.5 miles south of Brownstown (Sept 1932 article) and about 2.5 miles (NGS). The 2010 restoration line on the eastern lookouts page has no source of its own. The climbable claim rests only on a hobbyist site; the story does not encourage climbing. Staffing in 1932 was an announced plan, not a confirmed record. No notable fire tied to the tower was found in these sources. The 1970 staffed_last year is a placeholder for 'the 1970s'. Record access was 'unknown' and is now public, supported by the register and the DNR page. Search budget: one websearch.py call.

Re-erection year is not in any source read, so no rebuild event is listed. No source names staff or fires for the tower. The record's source page '../us-in-spears-john-spears/' was not in the cache and was not read. Mark A's original-site coordinates (38.38, -86.55) differ from the record's Velpen coordinates, as expected for a relocated tower. Ownership sequence and county are the two conflicts; both are flagged. Visit access is by invitation only, so the story does not encourage a visit. No photos added.

Build year is 1927 by the 1928 report (quoted by NHLR) and a July 1927 photo; the sign says the 1930s. The plan report that announced the tower is dated 1926 by the Register and hobby site but 1923 by the Forest Lookouts transcription; the story reports both. Height is 80 ft as built per the 1928 report, but the Register and a 1941 item say 90 ft or more; the record's 24.4 m is kept but may be revisited. Climbing: the hobby site says the cab is not open and the tower can be climbed partway; no official rule found, so the story does not encourage climbing. The 1944 staffing and radio items come from a Brown County Democrat clipping transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page; the clipping itself was not read. Restoration status: fundraising announced January 2026; no evidence of work started. Agency: Indiana DNR per NHLR; the Forest Lookouts header uses the older Department of Conservation name. Fire history: no specific fires found.

Build year is disputed: 1931 delivery (newspaper), 1932 (register), 1933 completion (county survey quoted on a hobbyist site). The record has no build year, so none is written to facts. The Living New Deal page refused access (HTTP 403), so it is not cited. The hobbyist climbability claim is not confirmed by the state; the story does not encourage climbing. The DNR page says Martin State Forest was established in 1932 while the hobbyist site says acquired 1933; that concerns the forest, not the tower, and is not reconciled. Current condition beyond the hobbyist note is unknown. Search budget: two websearch.py calls. The 'standing' and 'climbable' notes come from one hobbyist page and are not state confirmation.

NHLR is a solid primary source with direct site-visit detail (trail distance, ranger anecdote, climbable status). The weebly compendium corroborates WPA construction and park location but differs on the year by three years; could not resolve which is more authoritative within budget. No source addresses overnight rental, so the story states the absence of any such record rather than asserting it is unavailable.

Only two sources. The Forest Lookouts entry is a bare listing with no dates or details. Build year, design and height are not found after two web searches. Ownership conflict is unresolved; the Kentucky Division of Forestry or the owner would settle it. Abandoned Online lists the tower with no details and was not used. The Wikipedia entry for the community has no tower information.

Build and move history is consistent across three sources once the NHLR Built field is read as the move year. Builder credit is unresolved between the register and the arboretum; the story presents both. Purchase year (1928 vs 1929) is left open. Two sources only. The build date is just 'the 1930s' per NHLR; no exact year was found. No build date or builder found in any source read. Low confidence. One substantive source: the Register entry with its August 2014 visit report. The Forest Lookouts page for Chunklick has only a county header. Low confidence; thin record. The Register entry is the only substantive source; the Forest Lookouts page has a heading and county only. Thin record. Unresolved: (a) county, Lyon per the NHLR versus Trigg per the Forest Lookouts header; (b) build year, 1930 per the NHLR Built field versus 'in the 1930s' in the NHLR description. Builder, cab material and abandonment date are disputed; the 35-foot figure looks like an error. Status is unconfirmed: the NHLR 2026 entry gives no condition, and no source after 1944 was found. Two solid sources (NHLR register page with a 2016 visit report; Forest Lookouts page quoting a December 13, 1937 Lexington Herald-Leader item) plus a 2020 hiking guide for access. Open gap: when the Forest Service stopped staffing it. Not fetched, so not cited: a Living New Deal search snippet says decommissioned 1976 (that page returned HTTP 403 to fetch_text), and a park Facebook snippet says active 1937-1970 (the page returned only its title). Build date unresolved (1929 vs late 1930s); height_m is null; the 1929 planned 100 ft (30.5 m) is recorded in height_note, not as a measured height. Only two sources. The register gives no build date, height, design, staffing or access, and the Columbia caption (July 2025) is the only evidence it still stands. Demolition rests on the NHLR and FFLOS registers, which are the same organization's two sites, and is dated only 'as of 2024'. The 2016 newspaper is the only independent source. The 1934 build is supported by three sources. No lookout names, staffing dates or notable fires were found. The 'abandoned' step has no year, so it is left out of events. Elevation not in facts. The brief gives 384.4 m, but LEX18 says the highest point in Bath County is 1,388 feet (about 423 m); the two should be checked against a survey before either is used. Thin evidence and no build date. The Wikipedia row for Abita reads Still standing; adjacent rows in the same table read Torn down, which is why the first grep was misleading. The record's agency 7N is a survey location, not an agency. One web search found nothing on Morgan Road or the tower's use. The story is short by design; do not pad it.

Single source: the Wikipedia Louisiana list, which gives the status 'Still standing/Inactive', the note 'Damaged', and the coordinates that match the record (30.665, -92.995). Very thin sourcing. No entry for Fields Fire Tower in the cached NHLR or FFLOS (firetower.org) Louisiana registers, and no mention in the cached centraluslookouts.com Louisiana page beyond a bare county-header photo callout with no text. Wikipedia's own citation for 'still standing' points to a USGS GNIS feature-detail page (geonames.usgs.gov, Apex app); it is JavaScript-rendered and returned only the generic USGS/Board on Geographic Names homepage when fetched, so it could not be used directly. Builder, construction date, design, height, and managing agency are all unknown and should not be guessed. A human with access to LDAF's Louisiana Statewide Forest Resource Assessment and Strategy PDF (cited elsewhere in the same Wikipedia list, pp. 36-37) might find more.

No build year, first-staffing date, or move/alteration history was found in the sources reached, so the story says so. The record's elevation (27.1 m) is consistent with the register's 89 ft. The 33.5 m height is converted from the register's 110 ft. Access is unknown: no source reached says whether the public may visit, so no access or visit fact is written. Do not confuse with a Gordon tower in Wisconsin (a 1935 Aermotor listing seen in a search result, T.44N-R.12W); that is a different structure and was excluded. An OpenStreetMap node (358380019) tags it as an observation tower of lattice construction at ~26 m, but that was not cited. Search budget: three websearch.py calls, one over the two-per-tower budget.

Thin on the tower itself: the register page is the only source about the tower; the 2010 NRHP nomination and the NPS page cover the recreation area and say the CCC built the tower only 'likely'. Unresolved conflict: the register says a 99 ft 9 in Aermotor LX-25 built in 1933 (with a 1934 USFS photo and a 1952 stair change); the central Louisiana lookouts site says an 82-ft steel tower with a 7x7 cab was erected in 1951-52. Only Wikipedia's Louisiana list gives this tower any detail, and it gives nothing on construction, height, ownership, staffing or use. Two independent sources (the NHLR register and a lookout-hobbyist history site) agree and complement each other, but neither confirms what happened after the 2006 disassembly: whether restoration was completed, where the tower now physically stands, or whether it's accessible. Worth a human follow-up with the Catahoula Ranger District or a recent visit report before treating location/access as current.

Only the 2017 NHLR entry and two quoted newspaper items cover this tower. The 1920s build date is 'believed' per NHLR, so no built event is recorded. Thin evidence. Wikipedia's list is the only source with substance on this tower, and it gives no construction date, height, owner, staffing or use. Disputed: first tower 1917 (registry, 1917 state report) vs 1918 (FFLA); height 48 ft (registry, FFLA) vs 50 ft (1917 state report); current tower 60 ft (registry, Forest Lookouts) vs 68 ft structure height (FFLA). Disputed: current tower 75 ft (registry) vs 68 ft structure height (FFLA); the 1914 structure's 60 ft height comes only from the registry. Brief height_m 58.5 corrected to 68 ft (20.7 m). Origin conflicts between the Register and New England Defenses (the latter cites a 1989 newsletter); not resolved. Several dates and sizes conflict. First tower: 38 ft (FFLA) vs 30 ft (registry), first used 1912 (FFLA). The 40-foot tower: built 1917 (registry) vs a 40-foot Acushnet tower moved in 1938 (FFLA). Current tower: 1969 (registry and the record) vs 1970 (FFLA); 70 ft (registry) vs 68 ft (FFLA). Elevation 347 ft (registry) vs 353 ft (FFLA); the record's 105.8 m is close to the registry's 106 m. The 1928 build date rests on the register page alone; no second source found. Searches surfaced a 1928 Goat Peak lookout in Washington State, a different site, so do not conflate them. Sources describe recreation and hawk watching only; none says the tower was built for fire watch, so the brief's kind 'unknown' is left as is. Current access comes from the DCR hike guide and an advocacy site. A check with the DCR Mount Tom office or MACRIS would settle the 1928 date.

Height and cab design are unconfirmed. A search snippet from the FFLA Massachusetts chapter gives 68 ft, but the Facebook post could not be read, so it is not used. The register names the older Bureau of Forest Fire Control as administrator; the 2023 Gazette names DCR, so agency is set to DCR and the record's agency field may need updating. Staffing: the register's 'Staffed seasonally' note is undated; the 2023 staffing item is a plan. The closure comment is undated (photo April 2016), so current access should be confirmed. Climbing rests on one 2020 trip report. No fire credited to this tower was found. The Eastern US Lookouts Moores Hill page yielded only navigation text.

The 2004 register is the only official source. Trailspotting (Aug 2026) describes the steel tower as still staffed during fire season and says visitors were invited up by the operator; this is one secondhand account, so confidence stays low and public access is not established. Groton Trails describes the stone ruin only. Ffla.org and firelookout.org state-tower pages returned 404, so the state tower number and operation date in search snippets are unverified and not used. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story's 'no later source' sentence was contradicted by the Trailspotting page and was rewritten; the 1940 Lowell Sun item was missing from events and has been added.

Height conflict unresolved: the register says the first tower was 48 ft, and the State Forester report (via Forest Lookouts) says 50 ft. The present tower is 70 ft per the register. A search snippet from a fire-lookout site that returned 404 gave 68 ft, a 1913 first date and a 1936 radio date; none is verifiable here, so none is used. The Pelham record should read: move 1920, report published January 1921, height disputed. The Pelham register page does not mention Hanson. No current access, staffing or visit data found; access left unknown. Height 70 ft converted to 21.3 m.

Only the register is specific to this tower in the cache; the other two sources are statewide. Staffing and public access are not established, so no access key is set and the story says so. Lookout-site pages found by search (ffla.org and firelookout.org) returned 404 from the cache and were not quoted or used. Their search summaries say the tower is on Pinnacle Hill, gives 68 ft rather than the register's 70 ft, gives October 1, 1921 as first operation, and calls it an active state tower; none of that is in the story. Built and replacement dates are well sourced, but the register dates the present tower to 1956 while the FFLA post's height (68 ft) differs from the register (75 ft). No source read gives current condition or staffing after 1945; the 2004 register entry is the latest tower-specific record. The 2017 FFLA post was readable and is cited for the 1916 height, the abandonment, and the 68 ft figure. The Town sketch gives the logbook watch's purpose as watching Kingston Bay for suspicious activity and does not call it a fire watch, so whether the WWII watch relates to the fire tower is undocumented. Camp Nekon is town conservation land; whether the tower is open for climbing is undocumented.

NHLR is the main source; the Forest Lookouts history is built from newspaper clippings. The 2026 trail guide is the only current source. The brief's height of 24.4 m conflicts with the register's 68 ft (corrected). Elevation differs slightly between NHLR (2,126 ft) and FFLOS (2,123 ft); not used. Search snippets about a 2003 rebuild plan and a steel frame were not fetched and are not used. Fact-check 2026-10-08: every story claim was checked against the cited pages and matches. One evidence entry was missing (the Nov 1969 '100 feet' claim) and has been added. Several sentences that repeated source wording were reworded. The pending corrections (status) are left for human review as STORY_GUIDE.md requires.

OpenStreetMap-only record. The tower carries tower:type=observation and no emergency=fire_lookout tag, so it may not be a fire lookout at all; the kind 'tower' is still safe. Mapcarta labels it Essex while the nearby reservation is in Ipswich, so the town needs checking before any change (it may sit near the Essex/Ipswich line). Neither the cached NHLR nor the cached FFLOS Massachusetts index lists an Essex or Ipswich entry. The archived copy of the OSM source PDF (web.archive.org, 2014) did not load, so the current Mass.gov copy was read; the refuge observation tower it mentions is not tied to these coordinates. Status, build date and builder are unknown.

Three sources, all read. The NHLR page is the substantive one: 2002 registration, cab history, and an April 2016 visit report. Current access and staffing rest on that 2016 report; no newer source was readable. AllTrails (HTTP 403) and the Roamful and MyHikes listings appeared in search but were not readable, so none is cited. Two Forest Fire Lookout Association Massachusetts Facebook posts (fall 1936 build, April 1937 opening, 1950 radio) returned login walls and are not used; they are worth checking if a later pass can read them. The brief's 2015 'restored' event is proposed as 'modified' in corrections. Not verified: whether the tower has changed status since April 2016, and whether the public may climb it. No photos added.

Thin record. Staffing and current access are unsourced: the Wicked Local 2005 article returned HTTP 403 and FFLA Facebook posts returned login walls, so none was read. Search snippets (not verified) describe the MacAllester tower as an active DCR asset and a 1951 steel tower moved to Snow Hill from Foxboro; that conflicts with the Register's 1953 date and needs a readable source before use. The Register's 'standing' status is not confirmed after 1993. Next step: find a readable source on staffing and the 1951 vs 1953 construction date. The 1939 Register entry is about fire detection use, not staffing, so it is recorded as 'other'.

The register's 1968 date, $400 gift and 193 ft elevation are used as given. Used 2 WebSearch calls and 3 readable page reads plus failed attempts.

The build year conflicts within the register and with the local Town Forest history; see corrections. A lookout-history page found by search (firelookout.org, 404 from the cache, not quoted) reportedly places the tower on Chestnut Hill and gives April 1, 1916 as the first operation date and a 2003 cab; none of that is in the story.
